Mo3-A Photonic-driven architectures for access networks and AI clusters
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: Mo3-A1 The role of programmable photonics in ai data centers
Mo3-A2: Demonstration of Ultra-high Link Budget, Low Cost/Latency Distributed AI Scale-across Network enabled by C-band 3.2-Tb/s/lane IM-DD Transmission over 20-km AR-HCF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Jingchuan / Li, Yibin / Li, Peng / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Zhong, Kangping / Yu, Changyuan / Lau, Alan Pak Tao / Lu, Chao

We demonstrate a C-band 32λ × 50-GBaud PAM4 transmission over 20-km HCF. We achieve a record link budget over 50-dB, showing that HCF-enabled IM-DD technology is strong candidate for AI scale-across scenarios requiring low-latency, low-cost, and zero packet loss.

talks.title: Mo3-A3: Is DSP-free Pluggable Optical Module More Suitable for Optical Circuit Switching?
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Chenxiao / Wang, Han / Wang, Ceng / Soma, Daiki / Wakayama, Yuta / Inohara, Ryo / Tsuritani, Takehiro

This paper presents the first comprehensive analysis of an LPO + OCS GPU network, from the optical to the application layer, including the impact of OCS reconfiguration. Stable 72-hour LLM pre-training was successfully demonstrated on this architecture.

talks.title: Mo3-A4: Dynamic RU-DU Reconfiguration in 6G Access Networks Using Fast Controlled Photonic Switches with 400G ZR+ Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bahari, Assad / Mefleh, Ali / Calabretta, Nicola

We demonstrate a novel 6G access network for dynamic RU-DU reconfiguration combining fast-controlled SOA-based photonics with 400G ZR+ optics. Cross-layer coordination achieves 206 μs end-to-end reconfiguration latency, with scalable performance across multiple nodes and < 3.8 dB penalty at pre-FEC 10-2 BER.

talks.title: Mo3-A5: Large-Scale Deployment of LPO in AI Clusters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Qin / Wang, Chunxiao / Lu, Rui / Yao, Zhiping / Zhu, Fangbo / Wang, Peng / Wang, Zhicheng / Chen, Liang / Wang, Anbin / Bao, Yun / Huang, Yiyuan

We present the large-scale deployment of 400G DR4 LPO modules in AI clusters, reporting statistical data on system conditions, link performance, and reliability from over 25.8 million device-hours of field operation, proving the long-term reliability of LPO technology

sessions.title: Mo3-B Hollow-core fibre fabrication and deployment
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: Mo3-B1: Breaking the Loss Barrier: Hollow-Core Fibers from Physical Limits to Mass Production
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Yingying / Gao, Shoufei / Xiong, Yifan / Sun, Yizhi / Ding, Wei

This tutorial reviews anti-resonant hollow-core fibers, from structure evolutions and loss reduction to manufacturable long-draw production, and discuss application-oriented trade-offs from intra-data-center links to long-haul networks.

talks.title: Mo3-B2: Rate of Water Ingress into Hollow-Core Fibre by Capillary Action
talks.abstract:
Authors: Agah, Samuel / Saw, Chiang Ping / Horak, Peter / Wheeler, Natalie

We investigate water ingress into a double-nested antiresonant nodeless fibre by capillary action, using two independent methods. We find that different parts of the fibre fill at different rates and that ingress is 2-4 times slower than into a cylindrical capillary of identical core diameter.

talks.title: Mo3-B3: Dynamic Response of Antiresonant Hollow-Core Fibre Drawing to Pressure Perturbations
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shakiba, Ali / Abokhamis Mousavi, Seyed Mohammad / Budd, Leonard / Sandoghchi, Seyed Reza / Baddela, Naveen Krishna / Poletti, Francesco / Jasion, Gregory T.

A transient thermo-viscous model for drawing antiresonant hollow-core fibre is presented and experimentally validated. Core and capillary pressure perturbations drive distinct geometric responses, with inter-capillary gap showing the largest sensitivity. Low-frequency disturbances induce the strongest modulation, providing guidance for stable pressure control during fabrication.

sessions.title: Mo3-D Integrated quantum photonics (i)
sessions.track: SC 11: Quantum communications, physical layer security, and optical quantum technologies

talks.title: Mo3-D1: Practical Real-time CV-QKD with a Chip-scale Receiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Servello, Igor / Gleissner, Peter / Loesch, Fabian / Khan, Imran

Scalable hardware and real-time operation are key requirements for field-deployable QKD. We demonstrate an automated CV-QKD system featuring a miniaturized receiver, built on chip-scale telecom laser and integrated coherent receiver. This system enables real-time key generation over 26 km and 52 km links.

talks.title: Mo3-D2: High-Speed Squeezed-State CV-QKD Over 10 km Fiber With a CMOS-Compatible Electronic-Photonic Integrated Receiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bastiaens, Sarah / Nguyen, Huy Quang / Sidhique, Aboobackkar / Cammarata, Simone / Andersen, Ulrik Lund / Hajomer, Adnan Adil Ebrahim / Gehring, Tobias / Yin, Xin

The bandwidth limitations of squeezed-state CV-QKD are addressed by implementing a photonic–electronic integrated receiver with a CMOS transimpedance amplifier and a broadband single-pass squeezer. A 8.45 Mbit/s asymptotic key rate is achieved over 10 km with 500 MBaud signaling rate, demonstrating scalable high-speed squeezed-state CV-QKD.

talks.title: Mo3-D3: Time-Bin BB84 QKD System Using Indium Phosphide and Silicon Nitride Photonic Integrated Circuits
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fatkhiev, Denis / Grebenchukov, Alexander / Dos Reis Frazão, João / Nazarikov, Gleb / Okonkwo, Chigo / Tafur Monroy, Idelfonso

We demonstrate a dual-chip InP-SiN photonic QKD system with on-chip pulse generation and reconfigurable decoding, implementing time-bin BB84 with finite-key security against coherent attacks. The system sustains a QBER below 4% and delivers secret keys at kbps rates over 150–250 km of fiber.

talks.title: Mo3-D4: Silicon-Native QKD Transmitter for Bidirectional Quantum/Classical Co-Existence in High-Speed PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Honz, Florian / Boxleitner, Winfried / Hentschel, Michael / Saggio, Valeria / Schrenk, Bernhard

We prove secure-key generation over passive optical network plants for co-existing C- / O-band quantum/classical channels utilizing an all-silicon QKD transmitter, involving a 2×16 power split while being able to tolerate bidirectional classical launch levels up to 0 dBm.

talks.title: Mo3-D5: Thin-film lithium niobate for quantum photonics: perspectives and challenges
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ding, Yunhong / Zhdanov, Innokentiy / Oxenløwe, Leif K.

Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) photonics has recently emerged as an appealing platform for quantum photonics thanks to its low-loss characteristics, large electro-optic and nonlinear coefficients, and broad transparency window. Here, we discuss the latest developments, promising directions, and challenges for future TFLN quantum photonics research.

sessions.title: Mo3-E Optical non-terrestrian networks
sessions.track: SC 06: Architecture, modelling and performance of optical networks

talks.title: Mo3-E1: Demonstration of WDM, QoT-Aware Rate Adaptation and Add/Drop Operation in Inter-satellite All-optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Oda, Shoichiro / Brasi, Anthony / Hirota, Yusuke / Kotake, Hideaki / Shinada, Satoshi / Furukawa, Hideaki

Using a seven-node inter-satellite all-optical network (ISAON) testbed driven by Starlink TLE data, we demonstrate WDM, QoT-aware rate adaptation, and WXC add/drop under realistic time-varying inter-satellite loss emulation. Under HPA-limited power, four-channel WDM reaches 800 Gb/s. WDM-capable QoT estimation enables upgrades with ≤1.4 dB error.

talks.title: Mo3-E1: Adaptive Lightpath-Correlation Refinement for Efficient QoT-Aware Routing in Transparent Satellite Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Higashimori, Katsuaki / Shimizu, Shimpei / Kawai, Akira / Ohara, Takuya

We propose a method for efficiently routing lightpaths by adaptively switching their QoT and objective policies in transparent satellite WDM networks under stringent and time-varying transmission conditions. The method demonstrates equivalent network performance while dramatically reducing more than 70% power and 98% computation time.

talks.title: Mo3-E3: Intelligent Empowerment of Optical-Computation Synergy: Signal Processing and Resource Management for Multi-Band Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gu, Rentao / Liu, Jiaxin / Mei, Feng / Gao, Xiaoxuan / Li, Yunxuan / Li, Xinyue / Ji, Yuefeng

This paper presents an AI-driven control architecture for optical-computation synergy in AI data center interconnection. Multi-band optical networks provide interconnect support, while AI enhances signal processing and resource management, further strengthening support for computing. We review recent advances and outline future integrated multi-agent control.

talks.title: Mo3-E4: Experimental Data-driven Forward and Inverse SOA WDM Gain and SNR Modelling using Gaussian Process Regression
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yuan, Alan / Harvey, Calum / Ye, Xiaoyan / Savory, Seb

We experimentally demonstrate data-driven Gaussian process regression for SOA modelling in a worst-case WDM system, with 0.1dB gain and 0.23dB SNR mean absolute error. Inverse modelling is demonstrated for estimating the required SOA injection current, temperature, and input channel powers to achieve channel-specific SNR targets.

sessions.title: Mo3-F DSP for high spectral efficiency and SDM
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: Mo3-F1: Turbo Equalization with Duobinary Precoding for High-speed Bandwidth-limited IM/DD Transmission Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kong, Tianyuan / Stojanovic, Nebojsa / Wettlin, Tom / Ben Yacoub, Emna / Matuz, Balazs / Dai, Xianbo / Xhemrishi, Marvin / Calabrò, Stefano / Kuschnerov, Maxim / Pachnicke, Stephan

We propose turbo equalization with duobinary-BCJR detection to mitigate error floors and boost performance of weak inner codes in bandwidth-limited channels. Simulations and experiments demonstrate significant SNR gains and error floor elimination using duobinary precoding. Analytical limits confirm advantages for high-speed optical links.

talks.title: Mo3-F2: Reduced-Complexity Partial MIMO Equalization for Real-Time GPU-based 10-Mode Transmission over 26 km GI-FMF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bravo Ospina, Ruby Stella / Winter, David / Ryf, Roland / Fontaine, Nicolas / Dallachiesa, Lauren / Sillard, Pierre / Bigot, Marianne / Achten, Frank / Neilson, David / Mazur, Mikael

We investigate partial MIMO equalization in real-time 10-mode transmission over 26 km of FMF and demonstrate that the technique successfully tracks channel dynamics over time, enabling flexible performance-complexity reduction trade-offs in MG-selective FMF transmission.

talks.title: Mo3-F3: Non-Data-Aided SDM MIMO Equalization for Randomly-Coupled Multi-Core Fibers with a Tap-Correlation Avoidance CMA
talks.abstract:
Authors: Oezsuna, Pamir / Arnould, Aymeric / Freund, Ronald / Rademacher, Georg

We propose the tap-correlation avoidance (TCA-)CMA, a low-complexity, non-data-aided MIMO equalizer for RC-MCFs, preventing singularities by penalizing tap-weight correlations. Simulations using 32 GBd 16-QAM signals show singularity-free convergence up to 600 ps total delay spread for 3-, 4-core fibers and 300 ps for 7-core fiber.

talks.title: Mo3-F4: Simple Direct Estimation of Link SMD and MDL for MIMO-DSP Design in Ultra-Wideband Coupled-Core Fiber Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kawai, Akira / Shibahara, Kohki / Imada, Ryota / Sakamoto, Taiji / Nakajima, Kazuhide / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We propose a simple optical setup for estimating SMD and MDL in coupled-core fibers over a 150-nm bandwidth without full MIMO-DSP characterization. The method is validated by measurements on 4- and 12-core fibers and by C+L-band WDM MIMO transmission over a field-installed 12-core link.

talks.title: Mo3-F5: Advances in High-Spectral-Efficiency Formats: Modulation and Coding
talks.abstract:
Authors: Batshon, Hussam / Raybon, Gregory / Che, Di / Chen, Xi

Probabilistic amplitude shaping, increasingly adopted in coherent systems, relies on bit-metric decoding that introduces residual demapping loss. This paper shows that single parity-check coded probabilistic shaping reduces this loss via iterative demapping, achieving up to 0.9 dB SNR gain experimentally confirmed in long-haul WDM transmission.

sessions.title: Mo3-G Submarine and unrepeatered systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: Mo3-G1 Technologies and challenges for beyond petabit submarine cable
Mo3-G2: Algorithmically-Optimized Real-Time 18 Tb/s Throughput over a 16,608 km Trans-Pacific Subsea Link
talks.abstract:
Authors: Stephens, Marc / Dunnigan, Zach / Meaklim, Colin / Hubbard, Michael / Santillo, Franco / Evans, Darwin / Karam, David / Kalaiyarasan, Periyathambi / Guimaraes, Thayso / Mehta, Priyanth / Hooi, Esther / Rivera-Hartling, Elizabeth / Perrier, Philippe

We report 18 Tb/s throughput across a 16,608 km trans-Pacific subsea link using an algorithmically-optimized channel plan, for a record 298.9 Pb/s·km. Bidirectional SNR margins were 0.18–0.75 dB for all 28 channels. Additionally, an 800 Gb/s (173 GBd) signal reached 4.57 bits/s/Hz spectral efficiency

talks.title: Mo3-G4: Few-Mode Fibre for Noise Transfer Mitigation in Co-Raman Amplified Unrepeatered Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Busson, Alexis / Quenu, Marion / Courty, Julien / Renot, Bastien / Bissessur, Hans

We present a real-time Unrepeatered experiment using a short section of Few-Mode Fibre at the transmitter side to mitigate non-linear degradation due to Co-Raman amplification. We demonstrate an improvement up to 0.4 dB of Q factor margin compared to classical fibre with large effective area.

talks.title: Mo3-G5: Impact of RIN Transfer and Pump-Induced XPM on Coherent Transmission with Forward-Pumped-Raman Amplification
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kimura, Kosuke / Shimizu, Shimpei / Nakamura, Masanori / Hamaoka, Fukutaro / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We propose a numerical framework for estimating the impact of pump-to-signal RIN transfer and pump-induced XPM on QoT under forward-Raman pumping. Numerical estimates show reasonable agreement with experiments in single-channel and WDM configurations. The results indicate that pump-induced XPM is more significant than RIN transfer

talks.title: Mo3-G6: Real-time 52.8 Tb/s (26.4Tb/s/core) Unrepeatered Transmission over 303.4km of Uncoupled 2-core MCF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, BENYUAN / Stegmaier, Matthias / Geisler, Tommy / Borel, Peter / Palsdottir, Bera / Jenneve, Philippe / Zhang, Hongbin

We demonstrate real-time unrepeatered transmission of 52.8 Tb/s over 303.4 km uncoupled 2-core MCF using commercial pluggable modules and ultra-low loss SCUBA2X fibre (0.147 dB/km). We achieve 26.4 Tb/s per core (33×800Gb/s/core) and show no measurable inter-core crosstalk penalty in both unidirectional and bidirectional operations.

sessions.title: Mo3-C Lasers and sources
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: Mo3-C1: Semiconductor Optical Amplifier for WDM and High-Power Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rocas, Stanislav / Vostrikov, Evgenii / Belykh, Vasilii / Poltavtsev, Sergey / Gebel, Julia / Zhabotinskii, Artem / Mikhrin, Vladimir / Kim, Boris / Mikhrin, Sergey / Rautert, Janina / Gubenko, Alexey / Kovsh, Alexey

Two different types of quantum-dot O-band semiconductor optical amplifiers are demonstrated using a single epitaxial structure. By varying the device length, both low-noise WDM amplification and near watt-class output power are achieved, enabling linear and high-power operation within a single technology.

talks.title: Mo3-C2: High Power ASE Source Module with Innovative Architecture
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gallet, Antonin / Wu, You / El Dahdah, Nayla / Lamkadmi Azouigui, Sheherazade / Brenot, Romain

We propose a 50nm and 70mW white source module with innovative design based on a single Semiconductor Optical Amplifier (SOA) with an optical circulator. By combining it with a high power SOA amplifier, we obtain 430 mW in-fiber power.

talks.title: Mo3-C3: Rare-earth ion doped on-chip amplifiers in the Al2O3 platform
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jongebloed, Bjorn / Wang, Kai / Osornio Martinez, Carlos / Bonneville, Dawson / Mashlah, Abeer / Dijkstra, Meindert / García-Blanco, Sonia M.

Reactive sputtering of rare-earth-ion-doped Al₂O₃ enables scalable on-chip optical amplification across multiple wavelength bands. Monolithic integration with passive photonic platforms, combined with low nonlinearities and high-power handling, supports applications in telecommunications, datacom, sensing, and quantum photonics. Recent progress using erbium, thulium, and neodymium is reviewed.

talks.title: Mo3-C4: Compact Widely Tunable InP Laser with 10 kHz Linewidth
talks.abstract:
Authors: Leissling, Victor / Kähler, Maximilian

We demonstrate a monolithic InP laser foundry-fabricated on a multi-project wafer that employs two passive parallel ring resonators, targeting coherent interconnects. It achieves 10 kHz intrinsic linewidth, 46 nm tuning range, >35 dB SMSR and 6 mW on-chip output power within a 0.8 mm² footprint.

talks.title: Mo3-C5: Over 400-mW O-band Monolithic MOPA Laser Array Based on REC Technology for CPO/OIO
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Zhenxing / Xiao, Rulei / Shi, Yuechun / Xu, Pengfei / Wang, Yan / Chen, Xiangfei

We propose and demonstrate a MOPA array with precise wavelength spacing based on the REC technique. The MOPA laser array achieves an output power exceeding 400 mW when operating at 50°C, providing an excellent high-power light source solution for CPO/ OIO technologies.

sessions.title: Mo3-H New approaches for linear and nonlinear functionalities
sessions.track: SC 12: CLEO® Special Session on Emerging Trends in Optics and Photonics

talks.title: Mo3-H1: Frequency Comb Generation in Single-Mode Silicon Microresonators at 1550 nm in Normal Dispersion Regime
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shetewy, Abdou / Zhang, Weizhong / He, Menglong / Hamerly, Ryan / Jamshidi, Kambiz

We demonstrate frequency comb generation in a single-mode silicon microring resonator under normal dispersion at 1550 nm. Using a dual-pump configuration (2.5 mW and 27 µW) and an 11 V bias, seven comb lines spanning 3.74 THz are observed, indicating stable and coherent oscillation.

talks.title: Mo3-H2: Large-aperture Optical Antenna with Vertical Emission in Silicon-on-Insulator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Godoy Lorite, Elio / Moreno Pozas, Laureano / Halir, Robert / Wangüemert Pérez, J. Gonzalo / Ortega Moñux, Alejandro / Molina Fernández, Iñigo

Vertically emitting optical antennas with large mode-fields diameters are key for free space optics and atomic spectroscopy, but have not been yet reported in silicon-on-insulator. We present a novel vertically radiating antenna with a mode-field diameter of 200µm by 320µm with measured 48% efficiency.

talks.title: Mo3-H3: Sputtered AlN buffer layer for low loss crystalline AlN on sapphire integrated photonics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Brès, Camille-Sophie / Brunetta, Samuele / Sbarra, Samantha / Carlin, Jean-François / Grandjean, Nicolas / Butté, Raphaël

To fully exploit the broad transparency window of crystalline AlN through nonlinear optics, both dispersion engineering and low optical losses are required. We present thick regrown AlN waveguides enabling three-octave supercontinuum generation and show how a sputtered AlN buffer suppresses void-induced scattering, establishing a pathway toward low-loss visible-to-mid-infrared integrated photonics. ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: Mo3-H4: Harnessing Nonlinear and Optomechanical Phenomena in Silicon Nanostructures
talks.abstract:
Authors: Alonso Ramos, Carlos

Subwavelength silicon nanostructures enable precise control of light and optomechanical interactions in integrated devices. We review our recent advances in mid-infrared silicon photonics and the optimization of Brillouin interactions in non-suspended optomechanical cavities. ©2026 The Author(s)

sessions.title: Mo3-I Winning interconnects for AI: scale-up & scale-out technology paths
Afternoon coffee break
Mo4-P Poster

talks.title: Mo4-P-100: Field Demonstrations of Operational Strain Modal Analysis of a Historic Suspension Bridge Using Installed Telecom Fibres
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fan, Bo / Rui, Haozhe / Purnell, Mathew / Jin, Wei / Yi, Xingwen / Giddings, Roger / Faruk, Md Saifuddin / Tang, Jianming

We demonstrate operational strain modal analysis of the Menai suspension bridge using installed telecom fibre and distributed acoustic sensing. Using enhanced frequency-domain decomposition, we extract key structural health indicators, including natural frequencies, mode shapes, and damping ratios, providing a cost-effective, continuous, and robust SHM solution.

talks.title: Mo4-P-101: A New Optical Fiber-Based Sensor for Concentrated Solar Flux Monitoring in Concentrated Solar Power Plants
talks.abstract:
Authors: García-Borja, Javier / Carballar, Alejandro / Conceição, Ricardo / González-Aguilar, José / Thies, Alexander

This paper presents the proof of concept of a novel optical fiber-based sensor to measure concentrated solar flux up to 1 MW/m2 in Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) applications. The proposal constitutes an efficient, passive, robust and low-maintenance alternative to traditional radiometers.

talks.title: Mo4-P-102: A Field Demonstration of Cross Lake Free Space Optical Communication for 10GPON Backhaul
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wei, Buzheng / Zhang, He / Zhou, Changzheng / Feng, Zhongyi / Shen, Shikui / Wang, Guangquan / Wang, Zelin / Xu, Feng / Tang, Xiongyan / Zhou, Yantao / Zhao, Liang / Yang, Yuetang / Liu, Zhuchen / Yu, Mingjiao / Lin, LIning

This paper demonstrates a field trial in PON network utilizing a custom-designed FSO system cross an 1.3km lake environment. Operating at C-band without OA and FEC, the system achieves consecutive 6 hours of error-free 10Gbps transmission, validating FSO as an alternative solution for operator backhaul.

talks.title: Mo4-P-103: Geometric-Configuration Modulation: A Novel Free-Space Optical Communication Paradigm for D/r0 ~ 5 Turbulence Resistance
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bai, Yu-Ming / Ding, Ming-Han / Liu, Yu-Xuan / Li, Jun-Lin

We propose Geometric-Configuration Modulation (GM), a novel AO-free FSO paradigm utilizing multi-source geometric configuration encoding and active correlative decoding. GM demonstrates exceptional resistance to strong atmospheric turbulence (D/r0~5.0) over a 1.2 m link in preliminary experiments. ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: Mo4-P-104: Experimental Demonstration of Dual-Polarization PAM3 for Visible-Light Underwater Optical Wireless Communication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hanawa, Masanori / Khansalee, Ekkaphol / Rahman, Md Ashiqur / Yoshino, Ryoko

We experimentally demonstrate dual-polarization PAM3 as a 3 bit/s/Hz IM/DD scheme for visible-light underwater optical wireless communication. Polarization-axis mismatch between transmitter and receiver deformed square-like constellation maps into rhombic ones, causing BER floor; affine compensation was effective for ρ ≤ 20° but not at 30°.

talks.title: Mo4-P-105: High Sensitivity and High Speed SiPM Array Based Optical Wireless Receiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hou, Jingyu / Ali, Wajahat / Penty, Richard / Crisp, Michael

1×2 SiPM receiver arrays are experimentally demonstrated in high-speed optical wireless links. 9.5 Gbps transmission is achieved using a 2× 10010 SiPM array, while the required irradiance at 8 Gbps is reduced by 6.25× compared to a single 10010 SiPM receiver.

talks.title: Mo4-P-106: Enhancing Turbulence Resilience in Free-Space Optical Communications Using Germanium-Silicon Photodiode Array Interfaced with Multi-Core Fiber via Vertical Grating Couplers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lin, Yuan-Zeng / Lin, Yu-Han / Weng, Cheng-Si / Kuo, Hsiang-Yi / Lee, Shin-Yu / Chow, Chi-Wai

We demonstrate a free-space-optical-communication (FSOC) with enhanced atmospheric-turbulence resilience using germanium-silicon (GeSi) photodiode-array interfaced with multi-core-fiber (MCF) via vertical-grating-couplers (VGC). Experimental results show the proposed scheme significantly improves FSOC performance under different turbulence conditions.

talks.title: Mo4-P-107: A Novel Integrated Multi-Gb/s Optical Wireless Communication and Sub-μm Particle Sensing System for IoT Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jiao, Tiankuo / Kazemi, Hossein / Huang, Yifan / Haas, Harald

A proof-of-concept optical wireless integrated sensing and communication (OW-ISAC) system is proposed, demonstrating 0.5–10 μm particulate matter (PM) detection and 7.3 Gb/s optical wireless communication (OWC) at hard decision forward error correction (HD-FEC) bit error ratio (BER), using a single laser diode (LD).

talks.title: Mo4-P-108: Optical Hotspot for Adaptive Pencil-/Wide-Beam Formation for Fiber-Wireless Connectivity with Integrated User Localization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Honz, Florian / Schrenk, Bernhard

We propose an optical hotspot for adaptive pencil-/wide-beam formation, enabling user localization and the establishment of an optical fiber-wireless connection by means of tunable optics. We confirm stable optical wireless operation over a free-space link reach of 107 m.

talks.title: Mo4-P-109: Compact VCSEL–Metasurface OAM Transmitter with SIMO Processing for Optical Wireless Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ahmad, Rizwana / Nieminen, Arttu / Caglayan, Humeyra / Haas, Harald

Optical wireless interconnects require compact transmitters and robust detection. We demonstrate a VCSEL–metasurface OAM link with SIMO processing for short-reach interconnects. At the FEC threshold, ZF achieves 3.84 Gbps (no turbulence) and 1.96 Gbps (D/r0 = 0.2), outperforming MRC, confirming interference-limited operation under considered receiver.

talks.title: Mo4-P-10: Novel Photonic Lantern with Higher Order Radial Mode Suppression
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wei, Jin

We present the design and fabrication of a novel 6-core photonic lantern to suppress the LP02 mode, by omitting its central core. The device was characterised by off-axis digital holography achieving
an average 27.41 dB suppression (versus 32 dB simulated) with -0.19 dB throughput loss.

talks.title: Mo4-P-110: AI-Driven Detection and Localization of Optical Filtering Soft Failures via Digital Twin
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rosso, Andrea / Miotto, Enrico / D'Ingillo, Rocco / Curri, Vittorio

We propose a digital twin-assisted neural network for detecting, localizing, and characterizing soft failures in optical filters. Leveraging optical channel monitor and transceiver metrics, the method achieves high accuracy enabling scalable monitoring in complex optical networks.

talks.title: Mo4-P-111: Experimental Demonstration of Compilation-oriented AI Agent for Autonomous PON Slice Provisioning
talks.abstract:
Authors: Park, Chansung / Ra, Yongwook / Chung, HwanSeok

We demonstrate a compilation-oriented AI agent for autonomous PON slicing. By aggregating multi-source evidence into a shared specification, the AI agent enables model-agnostic improvements in provisioning reliability and token efficiency. Experiments on a 25G PON testbed demonstrate consistent dual-slice provisioning performance across multiple LLMs.

talks.title: Mo4-P-112: Wavelength and Polarization Diversity OTDR for Highly Accurate Fiber Faults Identification
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wu, Hongcheng / Li, Desheng / Liu, Zecong / Zhong, Kangping / Khan, Faisal

We experimentally demonstrate a wavelength- and polarization-diversity OTDR for fiber faults identification in data-center networks. Our system accurately distinguishes fiber faults beyond conventional OTDR capabilities. Six critical fault types are emulated, and the proposed OTDR architecture, aided by ML, demonstrates over 99% faults identification accuracy.

talks.title: Mo4-P-113: Bridging the 6G Gap: Scaling Sustainable ROADM-Based IP-over-WDM via DSCM-Enabled Point-to-Multipoint Designs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rafiei Forooshani, Matin / Arpanaei, Farhad / Beyranvand, Hamzeh / Ranjbar Zefreh, Mahdi / Fernández-Palacios, Juan Pedro / Sánchez-Macián, Alfonso / Hernández, José Alberto / Larrabeiti, David

This study compares transponder-based, Point-to-Point, and DSCM-based Point-to-Multipoint
(PtMP) access-metro architectures. Findings demonstrate that PtMP IPoWDM significantly optimizes
efficiency across diverse geotypes, slashing CAPEX by 92.0% and power by 99.2% compared to
traditional benchmarks over a ten-year horizon.

talks.title: Mo4-P-114: Demonstration of Full-network Level Digital Twin for QoT Estimation in Field-deployed ROADM Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jiang, Xiaotian / Huo, Xiaoli / Chen, Chaolun / Zhao, Guoyong / Cheng, Xianghao / Qin, Xin / Wang, Yisong / Han, Yuqing / Lv, Zheqing / Liu, Yuyang / Gong, Yadong / Zhang, Anxu / Li, Junjie

We propose and demonstrate a full-network level digital twin framework for QoT estimation in China Telecom's field-deployed ROADM networks, achieving mean aboslute errors of 0.53 dBm power and 0.68 dB OSNR for 95% test samples across all frequencies and loading rates.

talks.title: Mo4-P-115: Max-Flow-Based OCS Reconfiguration Scheduling for Full-Stack Distributed LLM Training Acceleration in Optical AIDC
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fu, Dianxuan / Liu, Xingyu / Liu, Qile / Li, Jiaqiu / Zhang, Yihao / Qiu, Qizhi / Liu, Xiaomin / Hu, Weisheng / Zhuge, Qunbi

We propose a max-flow-based OCS reconfiguration scheduling framework on our full-stack scale-out AIDC platform to accelerate LLM training. The proposed method reduces iteration time by up to 65.58% and improves All-Gather flow completion time by up to 15.36× under heuristically pruned GPU grouping.

talks.title: Mo4-P-116: Integrated Sensing and Communication for Real-Time Detection and Localization in Live Production Metro Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Malik, Gulmina / Ambrosone, Renato / Masood, Muhammad Umar / Ali, Ahtisham / Cheruvakkadu Mohamed, Mashboob / Straullu, Stefano / Kishore Bhyri, Sai / maria Galimberti, Gabriele / Napoli, Antonio / Pedro, João / Wakim, Walid / Curri, Vittorio

We present an integrated SOP-based sensing framework for real-time detection and localization of fiber disturbances in a 31 km live production metro network. The ML classifier achieved 96.2% accuracy, while bidirectional measurements enabled median localization errors below 23 m, supporting controller-assisted alarms and maintenance operations.

talks.title: Mo4-P-117: Highly Indistinguishable Dual-Channel Integrated Microring Single-Photon Source
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hou, Baojie / Chen, Donghui / Ma, Haoran / Zhao, Zichao / Liang, Qishen / Wang, Xinyu / Zhang, Bin / Tu, Yawen / Zhang, Yongdi / Gong, Bangmin / Dai, Tingge / Wang, Yuehai / Zhu, Huihui / Yang, Jianyi

Here, we propose a highly indistinguishable dual-channel integrated microring single-photon source based on bidirectional pumping. It achieves spectral purities of 96.13% and 96.96% in the two directions, respectively, alongside a 95.89% two-photon interference visibility.

talks.title: Mo4-P-118: Throttling Protocol for Quantum Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Noirie, Ludovic / Varloot, Rémi

We propose a new throttling mechanism for quantum link control in entanglement-based quantum networks. Using Markov chain modeling, we demonstrate Bell pair delivery stabilization, enabling an easier consumption by the upper layers of the quantum network protocol stack.

talks.title: Mo4-P-119: Performance Statistics and Joint Optimization of CV-QKD and Classical Traffic in Dynamically Allocated Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Alves Zischler, Lucas / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein / Mecozzi, Antonio / Antonelli, Cristian

We analyze the performance of classical and quantum CV-QKD systems, operating under dynamic classical traffic, assessing how classical signal statistics affects QKD performances. Furthermore, for channel-dynamics compensation, we introduce a novel gradient-descent-based approach for real-time optimization of quantum and classical throughput.

talks.title: Mo4-P-11: Machine Learning in Hollow Core Fiber Design
talks.abstract:
Authors: Abouelela, Rania Antar Eltaieb / Larochelle, Sophie / Rusch, Leslie A.

We generate numerous high-performance designs using neural networks predicting confinement loss in nested anti-resonant nodeless fibers. These designs provide meaningful statistics to identify a high-fidelity figure of merit, aiding future complex designs with multiple metrics.

talks.title: Mo4-P-120: Seamless Integration of Practical Quantum Key Distribution in Future Passive Optical Networks via Adaptive Scheduling
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gagliano, Alessandro / Fumagalli, Francesco / Gatto, Alberto / Boffi, Pierpaolo / Martelli, Paolo / Parolari, Paola

We investigate upstream DV-QKD in future passive optical networks under the finite-key regime, demonstrating that adaptive scheduling enables interference-reduced quantum-transmission windows and improves secret key rate, reach and scalability, especially in coexistence with XG-PON systems.

talks.title: Mo4-P-121: Performance Comparison of QKD Key Relaying Strategies Across Diverse Network Topologies
talks.abstract:
Authors: Álvarez Roa, María / Verschoor, Sebastian / Rommel, Simon

By evaluating across diverse network topologies, we provide a comparison of on-demand relaying and key flooding strategies for QKD using the key request success rate metric. Results show that key flooding outperforms on-demand relaying in sparse, low-connectivity networks, while on-demand relaying benefits from higher connectivity.

talks.title: Mo4-P-122: Quantum Time Synchronization in Star Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rollick, Brian / Huberman, Bernardo / Jia, Zhensheng

We demonstrate scalable multi-user clock synchronization using time-correlated photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric downconversion in a star network. Pairwise offsets are extracted from second-order correlations, while triangle closure provides a consistency metric. Measurements show sub-200 ps agreement, with Kalman tracking of offset and skew.

talks.title: Mo4-P-123: Joint Spectral Characterization of a Bright, Tunable, Continuous Wave Photon-Pair Source at Telecom Wavelengths
talks.abstract:
Authors: Scheijen, Stijn / Rieser, Thomas / Silanteva, Liudmila / Van Den Hout, Menno / Okonkwo, Chigo / Bradley, Thomas

We demonstrate a tunable fiber-coupled photon-pair source spanning λ = 1490 – 1630 nm with high internal spectral brightness (∼4.6·107 pairs/s/mW/nm). Using pulse carving, we measure the joint spectral intensity and achieve tunable spectral correlations via narrow-band filtering, enabling correlation control for quantum networking applications.

talks.title: Mo4-P-125: Optical Fuses and Isolation using 1D Grating Couplers against QKD Trojan Horse Attacks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Davidson, Zoe / Jones, Callum / Moses, Nathan / Joshi, Siddarth

The security of chip-based quantum key distribution (QKD) systems must be secured against high-power laser attacks. We test 1D grating coupler optical fuses as passive countermeasures. We find a heating-induced limit in back-reflections in addition to the damage threshold and discuss implications for QKD.

talks.title: Mo4-P-126: Adaptive Noise-Resistant Threshold Estimation for Quantum Zero-Knowledge Authentication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Giacomin, Livia / Gagliano, Alessandro / Gatto, Alberto / Martelli, Paolo

As quantum communications advance, user authentication becomes essential. This work studies a quantum identity authentication protocol under realistic noise, deriving a suitable threshold for Quantum Bit Error Rate verification and proposing an adaptive strategy that improves robustness and addresses information leakage across repeated authentication attempts.

talks.title: Mo4-P-127: Fully Automated Software-Defined Switched Quantum Key Distribution Network Enhanced with PUF Authentication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Makris, Nikolaos / Konteli, Persefoni / Sassalou, Evgenia N. / Kazazis, Stylianos A. / Papageorgopoulos, Alkinoos / Vasileiadis, Stefanos / Tsimvrakidis, Konstantinos / Tsintzos, Symeon / Nikolopoulos, Georgios M. / Kanellos, George T.

We demonstrate a fully automated 4-node switched-QKD network using PUF-based authentication orchestrated by a central SDN controller, enabling scalable and dynamic operation.

talks.title: Mo4-P-128: Secure 100-Gbit/s Real-time Spatially Multiplexed Quantum Random Number Generation Based on Vacuum Fluctuations
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tanizawa, Ken / Kato, Kentaro / Futami, Fumio

We demonstrate high-speed unpredictable random number generation using a single laser diode and parallel homodyne detectors. A spatially multiplexed setup with eight channels mitigates the trade-off between security and generation rate and achieves real-time 100-Gbit/s operation with a low security parameter of 5 × 10−30.

talks.title: Mo4-P-129: Frequency-Domain Locking of a Pulsed Microring Single-Photon Source via Low-Frequency Pump Transmission Extraction
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hou, Baojie / Zhao, Zichao / Ma, Haoran / Liang, Qishen / Wang, Xinyu / Yuan, Lingzhi / Guo, Zichen / Zhang, Bin / Liu, Yueyang / Wei, Zhujun / Wang, Yuehai / Zhu, Huihui / Dai, Tingge / Yang, Jianyi

Here, we report frequency-domain locking of a pulsed microring single-photon source by extracting the transmission spectrum derivative via low-frequency modulation. The generated zero-crossing error signal effectively compensates for resonance drift, enabling long-term, highly stable system operation.

talks.title: Mo4-P-12: Monolithically Integrated 2 × 226 Gbps Dual-Wavelength EML with a Passive MZI-based Optical Multiplexer
talks.abstract:
Authors: Terao, Kenichi / Tsuji, Toshiya / Morikawa, Takaya / Nishikawa, Satoshi / Morita, Yoshimichi / Ono, Akihito / Takase, Tadashi

We developed dual-wavelength integrated EMLs with a passive Mach‑Zehnder optical multiplexer requiring no phase‑tuning electrodes. The emission wavelengths are spaced for CWDM, and each supports 226 Gbps operation (113‑Gbaud PAM4). Measured insertion losses were 1.8 dB at 1311 nm and 4.3 dB at 1331 nm.

talks.title: Mo4-P-130: Practical Design of High-Density Bend Waveguide Array for Co-Packaged Fan-Out Routing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Matsumoto, Masaki / Furuta, Yuji / Denda, Tatsuaki / Katagiri, Noritaka

An optimised bend array under limited NA constraints reduces the minimum radius of curvature by 21% at 0.3 dB/turn and achieves −36 dB crosstalk (L/S= 2.5/40μm), enabling dense FO routing of 576 channels within a 15.0 mm length without major changes to existing package designs.

talks.title: Mo4-P-131: Lens-free on-chip vibrometer with millimetre working distance
talks.abstract:
Authors: Halir, Robert / Montilla-Gallardo, Manuel Jesús / Barona-Ruiz, Miguel / Arshad, Ayesha / Moreno Pozas, Laureano / De Oliva Rubio, José / Ortega Moñux, Alejandro

On-chip vibration sensors usually rely on bulk optics to deliver the sensing beam to the moving target, thereby limiting integration. We show that large optical antennas enable target distances of ~5mm while achieving measurement resolutions of 12nm, without using any bulk optics.

talks.title: Mo4-P-132: High-Extinction-Ratio Integrated Polarizer Based on a Subwavelength Grating Bent Waveguide
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lahbib, Hachim / Mokeddem, Zindine / D’anzieri, Gervasio / Salhi, Sarra / Edmond, Samson / Lanco, Loïc / Melati, Daniele

Silicon photonic devices show markedly different behaviors for TE and TM polarized modes, making polarization management critical. We experimentally demonstrate a TE-pass polarizer based on subwavelength-waveguide cut-off engineering and bend-assisted filtering, experimentally achieving an extinction ratio of 28 dB and insertion losses of −0.22 dB.

talks.title: Mo4-P-133: Software-reconfigurable wavelength-tunable dual optical frequency comb based on externally-injected gain-switched lasers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wei, Minghao / Rosado, Alejandro / Mcardle, Conor / Anandarajah, Prince M.

We demonstrate a software-reconfigurable wavelength-tunable dual optical frequency comb based on externally injected gain-switched lasers, achieving >30 nm contiguous tunability with minimum step of 2 pm. The system operates without wavelength-dependent re-optimisation while maintaining consistent DOFC performance across the tuning range, enabling broadband sensing

talks.title: Mo4-P-134: Efficient Fiber-Chip Optical Coupling in Silicon Nitride Photonics Using Amorphous Silicon Grating Overlays
talks.abstract:
Authors: Benedikovic, Daniel / Petrovic, Adam / Fraser, William / Korcek, Radovan / Schmid, Jens / Cheben, Pavel / Dominguez Bucio, Thalia / Gardes, Frederic / Ye, Winnie

We demonstrate α-Si/Si3N4 surface grating couplers with -1.6 dB experimental coupling loss. Inverse-designed multi-band couplers show −2 dB loss at O- and C-band wavelengths with -30 dB crosstalk. This enables compact and scalable fibre-chip interfaces for high-capacity optical communication and advanced photonic integrated circuits. Benedikovic

talks.title: Mo4-P-13: Demonstration of Higher-Order Tensor Contraction via Optical Nonlinear Wave Mixing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ko, Wing / Alhaddad, Abdulrahman / Ramakrishnan, Muralekrishnan / Li, Yichen / Zhang, Yixuan / Zuo, Yue / Jiang, Zile / Zhou, Huibin / Tur, Moshe / Habif, Jonathan / Willner, Alan

We demonstrate direct optical higher-order tensor contraction using nonlinear wave mixing in a periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide. The system performs the contraction of three order-3 tensors over three pairs of indices at 5 GHz with ~4-bit precision.

talks.title: Mo4-P-14: E-band InP-on-Si Tunable Laser via Micro-Transfer Printing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Dongbo / Soltanian, Emadreza / Qin, Senbiao / Vaissiere, Nicolas / Néel, Delphine / Ramirez, Joan / Decobert, Jean / Kuyken, Bart / Zhang, Jing / Roelkens, Gunther

We demonstrate a widely tunable E-band InP-on-Si laser heterogeneously integrated using micro-transfer printing. The laser achieves a tuning range of 41 nm (1398–1439 nm), with a side-mode suppression ratio above 45 dB and 3 mW output power in the silicon waveguide.

talks.title: Mo4-P-15: O-band InP Mach-Zehnder Modulator for 400 Gb/s per Lane in a Generic Pure-Play Foundry
talks.abstract:
Authors: Barcons Ruiz, David / Shamsafar, Alireza / Mameli, Alfredo / Augustin, Luc

To address increasing datacenter requirements of 400 Gb/s per lane we present an InP Mach-Zehnder modulator with measured electro-optic bandwidth above 67 GHz and Vπ of 2.6-3.4 V for an interaction length of just 0.8 mm. Our physics-based model predicts operation beyond 110 GHz.

talks.title: Mo4-P-16: Low-Loss Subwavelength Grating-Based Waveguide Crossings in Silicon Nitride at 1550 nm
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kolka, Polyxeni / Skënderas, Martin / Arzubiaga Totorika, Libe / Tran, Ying / Bao, Lifeng / Sandell, Elliot / Churchill, Glen / Liu, Hao / R. H. Bottrill, Kyle / Gardes, Frederic / Gates, James / Petropoulos, Periklis

We design, fabricate, and characterise subwavelength grating waveguide crossings in SiN for 1550 nm operation. Using cascaded structures, we measure state-of-the-art 0.052 dB/crossing loss with <−47 dB crosstalk. These results enable dense, low-loss routing for telecom PICs, surpassing prior SiN crossings.

talks.title: Mo4-P-17: Single-Drive Flat-Top Near-Visible Electro-Optic Frequency Comb Generation in Lithium Tantalate
talks.abstract:
Authors: Huang, Fei / Li, Haoran / Fu, Xinyan / Guo, Jingyan / Chen, Yuanchen / Xiong, Hongzhi / Yu, Zejie / Dai, Daoxin

We demonstrate a single-drive flat-top electro-optic comb generator at 798 nm in thin-film lithium tantalate. The device generates 49 comb lines, with a 5 dB bandwidth comprising 25 lines at an 18 GHz microwave drive.

talks.title: Mo4-P-18: Hybrid Integrated Tunable Laser with SiN Ring Resonators for Wide Wavelength Tuning and Locking
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kim, Jong-Hoi / Shin, Jang-Uk / Park, Sang-Ho / han, Young-Tak / Lee, Dong-Hoon / lee, Dongchoon / Cha, Sangjun

We demonstrate a hybrid integrated tunable external cavity laser utilizing SiN micro-ring resonators for tuning and locking of wavelengths, achieving a tuning range of 82 nm, an output power exceeding 16 dBm, and a SMSR over 56 dB.

talks.title: Mo4-P-19: A 500 Gbps Ultra-Compact Silicon Photonic Mach-Zehnder Modulator with >110 GHz Bandwidth
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Qian / Wei, Liqun / Cheng, Chao / Bao, Shenlei / Zhang, Wenfu / Wang, Binhao

We demonstrate a 500 Gbps silicon modulator with a length of 300 µm, integrating chirped phase-shifted grating and electro-optic frequency-domain equalization. The device achieves a tuning efficiency of 66 pm/V and an electro-optic bandwidth exceeding 110 GHz.

talks.title: Mo4-P-1: Simultaneous Rotational Alignment of Multi-Core Fiber Ribbons for Scalable Interconnection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sakaime, Katsuyoshi / Nagase, Ryo / Furukawa, Hideaki

We propose a simultaneous rotational alignment method for multi-core fibre ribbons, enabling scalable interconnection with reduced assembly time. Multiple fibres are aligned and selectively fixed during collective rotation using a dedicated jig. We experimentally demonstrate an average rotational misalignment of 0.83°.

talks.title: Mo4-P-20: Silicon Photonics Mode-Selective 3-dB Power Splitters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Izumisawa, Sora / Sato, Takanori / Saitoh, Kunimasa

Silicon mode-selective 3-dB power splitters based on multimode interference are experimentally demonstrated. They selectively split the TE0 or TE1 mode, allowing the other to pass. Furthermore, AI-based layout correction improves the power imbalance by up to 2.63 dB.

talks.title: Mo4-P-21: High-bandwidth and High-efficiency MOS Mach-Zehnder Modulator based on InGaAsP Membrane/Si Waveguide with Capacitively-loaded Travelling-wave Electrodes
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kasuya, Naotaka / Komatsu, Kento / Tanaka, Hajime / Inoue, Naoko / Kikuchi, Takehiko / Mitarai, Takuya / Kimura, Shun / Fujiwara, Naoki / Nishiyama, Nobuhiko / Takenaka, Mitsuru / Yagi, Hideki

We demonstrate InGaAsP/Si MOS Mach–Zehnder (MZ) modulators with capacitively-loaded travelling-wave electrodes. With a reduced RC constant, VpL-bandwidth trade-off is significantly improved, achieving bandwidth exceeding 60 GHz with VpL ~ 0.5 Vcm, representing the highest reported bandwidth for MOS MZ modulators on Si photonics platforms.

talks.title: Mo4-P-22: 80 GHz C+L Band Germanium Photodetector via Microheater
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Bingyan / Yin, Yuxiang / Li, Yihang / Wang, Yi / Tong, Yeyu / Du, Jiangbing / Xu, Ke

A germanium photodetector integrated with microheater is demonstrated for operation in C+L band. The detector has a measured dark current of 30 nA and responsivity of 0.76 A/W at 1625 nm. The bandwidth is 80 GHz supporting 96 Gbps NRZ signalling at 1600 nm.

talks.title: Mo4-P-23: Broadband Vernier-Programmable Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Triple-Ring Electro-Optic Modulator for High-Speed Optical Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yu, Tiancheng / Yan, Ao / Yang, Jie / Leong, Jin Feng / Zeng, Chenxuan / Wang, Tianyi / Zhao, Shi / Pan, Jieming / Hooda, Sonu / Zamburg, Evgeny / Thean, Aaron

We demonstrate a broadband Vernier-programmable triple-ring lithium niobate electro-optic modulator that overcomes single-ring high-frequency efficiency roll-off through supermode coupling. DC bias enables 19.4-GHz tuning of the peak RF operating frequency. The extracted response indicates a sideband-to-carrier ratio from -1.4 to -2.7 dB over this range.

talks.title: Mo4-P-24: A 112 Gbps and Direct-drive Silicon Microdisk Modulator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Jian / Zhang, Yunhao / Zhang, Bowen / Li, Yihang / Shu, Haowen / Li, Ke / Wang, Lei / Wang, Yi / Cai, Yan / Xu, Ke

We present a silicon microdisk modulator with 30 GHz electro-optic bandwidth and 0.57 V·cm modulation efficiency. For the first time, the silicon microdisk modulator can be directly driven with 0.8 Vpp swing for 112 Gbps four-level pulse amplitude modulation

talks.title: Mo4-P-25: Wafer-scale process-decoupled spectral stabilization in SiN CWDM (de)multiplexer
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Chih-Hsien / Hung, Yung-Jr

We demonstrate wafer-scale process decoupling and spectral stabilization in SiN CWDM photonics using sensitivity-engineered cascaded MZIs. Independent extraction of linewidth and thickness variations enables a Δλ/Δw-compensated design achieving -1.92 ± 0.95 nm wavelength shift with <2 dB insertion loss across a 12-inch wafer.

talks.title: Mo4-P-26: High-Power Multi-Wavelength Hybrid Integrated Laser Array for Co-Packaged Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Lei / Pile, Brian / Boothroyd, Simon / Yang, Jing / Soldano, Lucas / Guevarra, Enrico / Wang, Lin / Lee, James / Mo, Jinyu / Venkatesan, Suresh

A four-channel L-band hybrid laser array is demonstrated using an InP gain-chip array integrated on a CMOS-compatible optical interposer. Single-mode operation with >50 dB SMSR and 400 GHz spacing is achieved without active wavelength tuning. Each channel delivers over 20 dBm at 50 °C.

talks.title: Mo4-P-27: C+L Band Tunable External Cavity Laser Array Integrated using Photonic Wire Bonding
talks.abstract:
Authors: Saghiran, Youssef / Lamkadmi Azouigui, Sheherazade / El Dahdah, Nayla / Gallet, Antonin / Wu, You / Xie, Hongbo / Li, Zhaoming / Bregoli, Matteo / Eldahrawy, Tarek / Brenot, Romain / Charlet, Gabriel

We report on an 8-channel external cavity-based TLS integrated using PWB between a RSOA array and a SiN circuit array. We demonstrate a wide tunability over C+L band, output power>16 dBm, SMSR>60 dB and intrinsic linewidth<10KHz.

talks.title: Mo4-P-28: Multi-mode Microring Spectrometer without Photodetector
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yin, Yuchen / Xu, Chaojun / Xiang, Jinlong / Chen, Youlve / Zhao, Zhenyu / Zhao, Yaotian / Su, Yikai / Guo, Xuhan

We demonstrate a multi-mode microring resonator spectrometer assisted with two-photon absorption, achieving a 40 pm resolution across 50 nm bandwidth and record-high channel‑number‑to‑footprint ratio of 2.8 × 10⁶ mm-2. Without any external photodetector, this fully integrated spectrometer demonstrates excellent capability in on-chip optical sensing applications.

talks.title: Mo4-P-29: High-Density High-Throughput WDM Optical Transmitter Based on Lithium-niobate-on-insulator Platform
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dai, Yiqi / Cheng, Guanglian / Sun, Aolong / Yuan, Yuqin / Yuan, Hanming / Li, Chijun / Huang, Yuankang / Chen, Geng / Lu, Siyu / Shang, Chenglin / Xia, Jinsong / Chi, Nan / Zheng, Shuang / Zhang, Junwen / Zeng, Cheng / Shen, Li

We propose an ultra-compact Bragg microcavity modulator on LNOI platform, with a length of ~100μm, a measured 3-dB electro-optic bandwidth >110GHz and a modulation efficiency of ~6.6pm/V. It supports high-speed transmission of 140Gbit/s OOK and 180Gbit/s PAM4, enabling a 720Gbit/s four-channel transmitter.

talks.title: Mo4-P-2: Two-Pump Distributed Parametric Amplification of 25x 32Gbaud 16-QAM Channels over 25 km SSMF with ~20dB Gain
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mostafa, Munira B. / Saxena, Shekhar / Bastamova, Mariia / Elson, Daniel J. / Vitaly, Mikhailov / Emmerich, Robert / Luis, Ruben S. / luo, Jiawei / Furukawa, Hideaki / Schubert, Colja / Freund, Ronald / Digiovanni, David J. / Wakayama, Yuta / Phillips, Ian / Donodin, Aleksandr / Ellis, Andrew D. / Gordienko, Vladimir

We demonstrate distributed fiber optic parametric amplification of 25x 16-QAM 32Gbaud channels over 25 km of G.652.D in the O-band with GMI-estimated throughput of 3.148Tbps and on/off gain of ~20dB by employing two ~125mW pumps.

talks.title: Mo4-P-30: A 3.2 Tbps 2.5D Integrated Silicon Photonic Transmitter for Co-packaged Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Shuxiao / Dai, Dehua / Zhang, Huanwen / Zhang, Kai / Wei, Jingyu / Lu, Han / Zhang, Jianmin / Zhang, Dongyu / Xiao, Kelaiti / Cai, Yan

We demonstrate a 3.2 Tbps 2.5D integrated silicon photonic transmitter supporting a date transmission of 200 Gbps PAM4 modulation per channel. Full-link operation is experimentally validated, achieving 4.01 pj/bit energy efficiency at a total power consumption of 12.83W, highlighting its potential for co-packaged optics.

talks.title: Mo4-P-31: O-, E- and S-band Silicon Photonics Wavelength Cross-Connect Switch with Waveguide Bragg Gratings
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ikeda, Kazuhiro / Konoike, Ryotaro / Suzuki, Keijiro

We demonstrate an extended multiband operation over 300 nm using an improved wavelength cross-connect switch circuit in 2x2 and 32-ch scale, fully exploiting the potential available wavelength range of wavelength-selective couplers with waveguide sidewall gratings.

talks.title: Mo4-P-32: An All-Silicon Coherent Optical Receiver Beyond 100 GBd Using a Traveling-Wave SiGe BiCMOS TIA
talks.abstract:
Authors: Declercq, Jakob / Bomhals, Axl / De Busscher, Jonas / Sidhique, Aboobackkar / Moeneclaey, Bart / Bauwelinck, Johan / Yin, Xin

We demonstrate a coherent optical receiver integrating a silicon-photonic front-end with a 55-nm SiGe BiCMOS traveling-wave TIA. The receiver achieves 44-GHz bandwidth and supports single-polarization QPSK up to 140 GBd and 16-QAM up to 112 GBd.

talks.title: Mo4-P-33: Integrated Diffractive Slab Photonic Processor for Real-Time RF Spectrum Sensing and Matched Filtering
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shen, Zichao / Zhou, Wei / Ma, Weichao / Li, Wangzhe

We demonstrate a silicon-nitride diffractive slab photonic processor for real-time RF spectrum sensing and matched filtering. A 24-point, 9.12-GHz one-shot processor achieves 380-MHz resolution and 3-ns-scale response, while frequency stitching improves matched-filtering resolution to 47.5~MHz and yields >20-dB sidelobe suppression in pulse compression.

talks.title: Mo4-P-34: Highly Efficient Broadband Thin-Film Lithium Niobate MZM for 1μm Optical Communications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Aimone, Alessandro / Thomas, Philipp / Suganuma, Takahiro / Chen, Xi / Kim, Kwangwoong / Huynh, Tam / Fontaine, Nicolas

We demonstrate the first compact 1µm TFLN modulator with Vpi = 4.2 V (VpiL = 1.1 V‧cm) and electro-optical bandwidth > 110 GHz. We successfully demonstrate data modulation up to 145 GHz electro-optic bandwidth by upconverting a 20 GBd signal combined with single-ended heterodyne detection.

talks.title: Mo4-P-35: 212.5 Gbps SerDes-Driven Optical Engines Based on SiPh and TFLN Platforms
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Aoxue / Yin, Yuchen / Zhao, Yaotian / Jia, Erse / Hu, Xiao / Xu, Chaojun / Wei, Yiran / Xu, Bo / Hu, Fangchen / Shi, Jianyang / Guo, Xuhan / Cai, Haiwen / Chu, Wei

We demonstrate a 212.5 Gbps SerDes-based LRO interconnect to compare SiPh and TFLN engines. We employ EIC-PIC analog peaking to overcome SiPh bandwidth limits. Conversely, while a SerDes direct-drive architecture improves TFLN’s energy efficiency, it restricts signal integrity. This paper highlights these trade-offs.

talks.title: Mo4-P-36: Agile Wavelength-Switchable Self-Injection-Locked Narrow Linewidth DBR Laser for Coherent Wavelength Routing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Xiangyue / Su, Qingshuai / Wei, Fang / Han, Hexi / Chen, Chen / Yan, Yi / Chu, Wei / Cai, Haiwen

We propose a hybrid self-injection-locked DBR laser with a Si3N4 micro-ring external cavity for coherent wavelength routing. Enabled by optical feedback over C-band ITU channels, it achieves 89 ns switching, stable wavelength locking, and a 2.5 kHz linewidth for high-speed optical switching.

talks.title: Mo4-P-37: A 4-λ × 32-Gb/s Silicon Micro-Ring-Resonator-Based DWDM Receiver with On-Chip Temperature Controller
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lee, Jae-Ho / Yang, Seung-Jae / Ji, Yongjin / Wang, Xu / Kim, Dong-Hyeon / Kim, Hyun-Kyu / Choi, Woo-Young

We demonstrate a 4-λ x 32-Gb/s silicon MRR-based DWDM receiver with an on-chip temperature controller, automatically aligning and locking each MRR resonance wavelength to its target wavelength. Its operation is confirmed by electronic-photonic co-simulation using the Cadence design environment and experimentally verified under thermal stress.

talks.title: Mo4-P-38: Machine Learning-Assisted Digital Predistortion for Mask Margin Recovery in EML Transmitters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kaya, Cengizhan / Caruso, Giuseppe / Schulte, Patrick / Calabrò, Stefano

We demonstrate that machine learning-assisted digital predistortion effectively recovers eye-mask margin in EML transmitters biased in nonlinear region. Experimental results at 25GBd show a 13% margin improvement over the first order hold interpolation, while filter- and lookup-table-based approximations achieve comparable performance.

talks.title: Mo4-P-39: A Novel Low-Complexity Clock Recovery for Non-Integer Oversampling Coherent Optical Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, YuKun / Gong, XiaoXue / Hou, WeiGang / Guo, Lei

Non-integer oversampling technique has been widely adopted in high-speed coherent optical transmission. We propose a novel low-complexity clock recovery algorithm for recovering the clock of non-integer oversampled signals. Compared to conventional methods, the novel clock recovery algorithm reduces the number of real multiplications by 93%

talks.title: Mo4-P-3: Generation and Modulation of Second-order Nonlinearity in the Microfibre
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ma, Yuxin / Jiang, Biqiang

We demonstrate optical fibre schemes assisted with low-dimensional materials to implement second-order nonlinear processes. The functionalized fibre devices have achieved tunable and broadband second harmonic and sum-frequency generation under low peak-power CW lasers, facilitating applications in nonlinear fibre optics.

talks.title: Mo4-P-40: Enabling High-Reliability Link Monitoring in In-Vehicle PONs via Correlation OTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xu, Zhaojun / Liu, Wu / zhang, Yaoyang / luo, Ming / Li, Hanbing / Han, Wenjun / Luo, Wenyong

We propose an in-vehicle PON monitoring scheme based on correlation OTDR. By incorporating in-band communication, the scheme achieves centimeter-level spatial resolution while enabling the detection of nanosecond-level outages and sub-0.2 dB power fluctuations.

talks.title: Mo4-P-41: Real-Time FPGA Implementation and Verification of OSA-Aided SBC-BCH FEC for 100G Coherent Optical Access Network
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hwang, In-Ki / Kang, Hun-Sik / Lee, Joon Ki

We present the first real-time FPGA implementation of an OSA-aided SBC-BCH FEC for 100G coherent optical networks. Featuring a 7.6μs round-trip latency, it achieves a 2.5×10⁻¹⁰ post-FEC BER at 8.6×10⁻³ pre-FEC BER, confirming stable operation with a PTBC-based coherent DSP.

talks.title: Mo4-P-42: In-Service Transceiver Calibration for Digital Subcarrier Signals with Synthesising IQ Imbalance via Offloaded Multi-layer Filters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sato, Masaki / Arikawa, Manabu / Matsui, Junichiro / Hosokawa, Kohei

We proposed Tx/Rx-IQ imbalance calibration for digital-subcarrier signals using synthesised responses from multi-layer filters. In 1,200‑km WDM transmission of 128‑GBd 8‑DSC PM‑PCS‑64QAM, Q-penalties within 0.1 dB under 2.5-ps Tx-IQ skew, 3-ps Rx-IQ skew, 2.5-dB Tx-IQ peaking error, and 63‑GHz Rx-IQ imbalanced bandwidth limitation were demonstrated.

talks.title: Mo4-P-43: High-Fidelity Fiber Longitudinal Power Monitoring via Spatially-Decoupled Sparse Regularization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zuo, Yan / Su, Xingrui / Liu, Wu / Luo, Ming / Li, Hanbing

We experimentally demonstrate a non-uniform sparse regularization approach for longitudinal power monitoring. Leveraging spatial decoupling, this method accurately recovers all power discontinuities, including EDFA gains and anomalies. Using limited measurements, it achieves 1-km localization accuracy and an RMSE reduction of 0.41–0.6 dB.

talks.title: Mo4-P-44: 128 Gb/s CAP-16 Transmission Over 100 m OM4 MMF Using Low-Complexity ABCD Linearization of a Directly Modulated VCSEL
talks.abstract:
Authors: Low, Yee Hui / Bamiedakis, Nikos / Cunningham, David / Penty, Richard

We demonstrate 128-Gb/s (32-Gbaud) CAP-16 transmission over 100-m OM4 MMF using a low-cost commercial 21-GHz VCSEL and low-complexity ABCD linearization. The method successfully mitigates the VCSEL non-linearity, achieving a ~2x EVM reduction vs conventional FFE. FFE-only implementation fails to support this data rate.

talks.title: Mo4-P-45: Online Low-Power Time-Varying IQ skew Estimation Scheme for Ultra-High-Speed Coherent Receivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Chengbo / Wei, Shuai / Jiang, Hexun / Wang, Zhuo / Chen, Yizhao / Wang, Yongben / Zhao, Ye / Li, Xiang / Liu, Hengqi

We propose to use an online low-power side-path DSP to estimate the IQ skew of ultra-high-speed coherent receivers. Its effectiveness is experimentally verified in a 90 GBaud transmission experiment, with an estimation error of less than 1% of the symbol period.

talks.title: Mo4-P-46: HCF Gas Line Absorption Mitigation: On the Interplay between Pre-emphasis and SOA Nonlinear Compensation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nguyen, Trung-Hien / Lorences-Riesgo, Abel / Mumtaz, Sami / Nguyen, Hoang-Long / Qiu, Haoyang / Chen, Hao / Charlet, Gabriel

We experimentally and numerically investigate the interplay between GLA-dip emphasis (GE) and SOA-booster nonlinear compensation in 140 GBaud PCS-64QAM transmission system. Results show that the interplay causes 0.3 dB SNR penalty and the partial-GE is more favorable, providing 0.5 dB SNR gain at 7-dB dip.

talks.title: Mo4-P-47: Experimental Demonstration of Polar Coded Many-to-one Mapping based Truncated PS-PAM8 with 37-dB power budget
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jia, Xiaoshuo / Li, Junwei / Wang, Ning / Li, Jie / Luo, Ming / Li, Yan / Wu, Jian / Li, Han / Zhang, Dechao

In this paper, a polar coded truncated probabilistic shaped PAM-8 (PTPS-PAM8) operating at 200-Gb/s/lane is proposed and experimentally investigated using the intensity-modulation and coherent-detection structure. Adopting the PTPS-PAM8, a 2-dB ROP sensitivity improvement is obtained over the uniformly-distributed polar-coded PAM8 after 20-km transmission.

talks.title: Mo4-P-48: On LLR Calculations for Soft-decision Decoding in Next-generation IM-DD Systems with Laser RIN
talks.abstract:
Authors: Villenas, Felipe / Can Gültekin, Yunus / Alvarado, Alex

We propose a low-complexity LLR approximation for SD decoding in IM-DD systems with relative intensity noise. Our approximation results in no BER performance penalty for a concatenated KP4+Hamming FEC scheme, and outperforms mismatched AWGN-based LLRs.

talks.title: Mo4-P-49: Quantum-Well Comb DWDM Transmission via Residual Carrier-Based Phase Recovery and EEPN Mitigation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cai, Xiang / Niu, Yueying / Zhu, Yixiao / Zhong, Tianchi / Sun, Defan / Zhang, Tianhong / Lin, Fanghuasong / Song, Hao / Fang, Xiansong / Zhou, Xian / Lu, Dan / Zhang, Fan

We experimentally demonstrate 8λ×70-GBd 16QAM DWDM transmission over 1280-km SSMF using quantum-well mode-locked laser combs. We employ residual comb line-based phase tracking to address the 9.0-MHz and 54.6-MHz comb linewidths, achieving >6-dB Q2-factor improvement at BTB and 3.6-dB additional gain from EEPN after 1280-km transmission.

talks.title: Mo4-P-4: Enhanced Radiation Hardness of High-Hydroxyl Fluorine-Doped Silica Optical Fibers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kim, Youngwoong / Kim, Jongyeol / Ryu, Gukbeen / Jeong, Wookjin / Hwang, Younggwan / Moon, Dae Seung / Jung, Chang Hyun

We developed high-hydroxyl (OH) fluorine-doped silica optical fibers and evaluated their radiation response at 1550 nm under γ-ray irradiation. The developed fiber exhibits significantly reduced radiation-induced attenuation and improved saturation behavior compared with conventional radiation-hardened fibers, demonstrating synergistic benefits of combined fluorine and OH incorporation.

talks.title: Mo4-P-50: Complexity Reduction of SD-FEC by Bayes-Based Simple-Soft-Output MLSE in Coherent Transmission with Chase Decoder
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yamamoto, Shuto / Nakajima, Yukinobu / Taniuchi, Hiroki / Nakamura, Masanori / Yamazaki, Etsushi

We evaluate the applicability of Bayes-based simple-soft-output MLSE to coherent transmission systems with LR-FEC and turbo product codes. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme reduces the number of test patterns and the number of iterations in Chase decoding by approximately 50% and 25%, respectively.

talks.title: Mo4-P-51: 224 Gbaud On-Off Keying Optical Link Using O-Band Vertical P–N Junction Ring Resonator Modulator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Dan / Ostrovskis, Armands / Osadchuk, Yevhenii / Cirjulina, Darja / Salgals, Toms / Jiang, Tianyu / Da Ros, Francesco / Zibar, Darko / Kim, Minkyu / De Heyn, Peter / Zhang, Lu / Yu, Xianbin / Bobrovs, Vjaceslavs / Pang, Xiaodan / Ozolins, Oskars

An O-band vertical p–n junction ring resonator modulator-based IM/DD link is demonstrated using bi-LSTM equalization. We achieve 224 Gbaud OOK and 140 Gbaud PAM4 over 1 km single-mode fiber with BER below the 6.25% overhead HD-FEC threshold.

talks.title: Mo4-P-52: Joint Transmitter-Receiver Design for High-Baud-Rate IM/DD Transmission with Low-Resolution DAC over 20-km Hollow-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Yibin / Wang, Jingchuan / Wei, Zixian / Wu, Qi / Wang, Li / Li, Peng / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Zhong, Kangping / Lau, Alan Pak Tao / Lu, Chao / Yu, Changyuan

We propose a joint transmitter-side VF-DRE and receiver-side NWF and MLSE scheme for high-baud-rate IM/DD transmission with low-resolution DAC. 140-GBaud OOK with 2-bit DAC and 100-GBaud PAM4 with 3-bit DAC are experimentally demonstrated over 20-km hollow-core fiber.

talks.title: Mo4-P-53: Robust Pilot-Tone-Based Timing Recovery Scheme for Coherent Digital Subcarrier Multiplexing Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jin, Yongchao / Lin, Jiexing / Gong, Siyu / Xiang, Qian / Zhang, Qun / Cheng, Chen / Fan, LinSheng / Yang, Pengxi / Yang, Bang / Yang, Yanfu

A robust, high-precision, and fast-converging frequency-domain pilot-aided timing recovery scheme for DSCM systems is proposed. By dividing two pilot tones, the scheme achieves FO/PN immunity. Experiments show strong robustness to roll-off and SFO, ensuring stable operation up to 280-ppm SFO.

talks.title: Mo4-P-54: Low-Complexity FO-Tolerant Frame Synchronisation Using an Amplitude-Weighted Timing Metric and QAM-Based Training Sequence for Low-SNR Coherent Optical Inter-Satellite Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tateno, Shoma / Noguchi, Hidemi / Hosokawa, Kohei

We propose a high-sensitivity, low-complexity FO-tolerant frame synchronisation scheme for low-SNR coherent optical inter-satellite links based on an amplitude-modulated training sequence and a multiplication-free amplitude-weighted timing metric, reducing the required overhead length by 37.5% and the computational complexity by 36.3% compared to conventional schemes.

talks.title: Mo4-P-55: Self-Adaptive Silicon Photonic Equalizer for Polarization-Insensitive and Multi-Wavelength 200-Gbps O-Band Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yan, Guofeng / Wan, Yuanjian / Han, Bing / Wang, Ning / Yang, Xuefeng / Ma, Weidong / Wang, Jian

We demonstrate a self-adaptive silicon photonic equalizer for polarization-insensitive, multi-wavelength division O-band transmission. The equalizer simultaneously equalizes 2x50-Gbaud PAM4 signals transmitted in a WDM system, improving the received sensitivity about 4 dB.

talks.title: Mo4-P-56: High spatial resolution and large strain measurement in long-distance OFDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Qu, Shuai / Zhang, Xiaoying / Wu, Qi / Yan, Yaxi / Lau, Alan Pak Tao / Lu, Chao

We present a distance-domain gating method that simultaneously achieves long sensing distance, high spatial resolution and wide strain measurement range. Strain range of 8000με is achieved over a 54m fiber with a 1.9mm spatial resolution.

talks.title: Mo4-P-57: Nonlinear Distortion of Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers as a Source of Equalization Enhanced Phase Noise
talks.abstract:
Authors: Qiu, Meng / Gao, Ying / Tang, Xuefeng / Li, Chuandong

We demonstrate the interaction between nonlinear phase distortion induced by semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOA) and digital equalization via both simulations and experiments. Properties of the resulting equalization enhanced phase noise (EEPN) are also compared with the well-studied EEPN caused by laser phase noise.

talks.title: Mo4-P-58: 375 km, Unrepeatered Transmission Using a Erbium-Doped, Tellurite Fiber Based, 69 nm bandwidth, ROPA
talks.abstract:
Authors: Schneck, Julian / Luis, Ruben S. / Orsuti, Daniele / Gaiani, Stefano / Vogel, Wolfgang / Boffi, Pierpaolo / Rademacher, Georg / Furukawa, Hideaki

We use a 69 nm bandwidth ROPA based on an erbium-doped tellurite glass fiber, combined with bidirectional distributed Raman amplification, to transmit 333 x 24.5 Gbaud channels over 375 km with a minimum span loss of 56 dB, achieving a total throughput of 40.9 Tb/s.

talks.title: Mo4-P-59: Impact of Kerr Nonlinearity within High Power Optical Amplifiers on HCF Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vassilieva, Olga / Kim, Inwoong / Irie, Hiroyuki / Hoshida, Takeshi / Tanaka, Yu / Palacharla, Paparao

We quantify Kerr nonlinearity generated within C-band high-power EDFAs for long HCF links. We show that EDFA doped-fiber nonlinearity is the main contributor to system impairments, limiting allowable output power to below 32 dBm when the EDF length exceeds 10 m.

talks.title: Mo4-P-5: Virtual Draw of Arbitrary Geometry Hollow Core Fibres, a 3D Finite Element Approach
talks.abstract:
Authors: Najafigamasaei, Mohammadreza / Shakiba, Ali / Fatobene Ando, Ron / Poletti, Francesco / T. Jasion, Gregory

A novel 3D finite-element Computational Fluid Design tool is developed to study the fabrication of anti-resonant hollow-core fibres from preforms with arbitrary geometries. To showcase its unique capabilities, we study the draw of elliptical tubes and of hollow-core fibres with elliptical capillaries.

talks.title: Mo4-P-60: Characterization of Various Impairments in Coherent Optical Transmitters Using Spectrum Analyser Only
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Jingnan / Su, Xiaofei / Ye, Tong / Nakashima, Hisao / Hoshida, Takeshi / Aoki, Yasuhiko / Tao, Zhenning / Mori, Yojiro / Hasegawa, Hiroshi

Using probability-maintained multi-notch sequences and equally spaced multi-tone signals, various impairments in EDFA-embedded coherent transmitters including nonlinear distortion, additive electrical noise, and ASE noise are decoupled via spectrum-analyser-based measurements. The system's error vector magnitude is predicted with 0.4-dB accuracy based on the measured noise-to-signal ratio.

talks.title: Mo4-P-61: Cycle-Slip Resilient High-Precision Transmitter IQ Skew Estimation for Ultra-High Baud-Rate Digital Subcarrier Multiplexing Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Le, Huanyu / Xiang, Meng / Xiang, Junjiang / Zhou, Gai / Jiang, Hexun / Wang, Yongben / Wei, Shuai / Fu, Songnian / Qin, Yuwen

We propose a cycle-slip resilient high-precision transmitter IQ skew estimation scheme based on a designated training sequence. The 120-GBaud DP-16QAM digital subcarrier multiplexing (DSM) experimental transmission verifies its effective suppression of phase-extraction cycle slips, improving IQ skew estimation accuracy from 0.3 ps to below 0.1 ps.

talks.title: Mo4-P-62: In-Service Inter-Segment Skew Calibration Using a Built-in Low-Speed Coherent Detection Monitor
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ye, Tong / Su, Xiaofei / Li, Jingnan / Sobu, Yohei / Nakashima, Hisao / Hoshida, Takeshi / Aoki, Yasuhiko / Tao, Zhenning

We propose a power-efficient in-service skew calibration method for the transmitters with segmented modulators, utilizing a modulated local oscillator and low-speed coherent detection monitor. Experimental results demonstrate an accurate skew calibration with a maximum error within ±0.025 UI over a ±0.2 UI skew range.

talks.title: Mo4-P-63: On the Optimum Energy-per-bit Launch Power in Coherent Hollow-core Fibre Transmission Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sohanpal, Ronit / Sillekens, Eric / Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Killey, Robert / Bayvel, Polina

We investigate the optimum energy per bit in hollow-core-fibre transmission systems. We show that a 1000 km C-band link can achieve a 41.5% reduction in total power consumption when operating at the minimum energy-per-bit launch power with only 2.2% throughput penalty.

talks.title: Mo4-P-64: Driverless Net 3.2 Tbps (8×448 Gbps) PAM4 Transmission at 500m Using a Chirped Differential MZM DR8 PIC on TFLN
talks.abstract:
Authors: St-Arnault, Charles / Kita, Derek / Dickson, Ross / Beggs, Bruce / Ben-Hamida, Naim / Reimer, Christian / Plant, David

We report a novel ultra-compact chirped differential electrode layout on TFLN reducing VπL by 1.33x on a DR8 PIC enabling driverless 3.2 Tbps (8×448 Gbps) PAM4 with compliant TDECQ under the HD-FEC.

talks.title: Mo4-P-65: Link Diagnosis Enabled by Longitudinal Noise Monitoring
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hahn, Choloong / Guo, Qingyi / Chang, Junho / Jiang, Zhiping

We show that a longitudinal noise monitoring scheme utilizing coherent receiver DSP comprehensively monitors link health. By experimentally demonstrating dynamic SNR monitoring during channel-drop transients and the localization of abnormal noise increases, we establish an effective, spatially resolved diagnostic tool.

talks.title: Mo4-P-66: Longitudinal Power Monitoring in S+C+L Transmission with Forward and Backward Distributed Raman Amplification
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kaneko, Runa / Sasai, Takeo / Nakamura, Masanori / Kimura, Kosuke / Kawakami, Hiroto / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka / Yamazaki, Etsushi / Hamaoka, Fukutaro

We demonstrate longitudinal power monitoring in S+C+L transmission with bidirectional distributed Raman amplification (DRA) for the first time. Measurements over five 80-km spans spatially resolve the effects of DRA and inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS) on power evolution, revealing spatial features inaccessible to end-to-end monitoring.

talks.title: Mo4-P-67: KZ-Based Spectral Modeling of Nonlinear Interference with Data-Driven PSD Estimation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rahbarfam, Saber / Kschischang, Frank R.

Accurate modeling of nonlinear interference in optical fiber systems is investigated using Kolmogorov–Zakharov modeling and learning-based PSD estimation. KZ outperforms GN in accuracy and effective complexity. A linear regression model maps spectra to NLI PSD, enabling improved performance prediction in practical systems.

talks.title: Mo4-P-68: Real-Time MDM Transmission Trial Using 800G OTN Transceivers over Field-Deployed FMF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Long, Chengbin / Qiao, Gang / Yang, Yu / Ji, Tonghui / Liu, Lulu / Feng, Lipeng / Zhang, Anxu / Ji, Honglin / Wang, Shangcheng / Xu, Zhaopeng / Gao, Yuyang / Yu, Jinyi / Shen, Lei / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Zhang, Xu / He, Zhixue / He, Yongqi / Chen, Zhangyuan / Li, Hongbin / Hu, Weisheng / Yu, Shaohua / Li, Juhao

Through effective suppression of modal crosstalk including adopting bidirectional transmission and only selecting LP01 and LP02 modes as active channels, we demonstrate real-time MDM-WDM transmission over 80-km field-deployed FMF using commercial 800G DP-16QAM OTN transceivers.

talks.title: Mo4-P-69: Power Consumption Analysis of Terrestrial Systems with the Same Fiber Capacity
talks.abstract:
Authors: Downie, John / Ivanov, Viacheslav / Galdino, Lidia / Wallace, Colin

We analyze the relative power consumption of terrestrial long-haul systems constructed with different fiber types and optimized span lengths producing the same cable capacity. Advanced fibers with C-band amplifiers have the lowest power consumption and carbon footprint, saving up to 40% over conventional fiber.

talks.title: Mo4-P-6: Discrete-Raman-Amplification in the U+X-Band (1610-1690nm) Utilizing Twin EDFA ASE Peaks (1535nm and 1565nm) for Forward Pumping with Reduced Noise Generation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Akasaka, Youichi / Kim, Inwoong / Palacharla, Paparao

U+X band discrete Raman amplification covering 1610nm to 1690nm is demonstrated using twin peaks of C-band EDFA ASE at 1535nm and 1565nm, made by 4m EDF and 13m EDF, respectively. Forward pumping with incoherent ASE achieved a 1dB Lower noise compared to backward pumping.

talks.title: Mo4-P-70: Hollow-Core and Standard Single-Mode Fiber Hybrid Optical Networks: A Multi-Topology Investigation of Protection Switching
talks.abstract:
Authors: Saber, Md Ghulam / Jiang, Zhiping

We study cross-fiber protection switching in hybrid hollow-core and single-mode networks. At 50% deployment, CD steps reach 4,000-22,000 ps/nm with 1.6-3.1 dB penalties, causing 38-59% modulation downgrades. CO2-absorption degrades 9-26 of 64 L-band channels. Higher HCF fractions generally reduce all impairments across six network topologies.

talks.title: Mo4-P-71: SRS-Immune Fiber Attenuation Monitoring via Full-Band Power Aggregation in C+L Band Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yu, Chuxuan / Chen, Minggang / Liu, Lei / Li, Fangchao / Wang, Yu / He, Zekun / Wang, Yachen / Zou, Xianneng

We propose a full-band power aggregation method for real-time fiber attenuation monitoring in C+L band systems to overcome stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) interference in single-channel monitoring. Validation on 237 production spans reduces the false alarm rate from 24.9% to 0% at a 3.5dB attenuation variation.

talks.title: Mo4-P-72: Time-Error-Constrained Bidirectional Provisioning for Synchronization Services in Dynamic Elastic Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Haojie / Wang, Yixin / Zhao, Yongli / Zhang, Jie

Bidirectional slot mismatch in dynamic EONs induces chromatic-dispersion time errors that can invalidate synchronization services. We derive a path-dependent reverse-slot admissibility bound for bidirectional provisioning. On COST239, it lowers blocking versus timing-unaware and strict same-slot baselines while keeping admitted synchronization services within a 3-ns budget.

talks.title: Mo4-P-73: Inter-Port Crosstalk Reduction in Single Multi-Input-Port WSS-Based ROADM Architectures Using Interleaved Port Allocation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jinno, Masahiko / Sasaki, Ryunosuke / Rashdan, Emre Maleeq Bin Mohd / Miyamura, Takashi / Okamoto, Satoru / Yamanaka, Naoaki

We analyse joint-switching-induced inter-port crosstalk (XT) in single multi-input-port WSS-based ROADM architectures. We propose an interleaved port allocation scheme that suppresses XT without additional hardware and validate it experimentally, demonstrating considerable XT reduc-tion while preserving the simplicity and cost advantages of the single-WSS architecture.

talks.title: Mo4-P-74: Benchmarking of Switching Technologies under Various Traffic Distributions in Pan-European and US WDM Core Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zami, Thierry / Khan, Ihtesham / Simsarian, Jesse

We review the conditions of network topology and traffic distribution under which pure fiber switching can accommodate a total capacity close to wavelength switching for a North American and a Pan-European WDM networks

talks.title: Mo4-P-75: Impact of Statistical LCoS-induced PDL in WDM Networks Equipped with Multirail Amplifiers and 800ZR+ Interfaces
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rossi, Nicola / Zami, Thierry / Lavigne, Bruno
