This study quantifies the benefit on both the OSNR penalty and the network capacity of accounting realistically statistical PDL insertions vs. fixed reasonable worst-case values in the context of modern optical networks equipped with multirail amplifiers featuring integrated spectral equalizers

talks.title: Mo4-P-76: SMART Optical Network Integrating PTMP Sensing, 10×1-Tb/s Metro Superchannel, and Fixed-Mobile Access
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Yixiao / Zhang, Chenbo / Cai, Xiang / Zou, Yi / Pan, Yutong / Zhang, Tianhong / Li, Jingchi / Xie, Xiaopeng / Zhang, Fan / Hu, Weisheng

We present SMART (Sensing-Metro-Access-RoF-Transport) optical network integrating, for the first time, point-to-multipoint multi-event forward sensing with sub-28-m resolution, 10×1-Tb/s metro superchannel, co-wavelength access of super-rated 200G coherent PON with 35-dB power budget (ITU-T E2-class) and 1.05-Tb/s CPRI-equivalent rate 16384-QAM RoF.

talks.title: Mo4-P-77: CATS: Constraint-Aware Topology Scheduling Mechanism for Efficient LLM Training in O/E Hybrid Switching Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gao, Liang / Hu, Yakun / Shen, Shikui / Han, Bowen / Pan, Jiameng / Chen, Wei / Li, Wenzhe / Wang, Zelin / Guo, Bingli / Liao, Siyi / Tang, Xiongyan / Huang, Shanguo / Xue, Xuwei

We propose Constraint-Aware Topology Scheduling (CATS) mechanism to overcome the indiscriminate scheduling exclusively based on traffic volume in O/E hybrid networks. CATS strategically offloads the constraint-induced traffic to the contention-free, zero-jitter optical paths, accelerating LLM training average time by 0.49%–9.16% and boosting TFLOPS by 0.61%–9.12%

talks.title: Mo4-P-78: Distributed LLM Training over Passive Optical Networks: Performance Impact of Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xu, Xiaonan / Chen, Haoshuo / Bidkar, Sarvesh / Vijayan, Kovendhan / Borkowski, Robert / Ryf, Roland / Simsarian, Jesse / Fontaine, Nicolas / Mazur, Mikael / Dallachiesa, Lauren / Neilson, David

We implement data-parallel LLM training on a two-node 25GS-PON testbed and evaluate AllReduce performance under varying delay tolerance and bandwidth configurations. Results show that higher delay tolerance increases communication latency, demonstrating that properly configured PONs can feasibly support small- and medium-scale distributed training workloads.

talks.title: Mo4-P-79: Mixed DD and Coherent Receivers for VHSP using Digital CD Pre-Compensated PAM-2
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pilori, Dario / Kharbich, Hanane / Bosco, Gabriella / Rizzelli, Giuseppe / Ferrero, Valter / Talli, Giuseppe / Cano, Ivan / Gaudino, Roberto

In the ongoing research towards next-generation Very High Speed PON, we propose and experimentally investigate the combination of Digital Chromatic Dispersion Pre-Compensation (DCPC) PAM-2 transmission with coexisting mixed receivers: DD for PON up to 20km and coherent detection for extended reach up to 40+km.

talks.title: Mo4-P-7: Refractive-index profile dependence of an LPFG-based mode scrambler for broadband and low-loss MDL compensation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Iwaya, Taro / Wada, Masaki / Sakamoto, Taiji / Matsui, Takashi / Sato, Takanori / Saitoh, Kunimasa / Nakajima, Kazuhide

A dual-step-index (DSI) core reduces the insertion loss increase associated with mode-coupling efficiency for LPFG-type 2-LP mode scramblers. An LPFG-based mode-scrambler utilizing DSI-core fibre was numerically and experimentally demonstrated, achieving < 0.5 dB insertion loss and broadband mode-dependent-loss compensation over the C+L band.

talks.title: Mo4-P-80: An Integrated 150 Gb/s NRZ Heterodyne Detection RX Supporting 20km SMF with Simple FFE for VHSP PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Cheng / Coudyzer, Gertjan / Gu, Ye / Niu, Shengpu / Zhang, Jing / Yin, Xin

An integrated NRZ modulation heterodyne detection RX is demonstrated for VHSP PON. Analog signal processing for chromatic dispersion suppression and demodulation is implemented. 150Gb/s NRZ is detected with -22(B2B)/-16dBm(20km SMF) OMA at 1320/1295nm, using 0.5 dBm LO and
7/11-tap FFE.

talks.title: Mo4-P-81: Receiver-Informed Transmitter for 200Gbps C-Band Direct-Detection PON With FFE-Free ONU
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dabwan, Safiya / Gomes, Geraldo / Sygletos, Stylianos

We introduce and numerically demonstrate receiver-informed transmitter (RITX) waveform design for 200 Gb/s PAM-4 C-band direct-detection PON. Using 50 GHz optoelectronics, RITX achieves N1/E1 loss classes with FFE-Free ONU, enabling 40 km reach and 48.1%/66.7% network-wide complexity savings at 1:64/1:128 splits.

talks.title: Mo4-P-82: Passive Optical Networks Systems with Co-Propagating Distributed Acoustic Sensing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Simon, Gael / Potet, Jérémy / Saliou, Fabienne / Chanclou, Philippe / Bideau, Maël / Gavrilovic, Remi / Harisson, Robert Clayton / Sleiman, Bachir / Chedid, Alex / Calbris, Gaetan

We study the impact of distributed acoustic sensing on PONs. We show that wavelength isolation is required, and how Raman scattering can impact the downstream G-PON. We also provide guiding rules to mitigate DAS impact on PONs.

talks.title: Mo4-P-83: Wi-Fi Transmission Over In-building FTTR Networks Using Sigma-Delta Modulation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Thiele, Sophie / Bluemm, Christian / Calabrò, Stefano / Pachnicke, Stephan

Sigma-delta, unlike analog radio over fiber, enables robust Wi-Fi FTTR transmission with standard SFP+ modules not optimized for linear drive. Furthermore, a 27.5% reduction in required optical bandwidth is achieved for a 160 MHz 256‑QAM signal by reducing the oversampling rate through amplitude clipping.

talks.title: Mo4-P-84: Multipath Interference Mitigation Based on Low-Complexity Adaptive High-Pass Filtering in Data Centre IM/DD Systems with OCS
talks.abstract:
Authors: Parajuli, H. N. / Ji, Tonghui / Wang, Xinping / Deng, Ning / Shen, Shikui / Xu, Jing

We propose a low-complexity MPI mitigation scheme using adaptive high-pass filtering for data centre IM/DD systems. Experimental results demonstrate 4 dB improvement in SIR tolerance and 3.5 dB receiver sensitivity gain at HD-FEC threshold for a 56.88 Gbps PAM-4 signal in an OCS-integrated IM/DD link.

talks.title: Mo4-P-85: First Demonstration of Novel Combo-ONUs for Cost-Effective Evolution from XGS-PON to 50G-PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Luo, Yuanqiu / Wang, Ning / Li, Junwei / Effenberger, Frank / Liu, Dekun / Zhang, Dechao

We demonstrate the first 50G/XGS Combo-ONU deployment for PON evolution. It integrates XGS-PON and 50G-PON links. The business modeling and field trial results demonstrate reduced migration cost, operational flexibility, and enhanced system features for operators.

talks.title: Mo4-P-86: Experimental Evaluation of PAM2-SSB and PAM2-SSB+DCPC for a 2×100Gb/s/λ Very High Speed PON Downstream
talks.abstract:
Authors: Andrenacci, Lorenzo / Caruso, Giuseppe / Kharbich, Hanane / Rizzelli, Giuseppe / Cano, Ivan / Ferrero, Valter / Talli, Giuseppe / Bosco, Gabriella / Gaudino, Roberto

We experimentally demonstrate a digitally-generated PAM2-SSB modulation with direct-detection receiver. The results show that, even with limited DSP complexity, the CD tolerance can be enhanced to ensure coexistence with previous PON technologies while still supporting Class N1 power-budget. Further improvement is obtained by adding DCPC.

talks.title: Mo4-P-87: 400 Gbit/s IM/DD PON with >30 dB Power Budget Enabled by Quantum-Dot SOA Amplified Remote Node
talks.abstract:
Authors: Reza, Ahmed Galib / Rautert, Janina / Mikhrin, Vladimir S. / Gubenko, Alexey / Barry, Liam P.

We demonstrate 4×100 Gbit/s NRZ-OOK transmissions with 200 GHz channel spacing for next-generation 400G PON. By employing an InAs/GaAs quantum-dot SOA-amplified remote node, we achieve an optical power budget beyond N1 class after 20 km at the HD-LDPC BER limit, using a T-spaced FFE.

talks.title: Mo4-P-88: Environmental Sensing on XGS-PON OLT Using Upstream Burst Window Alignment
talks.abstract:
Authors: Montalvo, Julio / Borkowski, Robert / Das, Sandip / Cortés, Daniel / Vidal, Borja

We demonstrate PON integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for fiber ambient temperature estimation and continuous monitoring. Using operational XGS‑PON we measure change in fiber RTT at OLT using burst-mode upstream alignment. Experimental results in a climatic chamber show 0.63°C temperature RMS error over 4-km-long fiber.

talks.title: Mo4-P-89: Low-Tech SOP Sensing over FTTH for Seismic Monitoring in Campi Flegrei: Benchmarking Against Interferometry and φ-OTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Virgillito, Emanuele / Notarstefano, Federico / Herrero, André / Currenti, Gilda / Bianco, Francesca / Corsaro, Miriana / Prestifilippo, Michele / Bratovich, Rudi / Corsini, Raffaele / Donadello, Simone / Clivati, Cecilia / Di Lena, Francesco / Calonico, Davide / Hovsepyan, Marianna / Carpentieri, Francesco / Curri, Vittorio

We demonstrate, for the first time, PBS-based low-tech SOP sensing for seamless seismic monitoring using in-service FTTH infrastructure in the highly seismic area of Campi Flegrei. The approach detects earthquakes down to magnitude 1.9 and is positively benchmarked against consolidated interferometric phase and φ-OTDR techniques.

talks.title: Mo4-P-8: High-Density Cable Employing 160 μm Reduced-Cladding 4-Core Multi-Core Fibre for Data Centre Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Takehana, Hiroki / Kaji, Ryota / Kajikawa, Shota / Takenaga, Katsuhiro / Oda, Takuya / Yamashita, Noriaki / Sato, Hironori / Tsujimoto, Yusuke / Ichii, Kentaro

A high-density 288-fibre cable was fabricated employing reduced-cladding 100/160 μm, 4-core, multi-core fibres (MCFs) for intra-/inter-data centre links (lengths <10 km). The cable suppressed the microbending loss and maintained practical crosstalk and temperature stability levels, demonstrating the feasibility of reduced-cladding MCF cabling for practical deployment.

talks.title: Mo4-P-90: 252 Gbit/s, Polarization-multiplexed 128 QAM Fully Coherent Transmission over 10 km SMF and 40 m Wirelessly at 125 GHz
talks.abstract:
Authors: Joichi, Tomoki / Watanabe, Arata / Sakuma, Yusei / Kasai, Keisuke / Hirooka, Toshihiko / Yoshida, Masato / Nakazawa, Masataka

We report a 252-Gbit/s polarization-division-multiplexed (PDM) fully coherent transmission in the 125 GHz band. By employing frequency-domain-equalization that compensates for both imperfect frequency responses and IQ imbalance, PDM 18 Gbaud 128 QAM signals are successfully transmitted over a 10 km SMF and 40 m wirelessly.

talks.title: Mo4-P-91: Cost-Effective 50-km DAS Using a 200-kHz-Linewidth ECL with FDM Dual-Pulse Phase Noise Compensation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cheng, Jingchi / Qian, Zichen / Zhao, Can / Yang, Zhihuai / Jiang, Jing / Sun, Quan / Shang, Tao / Tang, Ming

We demonstrate a cost-effective 50-km DAS resilient to phase noise and fading. Leveraging a frequency-division-multiplexed dual-pulse delay-beat scheme, we achieve a strain sensitivity of 234 pε/√HzpεHz using a 200-kHz-linewidth ECL, and the performance using a 10-kHz-linewidth ECL is comparable to that of a 100-Hz-linewidth NLL.

talks.title: Mo4-P-92: Detection, Localization and Tracking of Underwater Acoustic Sources via A Passive Fiber Optic Hydrophone Array
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ozharar, Sarper / Li, Yaowen / Tian, Yue / Ding, Yangmin / Wang, Ting

A fiber optic hydrophone array comprising four passive fiber mandrels, interrogated by a distributed acoustic sensing system was deployed in a lake for field testing. Several stationary and moving underwater acoustic sources were localized, continuously tracked, and their acoustic signals were enhanced by beamforming techniques.

talks.title: Mo4-P-93: Comparison of Sigma-Delta-Over-Fiber and Analog Radio-Over-Fiber mm-wave Links With Optical Up-Conversion
talks.abstract:
Authors: Olofsson, Frida / Lim, Christina / Lee, Ka-Lun / Karlsson, Magnus / Aabel, Lise / Fager, Christian

Radio-over-fiber with central frequency up-conversion is promising for phase-coherent D-MIMO transmission, but extension to mm-wave requires impractically high sampling rates. We employ optical up-conversion to relax this constraint and compare ARoF and SDoF, showing SDoF performs better below 300 MBd.

talks.title: Mo4-P-94: Breaking the Manual Alignment Barrier: First Demonstration of an Automatically Aligned Kilometer-Scale 100-Gb/s Photonic THz Wireless Link in 300-GHz Band
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sung, Minkyu / Moon, Sang-Rok / Kim, Sooyeon / Cho, Sungmin / Kim, Seung-Hwan / Park, Heuk / Lee, Joon Ki / Cho, Seung-Hyun

We demonstrate the first automatically aligned km-scale 100-Gb/s photonic THz wireless link under realistic rooftop-to-rooftop deployment conditions. Sensor-assisted coarse acquisition and power feedback fine alignment achieve 25-GBaud 16-QAM transmission over a 1.1-km line-of-sight path at 300 GHz with a BER of 1.5×10-2.

talks.title: Mo4-P-95: Low-Penalty Joint Communication and Acoustic Sensing using P43 Polyphase Code
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rai, Vishal Chandraprakash / Sandmann, André / Azendorf, Florian / Schmauss, Bernhard

Polyphase coding is investigated for distributed acoustic sensing in joint communication-sensing systems. A P43 code is evaluated using CC-OTDR and compared to linear frequency-modulated probes. Experiments demonstrate an additional 17.4 dB crosstalk suppression, while inducing only a 0.09 dB OSNR penalty on co-propagating DP-16QAM signals.

talks.title: Mo4-P-96: Joint High-Speed Communications, Safety Power Delivery and Temperature Sensing over Multicore Fibers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Barco Alvárez, Javier / Vázquez, Carmen

We report the first measurement of temperature variations induced by PoF using FBGs. Tests on a 7-core MCF with 25.67 Gbps 5G-NR ARoF and 25 Gbps NRZ transmission, delivering 360 mW at 2km, show that 2W PoF increases core temperature by 16 ±1 ºC

talks.title: Mo4-P-97: Field Trial of Distributed Acoustic Fiber and 6G Radio Sensing Fusion for Enhanced Localization Accuracy in an Industrial Environment
talks.abstract:
Authors: Straub, Michael / Das, Sandip / Grudnitsky, Artjom / Fuchs, Rolf / Palhares, Victoria / Guerrier, Sterenn

We propose, analyse, and experimentally verify the effectiveness of combining radio and optical sensing for enhanced localization accuracy. First use cases to jointly sense within an industrial environment were demonstrated and analysed during a Field Trial at the research campus of Arena2026 in Stuttgart, Germany.

talks.title: Mo4-P-98: RF Interference Suppression with Synthesis of Field-Programmable Microwave Photonic Filters Based on Hexagonal Meshes
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Can / Deng, Qiuzhuo / Chen, Guanyu / Cao, Yuheng / Vidal, Borja / Pang, Xiaodan / Lin, Hongtao / Zhang, Lu / Yu, Xianbin

We demonstrate the synthesis of a field-programmable microwave photonic filter (MPF) on a 5×5 hexagonal mesh for RF interference suppression. Strong anti-interference ability of the synthesized integrated MPF architecture is validated with a 4 Gbps QPSK RF signal, achieving an EVM improvement of >40%.

talks.title: Mo4-P-99: External Modulation of an RF Signal Enhanced by Mutual Optical Injection Locking
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rama, Leonardo / Rodrigues, Carla / Santos, João / Vaz, Diogo / Rodrigues, Francisco / Varum, Tiago / Nogueira, Rogério / Drummond, Miguel / Teixeira, António

We demonstrate a novel external modulation scheme that increases the modulation efficiency for RF signals. It uses an EAM placed between two mutually injection-locked DFB lasers. Driving the EAM at the relaxation frequency of DFB lasers provides a modulation gain of 14 dB.

talks.title: Mo4-P-9: Core-Pitch Conversion Technique for Randomly Coupled Multi-Core Fibre Links by Cladding Mode Coupling
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kikuchi, Kazuhiro / Imada, Ryota / Sakamoto, Taiji / Matsui, Takashi / Nakajima, Kazuhide

We propose a core-pitch conversion technique using only a simple spliced-taper structure of randomly coupled multi-core fibres (RC-MCF). We demonstrate up to 20-µm core-pitch conversion with loss below 0.9 dB and low mode-dependent loss, which can connect RC-MCF transmission line and smaller-core-pitch amplifier.

sessions.title: Mo5-A Distributed optical sensing: from physics to network deployment
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: Mo5-A1: Distributed Optical Fibre Sensing: Where Elegant Physics Gives Rise to Smart Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Thévenaz, Luc

Distributed optical fibre sensing exploits Rayleigh, Brillouin and Raman scattering in silica fibres to measure physical quantities such as temperature and strain with spatial resolution. Each scattering mechanism offers distinct advantages and trade-offs. Operating principles, performance limits, and future prospects, notably hollow-core fibres, are reviewed.

talks.title: Mo5-A2: Rayleigh Fingerprint-Based DAS over a 688-km Repeatered Link with Co-Propagating 15-Tb/s WDM Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Orsuti, Daniele / Palmieri, Luca / S. Luís, Ruben / A. Colares, Robson / Sakaguchi, Jun / Cappelletti, Martina / Schenato, Luca / Santagiustina, Marco / A. A. Mello, Darli / Galtarossa, Andrea / Furukawa, Hideaki

We report the first demonstration of distributed acoustic sensing based on cross-correlation of the fiber’s Rayleigh fingerprint over >600 km using 500-MHz bandwidth pulses. The link includes 90 km of field fiber for seismic monitoring.

talks.title: Mo5-A3: Performance of L-band DAS on Live Traffic Fiber Compared to C-band DAS Over Dark Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bozorgebrahimi, Kurosh / Brenne, Jan Kristoffer

We present field-trial results with L-band DAS deployed in coexistence with C-band DWDM channels carrying live production traffic. We monitored the quality of DAS and optical communication channels during the test and uncompromised performance was achieved for both compared to sensing on dedicated dark fiber.

sessions.title: Mo5-B Hollow-core fibre design
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: Mo5-B1: Hollow Core Fibres: From Visionary Concept to Multi Problem Solution
talks.abstract:
Authors: Poletti, Francesco

Hollow-core fibres have evolved from early photonic bandgap concepts to modern antireso-nant nested designs, overcoming loss, bandwidth, and scalability challenges. Here we briefly trace this progress, highlighting recent DNANF advances achieving sub-silica loss, long spans, and multi-band operation

talks.title: Mo5-B2: A Unified Framework for Understanding Confinement Loss, and Engineering Bandwidth, and Modal-Dependent Loss in Hollow-Core Fibers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Melli, Federico / Trivigno, Daniela / Rosa, Lorenzo / Benabid, Fetah / Cucinotta, Annamaria / Vincetti, Luca

Exploiting a unified framework linking mode-coupling and tube-tunneling losses in Hollow-Core Inhibited-Coupling Fibers, we show how tube shape and position govern transmission bandwidth and anisotropic leakage, revealing Mode-Dependent loss in HC-IC fibers as a controllable outcome of geometric and azimuthal design choices

talks.title: Mo5-B3: Ultra-high Mode Purity and SMF-matched O-Band Hybrid Antiresonant Hollow Core Fiber for Intra Data Center Connection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dong, Zihan / Li, Peng / Chu, Jun / Dai, Lu / Li, Hongmin / Xu, Yifei / Chen, Guoqun / Jia, Anqing / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie

We report the first demonstration of an O-band hybrid antiresonant hollow core fiber with ~ 6000 dB/km LP₁₁ mode loss and 14/240 μm core/coating diameters. Meanwhile, this fiber delivers macrobending loss comparable to G.657.A2, rendering it well suited for high-density IDC interconnections.

talks.title: Mo5-B4: Active Antiresonant Hollow-Core Fibres Enabled by Internal Semiconductor Quantum-Dot Coatings
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nagamine, Gabriel / Rechcinska, Katarzyna / Hänzi, Pascal / Winkowski, Mateusz / Alhadi, Fatima / Giorgianni, Flavio / Stacewicz, Tadeusz / Buczynski, Ryszard / Hahm, Donghyo / Klimov, Victor / Heidt, Alexander

We demonstrate an active antiresonant hollow-core fibre with optical gain provided by thin internal semiconductor quantum-dot coatings. In a side-pumped all-fibre cavity, it shows 625-nm laser emission while preserving air-core guidance and eliminating the need for liquid or gas-based gain media.

sessions.title: Mo5-D Integrated quantum photonics (II)
sessions.track: SC 12: CLEO® Special Session on Emerging Trends in Optics and Photonics

talks.title: Mo5-D1 Photonic integrated circuits on soi and sin for quantum communications and quantum computing
Mo5-D2: Quantum and Classical Photonics for Advanced Smart Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bongiovanni, Domenico / Di Lauro, Luigi / Wang, Xutong / Shamim, Hosne / Yu, Hao / Alamgir, Imtiaz / Mazoukh, Celine / Liu, Yang / Perron, Nicolas / Dmitriev, Pavel / Mahadi, Masnad Md. / Monika, Monika / Little, Brent E. / Wang, Zhiming / Peschel, Ulf / Chu, Sai T. / azaña, José / Moss, David J. / Morandotti, Roberto

We report fiber-based and integrated photonic platforms that use time and frequency control to address scalable quantum communication and classical information processing. Through high-dimensional entanglement, ultrafast time-bin encoding, reservoir computing, spectral machine learning, and microcomb optimization, we demonstrate scalable telecom-compatible architectures for next-generation smart applications.

talks.title: Mo5-D3: III-V nanostructures for lasers and quantum emitters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tan, Hark Hoe

Selective area epitaxy is used to grow III-V semiconductor nanostructures – ranging from nanowires to nanosheets to microrings. The nanostructures are then used for various light emitting applications

sessions.title: Mo5-E Packaging and dense integration
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: Mo5-E1: Ultra-broadband, Ultra-Dense 2D-Array Optical I/O Interface Enabled by 3D Nanoprinting
talks.abstract:
Authors: Huang, Huiyu / Shi, Zhitian / Yao, Chunhui / Penty, Richard / Cheng, Qixiang

We demonstrate a 3D-nanoprinted high-efficiency, ultra-dense 2D-array optical I/O interface for photonic packaging, integrating 16 channels within 160×120μm². Experiments show stable 1–2dB channel losses, with rigorous simulations indicating a potential reduction to 0.4dB.

talks.title: Mo5-E2: Laser-Induced Forward Transfer of Photonic Integrated Circuits
talks.abstract:
Authors: De Louw, Nick / Arutinov, Gari / Abdou, Aly / Gelinck, Gerwin / Giesbers, Merijn / Roso Casares, Sergio / Karki, Akchheta / Fledderus, Henri / Ollearo, Riccardo

We present laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) as a novel die-to-wafer assembly approach for photonic integrated circuits (PICs). Placement accuracies approaching 500 nm (3σ) are achieved, alongside efficient electro-optical coupling, underscoring LIFT’s promise for high-throughput, high-precision PIC integration.

talks.title: Mo5-E3: Fully Interconnected Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Copper Bonding Process for Opto-Electrical Routing Platforms
talks.abstract:
Authors: Song, Da In / Min, Byung-Ju / Cha, JungHo / Ahn, Seok-Geun / Park, Sungbong / Kwon, Shin / Kim, Yong-Jae / Shin, Kwangil / Huh, Woong / Lee, Hyunjin / Hwang, Jaewon / Yoo, Dong Su / Lee, Yunseo / Kim, Han-Hyoung / Seo, Jihyun / Kim, Hyerin / Chung, Jongmin / Jung, Hyun-Chul / Jun, Kimin

We demonstrate simultaneous opto-electrical interconnection on a die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system. CMP erosion is < 100 A Å even with pattern density mismatch between optic and electric layers. Measured evanescent coupler loss is 0.32 dB at 1310 nm and measured electrical resistance is 0.30 Ω.

talks.title: Mo5-E4: Ultra-High-Resolution Silicon Photonic Beamformer via Path-Reversal Optical True-Time Delay
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Senyu / Chong, Yifei / Luo, Wei / Li, Yunlong / Zheng, Shuang / Zhang, Minming

We demonstrate a silicon photonic beamformer employing a path-reversal optical true-time delay mechanism, increasing squint-free pointing angles in switched M-bit architectures from 2M to 2M+1-1 without additional delay stages. Our 5-bit chip achieves 63 angles over 35 GHz with <0.5 ps delay error.

talks.title: Mo5-E5: Double-Layer Metasurface-based Interface for Dense PIC-to-MCF Polarization-Multiplexed Coupling
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tsubai, Yusuke / Ren, Chun / Suganuma, Takahiro / Soma, Go / Ishimura, Shota / Elfiqi, Abdulaziz E. / Takahashi, Hidenori / Tsuritani, Takehiro / Tanemura, Takuo

Efficient and compact edge-coupling interface between SiN photonic integrated circuit (PIC) and multicore fiber (MCF) is demonstrated using a double-layer metasurface device. The PIC-to-MCF coupling losses below 1.4 dB (numerically) and 4.9 dB (experimentally) with polarization-multiplexing functionality are obtained for all eight channels.

talks.title: Mo5-E6: Hybrid Photonic Integrated O-band PLC with SiN SSC and SOA Array Switches for Lossless Wavelength Selective Switching
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tesfa, Amare Kindu / Rombouts, Marijn / Shi, Zhaolong / Zheng, Boyang / Xia, Shiyi / Calabretta, Nicola

We demonstrate O-band lossless wavelength-selective switch using hybrid photonic-integrated U-shaped InP-SOA arrays and silica PLC AWGs with integrated SiN spot-size converters. Results show efficient coupling <1.5dB/facet, 12dB net-gain and WDM 100G/λ PAM4 switching with >46dB on-off ratio and <0.52dB power penalties at KP4.

sessions.title: Mo5-F ML and nonlinearity mitigation
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: Mo5-F1: Unsupervised-Domain-Adaptation Enhanced Learned Subband-based Perturbation Nonlinear Compensation for Optical Transmission Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tang, Xuan / Guo, Wanzhen / Deng, Hao / Zhao, Jian

We propose a learned subband-based perturbation-aided nonlinear compensation method, enhanced by unsupervised domain adaptation using polarization- and phase-agnostic power moments. Experiments of PS-64QAM signals over 1200 km demonstrate that this method is robust to parameter mismatch and can adapt to channel variations quickly and blindly.

talks.title: Mo5-F2: A Realistic Implementation of Fast Convergence Hypernetwork-based DSP for Coherent Data Centre Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lennard, Samuel / Barbosa, Fabio Aparecido / Marques Ferreira, Filipe

We experimentally demonstrate a hypernetwork-based algorithm to generate the weights of an adaptive equalizer in 30-GBaud DP-16-QAM coherent transmission. It achieves better performance than conventional algorithms, providing purely feed-forward coherent DSP and locking to unseen channels with comparable computational complexity but without feedback paths.

talks.title: Mo5-F3: Sequential Neural Probabilistic Amplitude Shaping: Learning the Channel’s Language
talks.abstract:
Authors: Askari, Mohammad Taha / Lampe, Lutz / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein

We present the first neural probabilistic amplitude shaping that outperforms existing methods while accounting for all implementation losses, using a block‑less, easily implementable sequential autoregressive encoder compatible with arithmetic distribution matching, yielding reduced rate loss and higher achievable information rates.

talks.title: Mo5-F4: DPD-KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Low Complexity Digital Predistortion in 5G Analog Radio-over-Fiber Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Khalid, Bilal / Cavaliere, Fabio / Giorgi, Luca / freire, Pedro / Turitsyn, Sergei K. / Prilepsky, Jaroslaw E.

We demonstrate the first KAN-based DPD model for 5G analog RoF fronthaul link, achieving a 24.2% lower EVM than multi-layer perceptron and 29.6% lower than Volterra-based GMP at equivalent Bit Operations. To attain an EVM below 2%, KAN requires ≈52% fewer BOPs than a perceptron.

talks.title: Mo5-F5: 168-GBd PCS-324QAM Signal Transmission with 2.1-Tb/s Net Bitrate Using Sample-Domain Volterra Nonlinear Pre-distortion
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nakamura, Masanori / Hamaoka, Fukutaro / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Yamazaki, Etsushi

We demonstrate 168-GBd PCS-324QAM signal generation and transmission using sample-domain Volterra nonlinear pre-distortion applied to the oversampled high-PAPR waveform. Our approach provides a 0.7-dB peak-SNR gain over a symbol-domain Volterra filter and achieves net bitrates of 2.18 Tb/s back-to-back and 2.10 Tb/s after 80-km transmission.

talks.title: Mo5-F6: Physics-Aware Contribution-Guided Pruning for Low-Complexity Sparse Volterra Equalization in 100-Gb/s IM/DD PAM4 Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yadav, Govind Sharan / Wang, Cheng-Chieh / feng, Kai-Ming

We experimentally demonstrate a novel physics-aware, contribution-guided pruned Volterra equalization framework for distortion mitigation in a 100-Gb/s PAM4 IM/DD link over 4.2-km SMF, achieving ~92% complexity reduction versus full VE and ~36.5% reduction relative to baseline MP-VE, while delivering superior performance at the KP4-FEC limit.

sessions.title: Mo5-G Very high speed PON
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: Mo5-G1: Low-Complexity VSB Generation and Chirp Management for VHSP Downstream Links Supporting GPON Coexistence
talks.abstract:
Authors: Füllner, Christoph / Breyne, Laurens / Lanneer, Wouter / Bonk, René

We propose a novel hybrid PON concept at 100 Gb/s combining vestigial sideband (VSB) generation with an easy-to-implement transmitter chirp management to enable GPON coexistence of VHSP. We show that dispersion levels from 0 to 125 ps/nm can be covered.

talks.title: Mo5-G2: On the Extinction Ratio penalty and Sensitivity of next-generation 120 Gb/s upstream IM solutions for Very High-Speed PONs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Houtsma, Vincent / Vijayan, Kovendhan / Breyne, Laurens / Borkowski, Robert / Van Veen, Doutje

The sensitivity and impact of extinction ratio on proposed IM upstream solutions for next generation 100-120 Gb/s VHSP is investigated

talks.title: Mo5-G3: Investigation of MPI and DGD Tolerance in Digitally CD Pre-Compensated PAM-2 for Very High Speed PON Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kharbich, Hanane / Bosco, Gabriella / Rizzelli, Giuseppe / Pilori, Dario / Ferrero, Valter / Talli, Giuseppe / Cano, Ivan / Gaudino, Roberto

Digital Chromatic Dispersion Compensation (DCPC) has been investigated through both experiments and simulations to assess its resilience to multipath interference and differential group delay. The results show a performance similar to conventional PAM-2, with MPI-induced penalty below 1 dB for interference values under 15 dB.

talks.title: Mo5-G4: 200 Gb/s PolMux Link with 32 dB optical power budget, 28GHz electrical bandwidth and LO reuse for VHS-PONs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Izquierdo, David / Herguedas, Natalia / Sevillano, Pascual / Cajal-Pérez, Ramón / Garcés, Ignacio

In this work we experimentally demonstrate a 25km long, 200Gb/s PolMux multiCAP downstream link for Very-High Speed PONs, using a narrow 28GHz electrical bandwidth and obtaining an optical power budget of 32dB while reusing the LO at the receiver as the upstream source

talks.title: Mo5-G5: Research Directions on Hybrid PON for Very High Speed PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cano, Ivan

Two systems are proposed for VHSP that aim to centralize the complexity at the OLT while having simple DD at the ONU-Rx: DCPC and SSB. An evaluation of both systems in terms of their CD tolerance is provided as well as motivations for further research

sessions.title: Mo5-C Resonators, TFLT and integrated routing devices
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: Mo5-C1: Ultrafast Resonance-Tracking Thin-Film Lithium Tantalate Resonator: Enabling Colorless Self-Coherent Reception
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Haojie / Pang, Lei / Deng, Miao / Zeng, Cheng / Fang, Yuhao / Xu, Jinhong / Shan, Jianghao / Lu, Weiqi / Shi, Dayu / Cheng, Xue / Yuan, Shuai / Xia, Jinsong / Shieh, William

We demonstrate a high-Q thin-film lithium tantalate (TFLT) microring resonator featuring a fast adaptive resonance-tracking speed with a convergence time below 1.3 μs. The ultrafast-tracking TFLT resonator enables colorless carrier-extracted self-coherent reception, achieving 375-Gbps transmission over 50-km SSMF using an uncooled DFB laser.

talks.title: Mo5-C2: Low-Noise Agile FMCW Source via Self-Injection Locking of a DFB Laser to a Micro-Transfer-Printed TFLT-on-Si3N4 Cavity
talks.abstract:
Authors: Su, Jinwei / Li, Xinhang / Dai, Yiqi / Xia, Yifan / Lu, Liangjun / Guo, Yuyao / Zeng, Cheng / Xia, Jinsong / Chen, Jianping / Zhou, Linjie

We demonstrate a low-noise, frequency-agile FMCW source by self-injection-locking a DFB laser to a micro-transfer-printed TFLT-on-Si3N4 cavity, achieving a 100 Hz linewidth and highly linear frequency sweeps from 1 kHz to 10 MHz.

talks.title: Mo5-C3 Thin film lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuits for next generation high speed communications and lasers.
Mo5-C4: Reconfigurable Optical Routing Using Microring Resonators with Interferometric Arms
talks.abstract:
Authors: Skenderas, Martin / Othman, Hilmi / Bottrill, Kyle R. H. / Thomson, David J. / Petropoulos, Periklis

We demonstrate energy-efficient, resonance-stable, reconfigurable optical power routing in a microring resonator with interferometrically controlled coupling. The device achieves up to 20 dB power extinction ratio and error-free 80 Gb/s transmission, establishing a compact building block for scalable reconfigurable silicon photonic interconnects.

talks.title: Mo5-C5: A 500 Gbps PAM4 Silicon Microdisk Modulator With a 3.2 THz FSR and >110 GHz Bandwidth
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bao, Shenlei / Lai, Houyou / Cheng, Chao / Zhang, Wenfu / Wang, Binhao

We demonstrate a microdisk modulator with an ultra-high bandwidth exceeding 110 GHz at a 6 dB IL detuning and a FSR of 3.2 THz. Clear PAM4 eye diagrams at 448 and 500 Gbps are obtained, with TDECQ values of 1.41 dB and 2.46 dB, respectively.

sessions.title: Mo5-H Control and optimization of optical network systems
sessions.track: SC 10: Control and management of optical networks

talks.title: Mo5-H1: Physical-Model-Based Optical Line System Transmission Optimization Integrating Probing Transceivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Borraccini, Giacomo / D'Amico, Andrea / Huang, Yue-Kai / Wang, Ting / Asahi, Koji

An automated methodology for optical line systems integrating probing transceivers to initialize a system-level digital twin is described. Physical model parameters are inferred from scratch by combining end-to-end spectrum measurements, pre-FEC BER and optical amplifier telemetry, enabling near-optimal configuration, model alignment, and precise QoT tuning.

talks.title: Mo5-H2: Importance Sampling for Deterministic Uncertainty when Estimating QoT in Autonomous Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Delezoide, Camille / Ramantanis, Petros / Layec, Patricia

We investigate importance sampling to significantly improve computational efficiency when assessing the probability of lightpath failure in complex scenarios. Results pave the way towards risk-informed decision-making in self-driven optical networks.

talks.title: Mo5-H3: Experimental Demonstration of Optical Network Partitioning and Parallel Configuration for Autonomous Power Re-Equalization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Chenyu / Aknin, Louis / Ayassi, Reda / Stavrou, Photios A. / Pointurier, Yvan / Charlet, Gabriel

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a digital twin–based optical network partitioning strategy on a 7-OMS mesh optical network testbed. By leveraging parallel closed-loop control across subnets, the proposed approach reduces power re-equalization time by over 80%.

talks.title: Mo5-H4: Hybrid FXC-WXC Networks with Selective Wavelength Conversion: Dynamic Path Control and Experimental Demonstration
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hosokawa, Ryota / Shimoi, Shunya / Sekizuka, Taisei / Mano, Koki / Kuno, Takuma / Mori, Yojiro / Hosokawa, Kohei / Yanagimachi, Shigeyuki / Hasegawa, Hiroshi

We propose a hybrid FXC-WXC architecture with selective wavelength conversion for low-loss and flexible optical networks. Network simulations show reduced blocking and improved OSNR under dynamic control, while transmission experiments demonstrate lower BER and longer reach than WXC-only networks, supporting ZR+ deployment in metro/core networks.

talks.title: Mo5-H5: LOME: A Low-latency Optimal Ports Matching Engine for Optical Circuit Switches
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yu, Yangmiao / Chen, Can / Zhang, Yifan / Zang, Dawei

We propose a hardware-accelerated, low-latency,optimal ports matching engine for optical circuit switches to accommodate mouse flows.It reduces port-matching latency to hundreds of nanoseconds,an improvement by multiple orders of magnitude compared to CPU baselines,and reduces mouse flow latency by a factor of 19 on the demo.

talks.title: Mo5-H6: Selective Deployment of Bidirectional Hollow-Core Fibers in Hybrid SMF/HCF Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ibrahimi, Mëmëdhe / Sticca, Giovanni S. / Ferrara, Angelo / Tornatore, Massimo

We investigate selectively deploying bidirectional transmission in hybrid Hollow-Core Fiber (HCF) networks. Upgrading 50% of links to bidirectional HCF yields at least a 40% throughput increase compared to unidirectional SMF and captures 85% of the power consumption reduction of a full unidirectional HCF network upgrade.

sessions.title: Mo4-I Winning interconnects for AI: scale-up & scale-out technology paths
Welcome reception at Cruise Terminal
Morning coffee
Tu1-A From high-Q resonators to frequency comb generation
sessions.track: SC 12: CLEO® Special Session on Emerging Trends in Optics and Photonics

talks.title: Tu1-A1: High-Q Integrated Photonics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vahala, Kerry

We review recent progress in chip-integrated high-Q resonators and discuss their applications to frequency microcombs, second-harmonic generation, and spontaneous parametric down-conversion, along with recent system-level demonstrations of high-performance microwave signal sources.

talks.title: Tu1-A2 flattop soliton microcombs for low power optical data links

sessions.title: Tu1-B Hollow core fibers in optical networks
sessions.track: SC 06: Architecture, modelling and performance of optical networks

talks.title: Tu1-B1: On the Practical Impacts of Inter-Modal-Interference (IMI) in Hollow-Core Fibers for High-Speed Data Center Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: He, Yan / Dou, Liang / Chen, Sai / Zhai, Zhiqun / Zhang, Huan / Su, Yuanchao / Lau, Alan Pak Tao

We measured IMI-induced SNR after different HCF transmission with different transponders and frequency and found that SNR can be worse than theoretical value. A delivered OSNR model validated by 1.6T/λ transmission experiments identify -54dB/km as a practical IMI threshold, providing guidance on HCF-based DCI standardization/optimization.

talks.title: Tu1-B2: MIMO Channel Memory Requirements for Randomly-Coupled Multicore Fiber Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kalla, Besma / S. Luis, Ruben / Gaiani, Stefano / Orsuti, Daniele / Blown, Patrick / Van Den Hout, Menno / A. Colares, Robson / A. A. Mello, Darli / Boffi, Pierpaolo / Bradley, Thomas / Okonkwo, Chigo / Furukawa, Hideaki

We evaluate the impact of network nodes on MIMO memory requirements in a C+L-band randomly-coupled multicore fiber network. While point-to-point transmission requires less than 1 ns of memory, constraining network operation to this length results in throughput penalties of 50–75% due to path delay misalignment.

talks.title: Tu1-B3: New opportunities in optical networks enabled by hollow-core fibres
talks.abstract:
Authors: Petropoulos, Periklis / Wantee, Suttikarn / Mcculloch, Douglas / Liu, Hao / Ostrovskis, Armands / Cirjulina, Darja / Jasion, Gregory T. / Sakr, Hesham / Pang, Xiaodan / Ozolins, Oskars / Poletti, Francesco / Bottrill, Kyle R.H. / Jung, Yongmin

Hollow-core fibres enable performance and applications that are challenging to achieve in conventional solid-core fibre systems. Here we review demonstrations in intensity modulation direct-detection transmission and simultaneous power-and-data delivery that offer opportunities for new
services and enhanced performance in optical communication networks.

talks.title: Tu1-B4: Physics-Driven Transfer Learning Approach for OSNR Prediction in Hollow-Core Fiber-Based Data Center Interconnect Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xu, Jiahui / Qin, Xin / Gu, Zhiqun / Chen, Wei / Li, Shaopeng / Jiang, Xiaotian / Yang, Zheng / Han, Yuqing / Zhang, Jiawei / Gu, Rentao / Ji, Yuefeng

This paper proposes a physics-driven transfer learning approach for Hollow-Core Fiber (HCF) OSNR prediction. Utilizing a theoretical analytical model for pre-training, it achieves robust predictions with minimal experimental samples, eliminating 17 dB cliffs, reaching 0.388 dB RMSE and 0.6 dB 95% error bounds.

sessions.title: Tu1-D Optical amplification
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: Tu1-D1: High-gain and Low-noise Integrated Fiber Amplifier with Seamless 102 nm Bandwidth Across the Extended C+L Band
talks.abstract:
Authors: Huang, Xin / Shen, Lei / Qi, Junjie / Zhou, Shiqi / Liao, Zhaolong / Ding, Yuanpeng / Li, Chan / Gao, Yuan / Zhang, Hui / He, Zhixiong / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie

We report a hybrid EBDF/BDF fiber amplifier that achieves integrated amplification with a seamless 102 nm spectral bandwidth in the extended C+L band for the first time. The amplifier exhibits a gain of 26.7 dB and a noise figure of 4.6 dB.

talks.title: Tu1-D2: High-Gain Sub-3 dB Noise Figure Chip-Based Phase Sensitive Preamplifier with Pulsed Pumping
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Junda / Larsson, Rasmus / A. Andrekson, Peter

We demonstrate a sub-3dB “black box” noise figure, Si₃N₄ waveguide-based phase-sensitive preamplifier receiver using pulsed pump. A 37 dB gain yields a sensitivity of -59 dBm at BER=10-3 for a 2 Gb/s QPSK signal, with an estimated 0.5 dB on-chip noise figure.

talks.title: Tu1-D3: Optical Amplification in the S-band and Beyond: From Materials and Mechanisms to Practical Deployment
talks.abstract:
Authors: Donodin, Aleksandr / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Pratiwi, Dini / Stoliarov, Dmitrii / Tan, Mingming / Luo, Jiawei / Digiovanni, David J. / Phillips, Ian / Forysiak, Wladek / Turitsyn, Sergei K.

We review recent advances in S-band optical amplifiers for communication systems, comparing doped-fibre, Raman, parametric, and semiconductor approaches. Gain mechanisms, performance, and efficiency are analysed, highlighting key trade-offs and emerging solutions for scalable, energy-efficient transmission within and beyond the S-band.

talks.title: Tu1-D4: Energy Harvesting over Optical Communication Networks Using Discarded Light from a Gain-Flattening Filter
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wada, Masaki / Sakamoto, Taiji / Matsui, Takashi / Nakajima, Kazuhide

We demonstrate electrical-domain energy harvesting over optical communication networks and show for the first time that more than 10 mW of electrical power per core can be extracted from discarded optical power at a gain-flattening filter in a four-core erbium-doped fibre amplifier.

sessions.title: Tu1-E Optical switches and demultiplexers
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: Tu1-E1: 200 Gbps Coherent Optical Switching Enabled by an Integrated Si3N4-TFLN Laser
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wu, Yilin / Ma, Yan / Li, Deqi / Xue, Qiyin / Yang, Sigang / Chen, Hongwei / Tang, Liwei / Wang, Hui / Yu, Zhenming / Chen, Minghua

We achieve 200 Gbps coherent optical switching with a switching latency of 80 ns and bit error ratios of below 1×10-4. It is enabled by a tri-material Integrated Si3N4-TFLN laser unifying an intrinsic linewidth of 181 Hz and below-15-ns electro-optic wavelength switching.

talks.title: Tu1-E2: Low-loss Silicon Photonic MEMS Switch Array Based on 2.5D Torus Topology
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Jiayue / Zhang, Xiang / Hu, Yinpeng / Liao, Jianxing / Dong, Xiaowen / Li, Huan / Dai, Daoxin

A scheme for scalable low-loss silicon photonic switch arrays using micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) switches and a novel 2.5D Torus topology is proposed and demonstrated, which exhibits one of the lowest insertion losses among widely used wide-sense and strictly non-blocking topologies.

talks.title: Tu1-E3 breaking the AI networking and memory wall with a wide-and-slow architecture and microleds
Tu1-E4: An 8×8 Optical Circuit Switch in Thin-Film Lithium Tantalate
talks.abstract:
Authors: Maes, Dennis / Chatzitheocharis, Dimitrios / Bing, Ju / De Mulder, Bert / Chen, William

We demonstrate the first 8×8 electro-optic optical circuit switch (OCS) on thin-film lithium tantalate (TFLT). The photonic integrated circuit comprises twelve 2×2 switches and achieves <4 ns switching, sub-1-µW static power consumption, and <0.5 dB output power stability over 1 hour without active feedback.

talks.title: Tu1-E5: Static and Dynamic Ring Assignment in a Clock-Forwarded DWDM Optical Link
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rekhi, Angad / Tell, Stephen / Zimmer, Brian / Xu, Li / Kalogerakis, Georgios / Song, Sanquan / Mehta, Nandish / Nedovic, Nikola / Nishi, Yoshi / Chen, Xi / Lopes, Ward / Lee, Benjamin / Greer, Thomas / Gray, Thomas

We present heater sweep-based in-situ minimum-power assignment of microrings to lasers during clock-forwarded optical link initialization (“static ring assignment”). We also show rotation of microring-to-laser assignment during live link operation (“dynamic ring assignment”).

sessions.title: Tu1-F AI-driven control and monitoring in optical access networks
sessions.track: SC 10: Control and management of optical networks

talks.title: Tu1-F1: Digital Twin, Agent and Artificial Intelligence Towards ION-2030
talks.abstract:
Authors: Busi, Italo / Li, Xiao / Yu, Henry

This paper explores trends in Artificial Intelligence, Network Digital Twin, and Agents aimed at enhancing the operations of optical networks. Following the ITU-T ION-2030 vision, it also addresses the standardization gaps that remain.

talks.title: Tu1-F2: A Deterministic Bandwidth-Mapper Scheme in Upstream TDM-PON for Time-Sensitive Industrial AI Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Das, Sandip / Bonk, Rene / Tsiaflakis, Paschalis

This paper proposes a real‑time, scalable deterministic bandwidth-mapper (BWmapper) for upstream TDM‑PON, capable of supporting a large number of Time-Sensitive Industrial-AI flows with diverse latency and jitter requirements alongside best‑effort traffic. Validated through simulation and experiments, the scheme demonstrates low computational complexity and high efficiency.

talks.title: Tu1-F3: Dynamic PON Monitoring System Based on Time-Frequency Encoded Optical Pulses
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Ruisi / Zhang, Yijie / Xiao, Xiangpeng / Yang, Qi / Deng, Lei / Cheng, Mengfan / Sun, Qizhen / Yan, Zhijun / Tang, Ming

We propose a novel PON monitoring method using time–frequency encoded optical pulse sequences and cross-correlation analysis for real-time fault localization and port detection in dynamic port switching scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves sub-meter localization accuracy and 100% port identification accuracy.

talks.title: Tu1-F4: Passive GPON Monitoring for Network Load Forecasting Using BWMap Information
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ingles Loggia, Lucas / Anet Neto, Luiz / Rattaro, Claudina / Morvan, Michel / Castro, Alberto / Nuaymi, Loutfi

We present a vendor and element management system-agnostic solution for passive upstream bandwidth monitoring in GPON. We demonstrate its usage in a commercial platform for forecasting the network congestion state and providing services profiling, enabling SLA verification and identification of low-congestion windows. ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: Tu1-F5: Demonstration of Optical Access Network Failure Management for RAN Control toward Rapid Recovery
talks.abstract:
Authors: Asada, Megumi / Harada, Takumi / Miyamoto, Kenji / Hatano, Tomoya / Shimada, Tatsuya

We propose RAN control based on failure notifications from the optical access network to shorten failure recovery time for high reliability services. Experiments show that the interruption time can be reduced by 66.9% compared with the conventional method.

sessions.title: Tu1-G Short reach interconnects
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: Tu1-G1: Scalable, High-Capacity Optical Transmission for AI Data Centre Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wakayama, Yuta / J. Elson, Daniel / Wang, Cen / Wang, Han / Tsuritani, Takehiro

This paper reviews ultrawideband optical transmission technologies for scalable AI data centre networks and presents an optical‑gateway‑based scale‑across architecture. Exploiting O‑band expansion, WDM/SDM aggregation, and RDMA‑over‑WDM, the approach enables capacity scaling beyond single‑facility limits whilst reducing fibre deployment.

talks.title: Tu1-G2: 24-l Coherent Optical Communications Using Passive Coherence Cloning of Dark-Soliton Microcombs for Homodyne Detection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Peng, Huanfa / Bao, Yiyang / Zheng, Yi / Freude, Wolfgang / Yvind, Kresten / Randel, Sebastian / Pu, Minhao / Koos, Christian

We report on the first demonstration of coherent multi-wavelength transmission using passive coherence cloning of Kerr microcombs. Our scheme leverages a coherence-cloned replica of the transmitter comb as a multi-wavelength local oscillator for homodyne reception of 24 16QAM and 32QAM channels with reduced digital-signal-processing effort.

talks.title: Tu1-G3: Regular Perturbation on the Group-Velocity Dispersion Parameter for Dual-Polarization Short-Reach Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cellini, Dario / Oliari, Vinícius / Agrell, Erik / Secondini, Marco / Liga, Gabriele / Alvarado, Alex

The Manakov equation governs the propagation of signals in dual-polarization systems. Its solution is usually approximated by regular perturbation on the nonlinear Kerr parameter. In this paper, we propose a novel regular perturbation on the group-velocity dispersion parameter for the Manakov equation.

talks.title: Tu1-G4: Water Vapor Robustness of Hollow-Core Fiber for O-Band Short Reach Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gao, Yuan / Dai, Lu / Xu, Yifei / Dong, Zihan / Chu, Jun / Li, Peng / Shen, Lei / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie

This work presents the first experimental investigation of water vapor's impact on O‑band hollow-core fibres. Results show that HCFs are robust to water vapor: even after prolonged high-humidity exposure, attenuation at the O‑band operating wavelengths remains virtually unaffected, confirming their reliability for O‑band short‑reach interconnects.

talks.title: Tu1-G5: 172 Tb/s GMI, O-band Coherent Transmission with OSNR Optimization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Donodin, Aleksandr / Saxena, Shekhar / Elson, Daniel J. / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Emmerich, Robert / Stoliarov, Dmitrii / Luis, Ruben S. / Luo, Jiawei / Furukawa, Hideaki / Schubert, Colja / Freund, Ronald / Digiovanni, David J. / Wakayama, Yuta / Tsuritani, Takehiro / Phillips, Ian / Turistyn, Sergei K.

We report a record GMI-estimated transmission of 172.87 Tb/s over 25 km of G.652.D in the O-band, achieved using 633 × 24.5 GBaud DP-64QAM and DP-128QAM channels, with optimized launched signal and Raman pump powers.

sessions.title: Tu1-C Advanced enabling technologies for free-space optical and optical wireless communications
sessions.track: SC 09: Free-space optics and optical wireless technologies

talks.title: Tu1-C1: Sweep-Free Coherent Tracking Using a Multi-Tone Local Oscillator with a 100-MHz-Bandwidth Quadrant Photodetector
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kan, Takashi / Fukuhara, Shin / Murakami, Kensuke / Akasaka, Akira / Takahashi, Hidenori / Tsuritani, Takehiro

With narrowband detectors, coherent beam tracking is challenging under signal–local oscillator frequency offset uncertainty, given reliance on frequency sweeping or wideband reception. We demonstrate frequency‑offset‑tolerant error signal generation and closed‑loop beam tracking under realistic disturbances using a multi‑tone local oscillator.

talks.title: Tu1-C2: Diversity Gain of 2-D PD Array in a 13.3°/s High-mobility FSO System with 13-ms Handover Latency
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yoshida, Yuki / Weng, Zu-Kai / Umezawa, Toshimasa / Hattori, Michikazu / Hara, Yuichiro / Matsumoto, Atsushi / Akahane, Kouichi / Shinada, Satoshi / Yamamoto, Naokatsu

We investigate the impact of 2-D PD array-based diversity reception in realistic mobile FSO scenarios, including terminal mobility and handovers. By eliminating tracking jitter-induced outages through diversity combining, the arrayed receiver achieved zero tracking-induced interruption under a 13.3°/s terminal velocity and 13-ms handover latency.

talks.title: Tu1-C3: Increasing the Alignment Tolerance in Long-Reach FSO Links by using a Photodiode Matrix
talks.abstract:
Authors: Koonen, Ton / Tangdiongga, Eduward

A matrix of 2D-interconnected PDs enables a broadband FSO receiver with large effective aperture and wide field-of-view. Without needing adaptive optics, it offers superior link robustness over single-PD and MMF-coupled FSO receivers, and compact receiver solution. Alignment tolerances increase >3x and scale with matrix size.

talks.title: Tu1-C4: Cost-Effective 448-Gbps Indoor Optical Wireless Access Via Dual-Polarization Carrier-Extracted Direct Detection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Haojie / Pang, Lei / Xu, Jinhong / Fang, Yuhao / Lu, Weiqi / Shi, Dayu / Yuan, Puzhen / Shieh, William

We propose a dual-polarization carrier-extracted direct detection without polarization tracking because of the polarization stability in free-space environment. The system achieves a 448-Gbps transmission data rate in 9-meter indoor free-space link without expensive local oscillators while meeting the eye-safety standard.

talks.title: Tu1-C5: Free-Space Optical Communication using Photonic-Crystal Sur-face-Emitting Lasers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ishimura, Shota / Inoue, Takuya / Morita, Ryohei / Takahashi, Hidenori / Tsuritani, Takehiro / De Zoysa, Menaka / Ishizaki, Kenji / Suzuki, Masatoshi / Noda, Susumu

Photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers (PCSELs) offer a compelling route to compact free-space optical (FSO) transmitters by combining watt-class single-mode output, narrow divergence, and direct modulation on a single chip. This invited paper reviews recent progress from initial lens-free demonstrations to >10-Gbit/s, and coherent PCSEL-based links.

sessions.title: Tu1-H Microwave photonics and radio over fiber
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: Tu1-H1: Reconfigurable Microwave Photonic Demultiplexer Using Integrated CROW and Lattice Filters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gonzalez Guerrero, Luis / Zarzuelo, Alberto / Tian, Jiale / Delgado Mendinueta, Jose Manuel / Mitsolidou, Charoula / Roeloffzen, Chris G. H. / Carpintero, Guillermo

We demonstrate an integrated microwave photonic demultiplexer using cascaded CROW and lattice filters, enabling tunable bandwidth (125–500 MHz) and strong channel suppression. Experimental demultiplexing of 16-QAM signals at 23 GHz is demonstrated, confirming reconfigurable filtering for flexible satellite payloads.

talks.title: Tu1-H2: Photonic Millimeter-wave Parallel Chaos Source Enabling Multi-Channel Secure Communication and Sensing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Deng, Qiuzhuo / Wang, Can / Ye, Kangpeng / Chen, Guanyu / Ozolins, Oskars / Pang, Xiaodan / Zhang, Lu / Yu, Xianbin

We experimentally demonstrate a 2×5 Gbps photonic mmWave secure communication and an interference-free MISO sensing with a single receiver, empowered by a parallel chaos source with 40 channels and up to 94.5 GHz bandwidth per channel, overcoming hardware bottlenecks in future multi-functional mmWave networks.

talks.title: Tu1-H3: A Monolithic Analog Radio-over-Fiber Uplink Transmitter with –100.8 to –98.3 dBm Effective Isotropic Sensitivity for mm-Wave Communications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ke, Jiacong / Fang, Jiaqin / Shekhar, Sudip

We present a monolithic analog radio-over-fiber uplink transmitter co-integrating LNAs, driver, and MZM on a CMOS SOI process. The transmitter achieves 26.1-dB gain, 8.2-dB noise figure, and –100.8-dBm EIS, enabling DPD-free 1.1% and 2.25% EVM of 16-QAM and 32-QAM, respectively, meeting 3GPP requirements.

talks.title: Tu1-H4: Integrated Photonic RF Receiver with Frequency Downconversion in a Packaged InP PIC for Satellite Payloads
talks.abstract:
Authors: Belchovski, Metodi / Benazet, Benoit / Sotom, Michel / Rommel, Simon

We demonstrate an integrated photonic RF front-end for satellite payloads using a packaged InP PIC, combining optical LO distribution with Ka- to C-band microwave downconversion, supporting 1×128 antenna elements, achieving 24 dB conversion loss, 53 dB noise figure, and < 15% EVM across modulation formats.

talks.title: Tu1-H5: Processing THz Signals with GHz Electronics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Schneider, Thomas

We present the fundamentals and latest findings on the generation, processing and reception of THz-bandwidth signals using low-bandwidth electronics and orthogonal base functions for communication and the acceleration of photonic signal processing.

sessions.title: Tu1-I Optical fiber sensing and its aplications
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: Tu1-I1: End-to-End Modelling of Earthquake-Induced Polarisation Perturbations in Submarine Optical Fibres
talks.abstract:
Authors: Butler, Rick M. / Núñez-Kasaneva, José / Liga, Gabriele / Karlsson, Magnus / Alvarado, Alex / Häger, Christian

We present an end-to-end model of earthquake-perturbed signal propagation in submarine fibres. Ground displacements are converted to fibre strain via ocean pressure, and injected into a split-step model. Our model shows good qualitative alignment with measurements from the Curie cable during the 2020 Oaxaca earthquake.

talks.title: Tu1-I2: Polarization Noise Anisotropy-Aware Technique for Enhanced Earthquake Detection Using Coherent Subsea Transponders
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mohammad Hosseini, Mohammad / Masanas, Miquel / Parisi, Giuseppe / Mecozzi, Antonio / Marullo, Alberto / Decaroli, Danilo / Napoli, Antonio

Polarization noise anisotropy, in coherent subsea transponders, limits the reliability of earthquake detection. We analyze lab- and field-deployed transponders using a tensor-based eigenvalue decomposition technique that dynamically aligns seismic signals with the eigenvectors, enhancing detection sensitivity up to 16 dB improvement in SNR.

talks.title: Tu1-I3: Path-Integrated Polarization Rotation Signatures in Subsea Networks: Cable Geometry Effects in 2023 Turkey Earthquakes
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mohammad Hosseini, Mohammad / Masanas, Miquel / Parisi, Giuseppe / Braga Melo, Wesley / Marullo, Alberto / Decaroli, Danilo / K. Turitsyn, Sergei / Napoli, Antonio

We analyze polarization data streamed from a commercial coherent transponder, used in MedNautilus link, during 2023 Turkey earthquakes. We show how earthquake features and cable geometry fundamentally govern the optical polarization response, taking the first steps for detailed interpretation in designing fiber-based seismic sensing systems.

talks.title: Tu1-I4: Towards SOP-based Real-Time Earthquake Detection: Limitations and Opportunities
talks.abstract:
Authors: Melo, Wesley / Gomes, Geraldo / Freire, Pedro / Turitsyn, Sergei / Mecozzi, Antonio / Hosseini, Mohammad / Napoli, Antonio

We statistically analyze real SOP data using a physics-informed seismic event-labelling model and show that 95% of the 798 seismic events have SNR below 1.64dB, independent of distance. We demonstrate a real-time low-cost pipeline extensible to 20Hz Jones sampling, while highlighting limitations and research opportunities.

talks.title: Tu1-I5: Passive Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Borehole Seismic Velocity Profiling: A 3 km Geothermal Well Field Trial
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Zehao / Stroujkova, Anastasia / Horowitz, Franklin G. / Eppink, Jeffrey / Ji, Philip N. / Li, Yaowen / Malin, Peter / Chen, Tingjun

We demonstrate passive borehole velocity profiling using coherent DAS on a 3 km geothermal well. Deconvolution interferometry with phase-weighted stacking recovers velocities from ambient micro-vibrations without active sources, achieving <80 m/s mean absolute error at 0.5–1 km depth against a calibration shot ground truth.

talks.title: Tu1-I6: Real-time Tracking and Localization of Rapid Instantaneous SOP Fluctuations for 100G Coherent System over FPGA
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tang, Yu / Shen, Shikui / Shi, Yan / Cui, Sheng / Liu, Jingpeng / xu, Menghong / Zhang, Chuanbiao / Tang, Ming / Wang, Guangquan

We demonstrate a two-step AEQ cooperating a loopback configuration to track and locate rapid instantaneous state of polarization in a 100G 16QAM coherent optical system based on FPGA. The localization error is within 115 m at 5 MHz.

sessions.title: Exhibition & coffee break
Tu2-Ex Demo zone

talks.title: Tu2-Ex10: OpticalClaw: An Interactive Agentic Digital Twin for Optical Communication System Design and Optimization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Zhiming / Zhong, Tianchi / Cai, Xiang / Fan, Runzhe / Shu, Hua / Li, Lingyuan / Fu, Sidi / Zhou, Xian / Zhang, Fan

OpticalClaw is a remote interactive agent for optical-link design. It embeds a high-fidelity waveform-level digital twin, enabling natural-language link construction, simulation, result analysis, and iterative parameter optimization in a closed loop.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex11: Demonstration of a Telemetry-Assisted QoS-Aware Scheduler over SOA-Based Time-Slotted Optical Metro-Access Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ghasrizadeh, Sadegh / Freire Santana, Henrique / Calabretta, Nicola / Costa, Nelson / Velasco, Luis

We demonstrate a telemetry-assisted QoS-aware scheduler controlling an SOA-based time-slotted optical metro-access network. Cyclic plans consider real-time telemetry measuring the state of the queues in the access nodes and the priority of 6G traffic flows.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex12: Demonstration of Joint Communication, Sensing & Monitoring with Unified Management on a 4-Core Multi-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jürgensen, Tom / Moawad, Abdelrahmane / Srivallapanondh, Sasipim / Kremling, Stefan / Fischer, Johannes / Napoli, Antonio / Dochhan, Annika / Pachnicke, Stephan

We experimentally demonstrate a 4-core multi-core fiber SDM system, enabling simultaneous bidirectional coherent transmission, IM/DD transmission, integrated longitudinal power monitoring, distributed acoustic sensing, and unified control-plane operation across communication, monitoring, and sensing functions.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex13: ML-Aided Transponder-Native SOP Sensing for Proactive Restoration in Live Metro Data Center Xchange
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ambrosone, Renato / Masanas, Miquel / Kholodov, Daniil / Malik, Gulmina / Schips, Riccardo / Straullu, Stefano / Colantonio, Matteo / Vuagnin, Gloria / Bolletta, Paolo / Aquilino, Francesco / Nespola, Antonino / Virgillito, Emanuele / Napoli, Antonio / Curri, Vittorio

We demonstrate transponder-native SOP sensing over a live metro DCX spectrum service. Coherent transponder telemetry feeds a Kafka-based ML pipeline that classifies fiber disturbances and triggers real ROADM restoration without external polarimeters.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex14: Autonomous Link Restoration and Capacity Management in Open Optical Networks for Connected Mobility Services
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vettori, Luca / Martínez, Ricardo / Casellas, Ramon / Vílchez, Francisco Javier / Casas, Josep Ramon / García-Gómez, Pablo / Subirana Pérez, Adrià / Muñoz, Raül / Royo, Santiago / Lázaro, José Antonio / Fabrega, Josep M.

This demonstration integrates sensing with programmable packet-optical infrastructure. We showcase autonomous capacity upgrades and network restoration to maintain high-performance connectivity for demanding mobility applications when using real-world data from a sensorized vehicle platform prototype.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex15: Telemetry-Driven Scale-Across over On-Demand Optical Slices in Federated Data Centres
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kretsis, Aristotelis / Soumplis, Polyzois / Ambrosone, Renato / Giorgetti, Alessio / Casellas, Ramon / Schips, Riccardo / Curri, Vittorio / Robles, Pablo Armingol / De Dios, Oscar Gonzalez / Lopez, Antonio Buendia / Fernandez, Enrique / Nespola, Antonino / Varvarigos, Emmanouel

We demonstrate telemetry-driven scale-across of distributed workloads over on-demand optical slices between geo-distributed data centres on a disaggregated multi-vendor testbed. Analytics anticipate SLA pressure across compute- and network-bound phases and trigger QoT-validated slice adaptation.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex16: Experimental Demonstration of AI in Performance Optimization of Short-Reach Optical Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Solaimani, Ramin / Civelli, Stella / Cellini, Dario / Secondini, Marco / Zhang, Li / Nizamani, Asfand / Forestieri, Enrico / Nadimi Goki, Pantea / Cavaliere, Fabio / Potì, Luca

We demonstrate a unified platform that compares AI-assisted optimization strategies for short-reach IM/DD interconnects (transmitter pre-distortion, neural-network and look-up-table receivers, and end-to-end learning) through live simulations and remotely operated laboratory experiments with real-time performance visualization.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex17: Preventing Data Hallucinations in Agentic AI for Optical Network Troubleshooting
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dötterl, Jeremias / Kuipers, Martin

An agentic AI system for automated troubleshooting in optical communication networks is demonstrated that integrates data references into the agent architecture to prevent data hallucinations, improving the interpretability and trustworthiness of root-cause identification and reasoning.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex18: Nanoseconds Reconfigurable Optical Switching Platform Based on REC-DFB Laser Arrays and AWGR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wu, Xianchen / Zhang, Dongxu / Zhang, Maosen / Hu, Yakun / Zhang, Shicheng / Guo, Bingli / Li, Wenzhe / Shen, Shikui / Wang, Guangquan / Yuan, Guojun / Huang, Shanguo / Xue, Xuwei

We demonstrate a nanosecond reconfigurable optical switching platform combining REC-DFB laser arrays, AWGR routing, FPGA-based scheduling, and visualized traffic steering to show destination-dependent wavelength selection and dynamic optical path reconfiguration in a four-node prototype.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex19: Exploiting Observability in Optical Networks for AI-driven Real-time Soft Failure Detection and Continual Learning
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sgambelluri, Andrea / Paolini, Emilio / Bottari, Giulio / Ponzini, Filippo / Valcarenghi, Luca / Castoldi, Piero / Iovanna, Paola

We propose an observability-enabled AI framework using telemetry for degradation management. The proposed autoencoder-based solution detects anomalies, localizes the soft-failures, automates re-action, and supports continual learning, for automatic model retraining while the network is evolving.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex1: TwinLight: A Multi-Timescale Physical-Layer-Aware T-API-Compliant Optical Domain Controller Digital Twin
talks.abstract:
Authors: Natalino, Carlos / Lechowicz, Piotr / Ambrosone, Renato / Miotto, Enrico / Curri, Vittorio / Monti, Paolo

We demonstrate TwinLight, an open-source optical-network digital twin acting as an optical domain controller. Its T-API REST and telemetry streaming interfaces use a physical-layer engine comprising a GNPy steady-state QoT baseline and four analytical transients.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex20: LLM-Orchestrated Optical-Fibre ISAC Platform for Sensing-Event Monitoring and Selective Network Response
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhao, Wanxin / Shen, Sen / Ge, Peiyun / Han, Jing / Teng, Yiran / Cai, Zhuojun / Xi, Lixia / Yan, Shuangyi / Simeonidou, Dimitra

We propose an LLM-driven integrated communication-and-sensing system for automated QoT monitoring, sensing-event interpretation, vibration localization, and adaptive network response. Our use case demonstrates real-time vibration-event classification and localization for proactive link-risk assessment.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex21: 240 Gbit/s Coherent PON Demo with Simplified ONU Design Using Uncalibrated Lasers and Coexistence with Legacy PONs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Adib, Md Mosaddek Hossain / Straub, Michael / Lanneer, Wouter / Das, Sandip / Bonk, Rene / Fuellner, Christoph

We demonstrate in‑service alignment of a wavelength‑uncalibrated LO laser in a proof‑of‑concept coherent PON setup, enabling a 240 Gbit/s downstream link. Coexistence with legacy PON validates a potential migration path toward future high‑capacity access networks.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex22: Modular & Hybrid Physical-Digital Twin for Optical-Mobile Networking
talks.abstract:
Authors: Brienza, Valentin / Ingles, Lucas / Rattaro, Claudina / Anet Neto, Luiz / Morvan, Michel / Castro, Alberto / Nuaymi, Loutfi

We demonstrate a modular optical-mobile testbed combining commercial G-PON equipment, an OMNeT++/INET optical DWDM network simulator, and open-source 5G/O-RAN components. Its interchangeable physical, simulated, and emulated segments support researcher-defined fixed-mobile convergence experiments.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex2: Comparative Demonstration of Coherent-Pluggable Control Architectures for Disaggregated IPoWDM Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zaid, Hussein / Mitrovska, Angela / Raulin, Julie / Xia, Chunmin / Shariati, Behnam / Jafari, Aydin / Kremling, Stefan / Lipp, Fabian / Hock, David / Melin, Stefan / Lindgren, Anders / Fischer, Johannes K. / Freund, Ronald

We demonstrate three IPoWDM coherent-pluggable workflows: hierarchical IP-controller-only management, EDCC-governed dual-controller access with hierarchical SDN coordination, and direct optical-controller access without hierarchical controller, validating responsibilities, access control, and policy enforcement on a live multi-vendor testbed

talks.title: Tu2-Ex3: MCP-Enabled Agentic AI for Autonomous IPoDWDM Network Lifecycle Automation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xia, Chunmin / Harbaczewski, Jakub / Dsilva, Nikhil / Raulin, Julie / Schneider, Dominic / Autenrieth, Achim

This demo presents an MCP-enabled agentic AI architecture for autonomous control of vendor-agnostic IPoDWDM networks. We demonstrate live end-to-end lifecycle multi-layer automation and closed-loop control using GNPy and telemetry, validated on a real testbed.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex4: Inter-Satellite All-Optical Networks (ISAON): Hands-on Demonstration of Orbit-Aware Routing Design and WDM Ground-Emulator Control
talks.abstract:
Authors: Brasi, Anthony / Hirota, Yusuke / Oda, Shoichiro / Kotake, Hideaki / Shinada, Satoshi / Furukawa, Hideaki

We developed a software prototype for inter-satellite all-optical network operation, demonstrating GUI-based visualisation of orbit-aware routing and live WDM ground-emulator control to monitor 100/200/300 Gbps transmission performance on the path corresponding to Barcelona–Mumbai.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex5: Demonstration of a Quantum-Safe Network Service Including Quantum Key Distribution, Software-Define Networking and Telco Edge Cloud Integration
talks.abstract:
Authors: Redolfi, Elisa / Orto, Domenico / Manco, Marco / Emanuele, Alessandro / Kwiecien, Piotr / Gatto, Alberto / Franceschini, Daniele

This demonstration presents a quantum-safe network service integrating QKD, SDN, and Telco Edge Cloud technologies, enabling secure key distribution, real-time monitoring, and industrial application protection, demonstrating scalability, interoperability, and deployment feasibility in realistic telecom environments.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex6: GsOQDC: A GUI-Driven Interactive Framework for End-to-End Simulation of Optical Quantum Data Centers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Elyasi, Seyed Navid / Bahrani, Sima / Wang, Rui / Simeonidou, Dimitra / Monti, Paolo / Lin, Rui

We present GsOQDC, an open-source graphical framework integrating optical-network design, distributed quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and DES-based remote-gate simulation, enabling end-to-end cross-layer evaluation of entanglement-resource dynamics and system-level performance in Optical Quantum Data Centers ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: Tu2-Ex7: Demonstration of Digital Twin Development and Validation Workflows in Heterogeneous Multi-Party Environments using OTDS
talks.abstract:
Authors: Akbari, Hassan / Mitrovska, Angela / Hirota, Yusuke / Xu, Sugang / Suzuki, Taiga / Raj, Agastya / Crognale, Claudio / Shariati, Behnam / Safari, Pooyan / Yoshida, Yuki / Ruffini, Marco / Invernizzi, Pietro / Shinada, Satoshi / Furukawa, Hideaki / Awaji, Yoshinari / Pasti, Mattia / Corti, Sara / Turolla, Silvia / Fischer, Johannes Karl / Freund, Ronald

We demonstrate a Digital Twin (DT) data space enabling policy-governed exchange of Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)-defined DT components across organizations. The demo showcases interoperable and real-time cross-organizational DT workflows using heterogeneous optical network environments.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex8: AI-Enabled Autonomous Service Migration for Proactive SLA Assurance in Optical Access and Transport Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rahimi, Hesam / Gifre, Lluis / Vilalta, Ricard / Akbar, Waleed / Muñoz, Raul / Armingol, Pablo / González, Oscar / Fernández-Palacios, Juan Pedro / Yu, Henry / Janz, Christopher / Lin, Yi / Zhang, Liang / Lønsethagen, Håkon

We demonstrate a fully autonomous Network-as-a-Service platform where an AI-assisted orchestrator proactively migrates the services between best-effort and deterministic performance across end-to-end F5G-Advanced access and transport segments to ensure SLA compliance for real-time immersive applications.

talks.title: Tu2-Ex9: Failure Detection and Recovery of IP Virtual Network Slice using P2MP DSCM Pluggable Transceivers for Xhaul Networks Controlled by Multi-layer SDN Control Framework
talks.abstract:
Authors: Akbar, Waleed / Radovic, Margita / Lawson, Marc / Armingol Robles, Pablo / Psaromanolakis, Nikos / Prassas, Apostolos / Zaid, Hussein / Schmidt-Langhorst, Carsten / Sgambelluri, Andrea / Sambo, Nicola / Gifre, Lluis / Vilalta, Ricard / Gonzalez De Dios, Oscar / Pedro Fernandez-Palacios Gimenez, Juan / Schubert, Colja / Freund, Ronald / Munoz, Raul

This demonstration showcases autonomous failure detection and recovery for Xhaul IP virtual network slices over P2MP DSCM pluggable, where optical controller detects failure, while the multi-layer SDN framework coordinates the slice migration to backup path.

sessions.title: Lunch
Tu3-A AI and advanced processing for optical communication systems
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: Tu3-A1 Communication engineering in the age of AI
Tu3-A2: 24×432-Gbps/λ All-Optical Equalization for DSP-Free Optical Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Benshan / Xiao, Qiarong / Wang, Dongliang / Chen, Yihao / Xu, Tengji / Fan, Li / Liu, Shaojie / Huang, Chaoran

We demonstrate an integrated all-optical signal processor (OSP), enabling WDM transmission of 24-channels at 432-Gbps/λ over 2-km SMF across the whole C-band. The OSP simultaneously equalizes fiber-dispersion and transceiver-bandwidth-limit with <50-mW power and <75-ps latency, offering a disruptive solution for energy-efficient and low-latency optical interconnects.

talks.title: Tu3-A3: 220-GBd optical coherent waveform generation using temporal unitary transforms
talks.abstract:
Authors: Deakin, Callum / Chen, Xi / Che, Di

We use temporal unitary transforms to generate 16-QAM up to 220 GBd using only 50-GHz electrical bandwidth. The technique is theoretically lossless and can generate arbitrary optical waveforms beyond the bandwidth of the constituent modulators.

sessions.title: Tu3-B Light propagation and manipulation from short to long distance
sessions.track: SC 12: CLEO® Special Session on Emerging Trends in Optics and Photonics

talks.title: Tu3-B1: Metamaterial Integrated Photonics for Light Coupling, Beam Steering and Spectral Filtering
talks.abstract:
Authors: Schmid, Jens / Cheben, Pavel / Zhang, Jianhao / Korcek, Radovan / Cheriton, Ross / Xu, Dan-Xia / Wang, Shurui / Vachon, Martin / Ma, Rubin / Halir, Robert / Wanguemert-Perez, Gonzalo / Ortega-Monux, Alejandro / Molina-Fernandez, Inigo / Sanchez-Postigo, Alejandro / Luque-Gonzalez, Jose-Manuel / Fernandez-Hinestrosa, Alejandro / Melati, Daniele / Alonso-Ramos, Carlos / Vivien, Laurent / Ye, Winnie

In this paper we provide an overview of recent developments in metamaterial integrated optics including efficient grating couplers on silicon nitride, optical antennas and phased arrays, as well as polarization-independent Bragg filters.

talks.title: Tu3-B2: Hollow Core Photonic Crystal Fibre: Perfect Light Pipe?
talks.abstract:
Authors: Russell, Philip

In the tutorial I plan to briefly review the history of hollow-core PCF, explore its many applications, and outline how “glancing incidence optics” has revolutionised hollow-core fibre design.

sessions.title: Tu3-D Integrated modulators
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: Tu3-D1: 400-Gb/s PAM4 Operation of an InP-on-Si Membrane EA Modulator Sub-Assembly with 1.0-V Differential Swing Voltage
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nishizaki, Kensho / Nagashima, Kazuya / Mogi, Takashi / Hiraki, Tatsurou / Fujii, Takuro / Aihara, Takuma / Maeda, Yoshiho / Takai, Yusaku / Yoneyama, Sho / Kimoto, Tatsuya / Nasu, Hideyuki / Kotoku, Masaki / Sato, Tomonari / Matsuo, Shinji

We demonstrate a 400-Gb/s PAM4 operation of a differential drive membrane electro-absorption modulator (EAM) sub-assembly with 1.0-V differential amplitude. 3-dB electro-optic bandwidth of >110 GHz is realized owing to a low capacitance 150-µm-long EAM flip-chip-bonded ceramic substrate as well as an integrated 80-ohm differential termination.

talks.title: Tu3-D2: Flip-chip Integrated Differential Drive EML with Dual Modulator Structure with AC-coupling for 226 Gb/s
talks.abstract:
Authors: Masuyama, Kei / Shirao, Mizuki / Okuda, Shinya / Higashide, Seiu / Matsumori, Kishin / Ohata, Nobuo

We report a flip-chip-mounted EML with a dual-EAM structure on an interposer, together with differential termination and an AC-coupling capacitor. The device exhibits >60 GHz 3-dB electro-optic bandwidth and 226 Gb/s back-to-back operation at 113-GBaud PAM4 with 2.8-dB TDECQ.

talks.title: Tu3-D3: A Mach–Zehnder Modulator Exceeding 110 GHz in a 300 mm Silicon Photonic Platform towards 400 Gbps/lane Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jia, Erse / Lu, Yanxiang / Zhao, Xinran / Li, Jun / Cai, Haiwen / Yang, Fenghe / Chu, Wei

A 420 Gbps PAM-8 Mach-Zehnder modulator with a compact footprint of 500 μm is demonstrated in a 300 mm silicon photonic platform, achieving an insertion loss of 5.6 dB, an electro-optic bandwidth exceeding 110 GHz, and a modulation efficiency of 0.49 V∙cm around 1310 nm.

talks.title: Tu3-D4: Energy-Efficient Optical Chiplet Link with Heterogeneously Integrated Membrane EA-DFB Laser Achieving 1.55 pJ/bit at 64-Gbit/s PAM-4
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yamaoka, Suguru / Hiraki, Tatsurou / Minotani, Tadashi / Shikama, Yoshiya / Kiyozawa, Tomomasa / Taguchi, Tomoya / Aihara, Takuma / Maeda, Yoshiho / Fujii, Takuro / Tsujita, Yuichi / Sato, Tomonari / Matsuo, Shinji
