We demonstrate a transmitter chiplet integrating a low-capacitance InGaAsP electro-absorption modulator and a membrane InGaAsP laser on a Si platform, co-integrated with an electronic IC through flip-chip bonding. Together with a Ge receiver chiplet, a 1.55-pJ/bit optical link at 64-Gbit/s PAM-4 is achieved.

talks.title: Tu3-D5: Zero-Post-Processing Micro-Transfer-Printed Heterogeneous Si/TFLN Mach-Zehnder Modulators with >67-GHz Bandwidth
talks.abstract:
Authors: Murai, Toshiya / Kou, Rai / Yamashita, Yohei / Takabayashi, Kazumasa / Imai, Masahiko / Meisaichi, Kohei / Makino, Shuntaro / Yamamoto, Noritsugu

We micro-transfer-print fully pre-fabricated thin-film lithium niobate modulators, incorporating RF CPW electrodes and SiO2 cladding, onto a silicon platform using a Mo sacrificial layer. Eliminating post-printing fabrication, the 3-mm-long device achieves a 3-dB bandwidth exceeding 67 GHz, enabling scalable integration.

talks.title: Tu3-D6: A 150-GBaud PAM2, 120-GBaud PAM4 Monolithic Transmitter Integrating a Silicon-Photonic Mach–Zehnder Modulator and a CMOS Driver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fang, Jiaqin / Ke, Jiacong / Weckenmann, Erwan / Shi, Wei / Shekhar, Sudip

We demonstrate a monolithically integrated optical transmitter consisting of a 46-GHz silicon photonic Mach-Zehnder modulator and a CMOS-SOI driver with on-chip continuous-time linear equalization. The measured E/O bandwidth is 70 GHz, with BERs below HD-FEC at 240-Gb/s PAM4 and 150-Gb/s PAM2.

sessions.title: Tu3-E Digital twin and autonomous network intelligence
sessions.track: SC 10: Control and management of optical networks

talks.title: Tu3-E1: A Robust Scalable Markov Chain Monte Carlo Approach for a Probabilistic Digital Twin of Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rinaldi, Davide / Ramantanis, Petros / Massaro, Antonio / Aghasaryan, Armen

We propose a method of refining the optical network parameters joint probability distribution, leveraging live measurements and integrating a differentiable reimplementation of GNPy into a Bayesian inference framework. We illustrate the benefits of our approach in terms of robustness and quality of the predicted distributions.

talks.title: Tu3-E2: Experimental Demonstration of Autonomous Class Aware Optimization via Digital Twin Aided Optical Network Agent
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lawson, Marc / Purkayastha, Ambashri / Delezoide, Camille / Sgambelluri, Andrea / Boitier, Fabien / Sambo, Nicola / Layec, Patricia

We demonstrate a Digital Twin-aided multi-agent LLM for autonomous class-aware optical network management on a network testbed. The system detects soft failures and autonomously adapts modulation format per service class requirements, ensuring marginless channel quality with minimal human intervention.

talks.title: Tu3-E3: ROADM and AI: a Perfect Symbiosis for Autonomous Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Morea, Annalisa / Dicorato, Giuseppe / Lonardi, Matteo / Momtahan, Paul

This article examines how AI is reshaping optical transport networks by driving architectural innovations to meet surging data center interconnect demands, while simultaneously enabling intelligent, agentic network automation frameworks that optimize operations, reduce costs, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

talks.title: Tu3-E4: Collaborative Measurement-Driven Digital Twin with Data Extrapolation for DRL-assisted Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Teng, Yiran / Yang, Ruizhi / Shen, Sen / Liu, Yuelin / Zhao, Wanxin / Mehrpooya, Ali / Yokar, Vaigai / Wang, Rui / Yan, Shuangyi / Simeonidou, Dimitra

We present a measurement-driven digital twin framework that integrates multiple lab-based emulations with AI-based extrapolation, offering a practical approach to data-driven digital twin construction. Using 5% measured data, it achieves below 0.05 dB error and enables DRL-based spectrum allocation with 0.4 dB Q-factor improvement.

talks.title: Tu3-E5: Experimental Demonstration of a Digital-Twin-Based Risk Map for Proactive Management of Fiber Flapping in a Mesh Network
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Chenyu / Chen, Yilong / Stavrou, Photios A. / Pointurier, Yvan / Charlet, Gabriel

We experimentally demonstrate a digital-twin-based framework simulates “what-if” fiber flapping and power dips across a mesh optical network, generates risk maps, and recommends proactive adjustments of inline amplifier gain or booster launch power profile to pre-compensate potential degradations, enhancing end-to-end SNR margin and network resilience.

sessions.title: Tu3-F AI for 6G and 6G for AI
Tu3-G Turbulence-resilient underwater optical wireless links
sessions.track: SC 09: Free-space optics and optical wireless technologies

talks.title: Tu3-G1 Optical wireless communications - progress and challenges
Tu3-G2: Blind Turbulence Mitigation Based on Ultra-Low-Latency Energy-Efficient Photonic Computing Processor: A Field Trial for Real-Time Underwater Links with 6D-AUV
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Geyang / Wang, Yuxin / ruan, Jiacheng / Zhang, Weipeng / Lederman, Joshua C. / Sun, Caiming / shatri, Bhavin J. / Chen, Lian-Kuan / Prucnal, Paul R.

We demonstrate a CSI-free blind turbulence-whitening equalizer (BTWE) using a novel compact modulation-and-weighting microring resonator-based photonic computing processor. Through 6D-AUV underwater field trials, photonic BTWE achieved orders-of-magnitude lower latency and energy consumption compared to advanced DSP with ~50% data-rate enhancement, successfully mitigating turbulence-induced power fluctuations.

talks.title: Tu3-G3: Turbulence-Resilient Self-Aligned Bidirectional Optical Wireless Using Optical Phase Conjugation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Zhaoming / Trichili, Abderrahmen / Faulkner, Grahame / Farmer, James / O'Brien, Dominic

We demonstrate a bi-directional OWC link in which an optical phase-conjugate uplink provides automatic alignment and turbulence compensation, enabling a reverse high-speed downlink that achieves a 10.1-Gb/s peak throughput while sustaining Gb/s-class transmission over an optical power equivalent distance of 80 m.

talks.title: Tu3-G4: Downlink-Assisted Uplink Beam Steering in an Asymmetric Underwater Optical Attocell for Turbulence-Resilient Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Miyamoto, Haruto / Kuzuhara, Daiki / Kuwahara, Kiichiro / Mitani, Kaho / Maekawa, Komei / Kodama, Takahiro

An asymmetric underwater optical attocell is proposed to mitigate the coverage-efficiency trade-off in underwater wireless optical communication. Downlink diffusive beams enable extended cell formation, while uplink beam steering exploits positional information. Experiments demonstrate turbulence-resilient coverage and stable communication throughout the attocell for mobile nodes.

talks.title: Tu3-G5: Underwater WDM-VLC Systems Enabled by Ultrafast Perovskite Superlattice and SiPMs Receiver Array
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xu, Zengyi / Chen, Zhiwu / Feng, Zhe / Hu, Zhuoran / Wang, Yunkai / Yang, Peng / Wang, Congcong / Li, Jingzhou / Chi, Nan

We proposed an underwater WDM-VLC system, combining a multi-wavelength laser transmitter and a large area receiver with ultrafast fluorescent antenna (FA) and SiPM array. The system achieves 117.6 Gbps⋅mm2capacity-area product in the 1.2 m tap water channel.

sessions.title: Tu3-C Microwave photonics and sensing
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: Tu3-C1: 280-Gbps Rx-DSP-Free Coherent Analog-RoF Fronthaul Enabled by Hybrid Optical-Electrical Frequency Combs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wen, Yiming / Xie, Xiangyu / Huang, Chuanming / Xue, Rui / Xu, Kai / Xia, Yu / Cheng, Mengfan / Yang, Qi / Liu, Deming / Deng, Lei

We demonstrate an Rx-DSP-free coherent A-RoF fronthaul using hybrid optical-electrical frequency combs to enable self-heterodyne detection and pre-equalization, mitigating laser phase noise and transmitter impairments. 5 channels of 14-GBaud 16-QAM signals with 22-GHz carrier frequency are successfully transmitted over a 10-km fiber link.

talks.title: Tu3-C2: Acoustic Imaging for 2D Tracking of Surface Vessels Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing on Submarine Optical Fibres
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mejías, Felipe / San Martín, Sebastián / Carrasco, Gonzalo / Zañartu, Matías / Soto, Marcelo A.

This paper presents a beamforming-based method using fibre-optic distributed acoustic sensing to map acoustic energy in two dimensions around submarine telecom fibres. The method enables near-field 2D localisation via beamforming and tracking through Kalman filtering of moving marine vessels, including regions without direct fibre deployment.

talks.title: Tu3-C3: Optical path difference measurements using symmetric dual-comb interferometry
talks.abstract:
Authors: Romero Barrueco, Alonso / Mateu-Comas, Julia / Soriano-Amat, Miguel / Quevedo-Galán, Clara / Matin-Lopez, Sonia / Gonzalez-Herraez, Miguel / Fernández-Ruiz, María R.

We present a common-path dual-comb technique for long-distance fiber ranging, addressing coherence and ambiguity limitations. Spectral phase retrieval combined with multi-Nyquist-zone pro-cessing enables measurements up to 102 km with 5.6 mm resolution.

talks.title: Tu3-C4: Quantitative Evaluation of Localised Fibre Loss in Multicore Fibre Systems Using Coherent OTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Komatsu, Kosuke / Ishida, Kodai / Beppu, Shohei / Soma, Daiki / Sumita, Seiya / Fukushima, Taiki / Takahashi, Hidenori / Inohara, Ryo / Wakayama, Yuta / Tsuritani, Takehiro

We quantitatively evaluate localised fibre loss in two-core fibre systems using coherent OTDR. Better than ±1-dB agreement with power meter measurements is confirmed for two distinct configurations, with and without high-loss loopbacks. Operational advantages and disadvantages of each configuration are also clarified.

sessions.title: Tu3-H Long-haul HCF systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: Tu3-H1: Hollow-Core Fibre Transmission Systems: From Metro to Long-Haul Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hong, Yang / Ali, Abdallah / Kamalian-Kopae, Morteza / Gholizadeh, Baset / Gorajoobi, Shahab Bakhtiari / Hooley, James / Bawn, Simon / Fokoua, Eric Numkam / Chen, Yong / Wallace, Colin / Gaudette, Jamie / Richardson, David / Puttnam, Benjamin

We review recent advances in high‑capacity optical transmission that exploit the unique beneficial properties of hollow‑core fibres (HCFs). Single‑span metro, multi‑span long‑distance, and long‑haul transmission scenarios are discussed, together with opportunities and challenges towards future HCF‑based transmission systems.

talks.title: Tu3-H2: Impact of Gas Line Absorption in Long-Haul transmission of 134 GBd Signals in C-Band over Low Loss and Low IMI HCF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Boddeda, Rajiv / Castineiras Carrero, Carina / Mardoyan, Haïk / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein / S. B. Ospina, Ruby / Li, Peng / Li, Shuhai / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Renaudier, Jeremie

We report on the C-band WDM transmission of 134-GBd channels using DP-16QAM and DP-64QAM over long-haul distances. Using a recirculating loop comprising of a single span made of 266-km of GTA‑ST‑HCF, we show the impact of gas line absorption on SC and MC modulation schemes.

talks.title: Tu3-H3: On the Impact of Gas-Line Absorption in Long-Haul C+L-Band Hollow-Core Fibre Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gan, Zelin / Sillekens, Eric / Yang, Jiaqian / Sohanpal, Ronit / Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Aparecido, Romulo / Killey, Robert / Bayvel, Polina

We numerically investigate gas-line absorption in hollow-core fibre C+L-band transmission. Results show limited C-band but severe L-band performance degradation. Ideal suppression enables a 1.5× higher L-band throughput, reaching 59.1 Tb/s over 1000~km, while reducing repeater number by up to 3.3×.

talks.title: Tu3-H4: Demonstration of Full C-band 400G ZR Transmission over 3-Span 427.97-km Hollow-Core Fibre
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hong, Yang / Gholizadeh, Baset / Hooley, James / Ali, Abdallah / Kamalian-Kopae, Morteza / Wallace, Colin / Gaudette, Jamie / Richardson, David / Puttnam, Benjamin

We experimentally demonstrate 400G ZR transmission over record reach thanks to the ultra-low nonlinearity and low-and-flat chromatic dispersion of hollow-core fibre (HCF). Using 34.5-dBm launch powers, real-time full C-band 400G ZR transmission over 3 spans with a maximum 427.97-km reach is demonstrated.

talks.title: Tu3-H5: Fundamental Quantum Limits of Power-Constrained Multi-Span Fiber-Optic Transmission: HCF vs Conventional Fibers
talks.abstract:
Authors: lukanowski, Karol / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein / Jarzyna, Marcin / Banaszek, Konrad

We explore fundamental quantum limits on the system capacity of multi-span HCF and standard silica-based fiber links in the power-constrained regime, comparing phase-sensitive and phase-insensitive amplifiers and Shannon vs Gordon-Holevo capacity.

sessions.title: Tu3-I Quantum state transmission and manipulation
sessions.track: SC 11: Quantum communications, physical layer security, and optical quantum technologies

talks.title: Tu3-I1: Air-to-Ground Transmission of Time-Encoded Qubits with Single-Mode Fiber Coupling for Terrestrial Network Compatibility
talks.abstract:
Authors: Widomski, Adam / Renneke, Stephanie / Krause, Jan / Huang, Sheng-Hsuan / Dolejsky, Till / Riester, Carlo / Rothe, Markus / Gebhart, Ingo / Walenta, Nino / Freund, Ronald

We present a demonstration of time-encoded quantum bit transmission over an air-to-ground link between a mobile airborne transmitter and an optical ground station. Our results pave the way to wards constructing secure and flexible hybrid Quantum Key Distribution links beyond currently available fiber-optic topologies.

talks.title: Tu3-I2: Quantum Readout based on Silicon Photonic Integrated Circuits for Enhanced Authentication Security
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mesaritakis, Charis / Sarantoglou, George / Tzekas, Nikolaos / Moustakas, George / Karydis, George-Aias / Kaminski, Veronika / Protsenko, Ekaterina / Gradkowski, Kamil / Bazin, Alexandre / Vigliar, Caterina / Bogris, Adonis

In this work, we present a quantum-driven physical unclonable function based on a silicon nitride photonic integrated chip, offering enhanced authentication security against eavesdropping. The maximally mixed state property conceals the hardware fingerprint, while a cloning probability as low as 10^-14 provides secure authentication

talks.title: Tu3-I3: Quantum Advantage with Continuous Variable Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Andersen, Ulrik Lund

In this talk, I will present our efforts to leverage CV optical quantum systems for achieving quantum advantage in learning, communication, and computation. Highlights include demonstrations of massive quantum advantage in quantum learning, progress toward quantum computational advantage, and recent advances in practical CVQKD.

talks.title: Tu3-I4: Measurement-Based Quantum Kernel Method for Data Classification on a Reprogrammable Silicon Photonic Device
talks.abstract:
Authors: Raschendorfer, Veronika / Alnor Christensen, Anton / Nikolaj Thomas, Zinner / Da Ros, Francesco / Vigliar, Caterina

We demonstrate a measurement-based quantum kernel estimation protocol on a reprogrammable silicon photonic chip. Using path-encoded four-qubit graph states, we achieve 90% classification accuracy. This provides a scalable, noise-resilient framework for quantum machine learning ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: Tu3-I5: Experimental Quantification of Layered Error Suppression in Fiber-Interconnected Quantum Data Centers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Elyasi, Seyed Navid / Bahrani, Sima / Wang, Rui / Simeonidou, Dimitra / Monti, Paolo / Lin, Rui

We perform experiments to quantify error suppression in fiber-connected superconducting QPUs using combined error mitigation techniques, demonstrating over 20% improvement in operational fidelity across interconnected quantum processing units under realistic noise conditions.

sessions.title: Afternoon coffee break
Tu4-A Access network evolution
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: Tu4-A1: Optical Access Network Evolution and Transformation Enabled by AI
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xu, Fan / Zheng, Zongzhao / Ye, Zhicheng / Wang, Xiang / Zeng, Yan / Liu, Dekun / Lu, Yanzhao / Wu, Xuming

Artificial intelligence has emerged as a key enabler to address challenges such as capacity demand, dynamic resource allocation, and intelligent management through data-drive optimiza tion and adaptive control in Optical Access Network. This paper reviews major aspects and dis cusses future directions for AI-driven OAN.

talks.title: Tu4-A2: 25 Years of PON standardization Tracking the Evolution of Technology and its Market
talks.abstract:
Authors: Effenberger, Frank

Passive optical networks have a long history of standardization that has tracked both the progress of the technology and the development of the broadband market. The goal is to find a good cost-performance trade-off. This paper reviews the major themes of this work.

sessions.title: Tu4-B Optical networks for AI datacenters and workloads
sessions.track: SC 10: Control and management of optical networks

talks.title: Tu4-B1: Dynamic Optical Pluggable Allocation and LLM-aware Job Scheduling for Distributed AI training in Regional Multi-Cluster Data Centers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lohani, Varsha / Muñoz, Raul / Casellas, Ramon

We propose an LLM-aware dynamic optical pluggable allocation for regional multi-cluster data centers, jointly optimizing DCI capacity and job queuing to support heterogeneous distributed AI training workloads, improving utilization, blocking probability, and training efficiency significantly.

talks.title: Tu4-B2: Energy-Efficient Machine Learning-Assisted Load Balancing for Fully Virtualized Access Networks on Multi-Node GPU Servers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Suzuki, Takahiro / Matsumoto, Yasuhiro / Kani, Jun-Ichi / Shimada, Tatsuya

We propose energy-efficient machine learning-assisted load balancing for fully-virtualized OLTs. The nonlinear change in computational load is estimated using a decision tree. Experiments on multi-node GPU servers show a 62% improvement in inference error and power savings of 95% to 98%.

talks.title: Tu4-B3: The Role of Optics in Next-Generation Multi-Gigawatt Datacenters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gangopadhyay, Bodhisattwa / vakili, Arash / Mukherjee, Debottym / Rahn, Jeff

Multi-gigawatt AI datacenters demand optical interconnects scaling from intra-cluster fabrics to inter-building backbone rings under strict power, latency, and reliability constraints. We present the deployed optical architecture spanning disaggregated AI fabrics and metro-ring backbones, covering 2×400G FR4-LITE optics, 800GZR coherent modules, and optical protection switching.

talks.title: Tu4-b4 optical networks for ai: the challenge and optimization for llm training and inference across datacenters

sessions.title: Tu4-D Long-range QKD and fields trials
sessions.track: SC 11: Quantum communications, physical layer security, and optical quantum technologies

talks.title: Tu4-D1 Practical quantum communications in deployed optical telecom networks
Tu4-D2: Field Trial of Commercial 1295-nm O-Band DV-QKD under Coexistence with Classical Channels in a High-Capacity ROADM-based Metropolitan Production Fiber Network
talks.abstract:
Authors: Rivas-Moscoso, José Manuel / Núñez-Bon, Javier / Melgar, Antonio / Armingol, Pablo / Villegas Zannella, Vanessa / Golderos Espadas, Pablo / Penedo, Pedro / Boso, Gianluca / Spitzbart, Daniel / Fröwis, Florian / Cantó Palancar, Rafael / Folgueira, Jesús

We report field deployment of a 1295.56 nm O-band DV-QKD system coexisting with high-capacity C-band traffic in a metropolitan link. Measurements under varying channel allocations and powers show robust coexistence, improved tolerance over 1310 nm operation, and no degradation in classical C-band performance or capacity.

talks.title: Tu4-D3: Field Demonstration of QKD–Classical Coexistence with Real-Time Encryption over Multi-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ramadan, Ibrahim Mohamed / Di Sciullo, Giammarco / Wu, Qi / Ribezzo, Domenico / Ann Shaji, Divya / Alves Zischler, Lucas / S. Luís, Ruben / Serena, Paolo / Lasagni, Chiara / Bononi, Alberto / Hayashi, Tetsuya / Gagliano, Alessandro / Martelli, Paolo / Gatto, Alberto / Parolari, Paola / Boffi, Pierpaolo / Marotta, Andrea / Centofanti, Carlo / Graziosi, Fabio / Mecozzi, Antonio / Antonelli, Cristian

We report the first field trial of quantum key distribution coexisting with classical signals over a fielddeployed multi-core fiber link, achieving 106.7 Tb/s classical transmission alongside real-time networklayer encryption at 132 Gb/s, with 63 µs latency overhead and key-refresh time interval of 15 seconds.

talks.title: Tu4-D4: Field Trials of Restoration-Capable Quantum Key Distribution Networks with Optical Routers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Duan, Xiao / Poh, Hou Shun / Wee, Matthew / Cai, Yu / Haw, Jing Yan / Qin, Hao / Kasper, Michael / Kurtsiefer, Christian / Ling, Alexander

We demonstrate physical-layer failure detection and automated recovery in quantum key distribution ne works utilising commercial prepare-and-measure BB84 and polarisation entanglement-based BBM92 systems integrated with self-developed all-transparent optical routers over a field-deployed network testbed.

talks.title: Tu4-D5: Demonstration of a Dynamic SD-KMS with Batch-Based Multipath Routing in a Field-Deployed QKD Network
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tsimvrakidis, Konstantinos / Selentis, Antonis / Papageorgopoulos, Alkinoos / Papastamatiou, Ilias / Christodoulopoulos, Konstantinos / Kanellos, George

We present a dynamic Software-Defined Key Management System (SD-KMS), integrated with a custom batch-based Linear Programming (LP) routing engine, to optimize dynamic key provision-ing in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) networks. The SD-KMS is experimentally validated across diverse operational scenarios in a field-deployed QKD network.

sessions.title: Tu4-E Mode division multiplexing
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: Tu4-E1: 20-Mode Spatial and Polarization Multiplexer using Vertically Stacked Three-Layer Dielectric Metasurfaces
talks.abstract:
Authors: Suganuma, Takahiro / Ren, Chun / Fontaine, Nicolas / Tsubai, Yusuke / Soma, Go / Tanemura, Takuo

A spatial and polarization multiplexer based on compact stacked metasurfaces is experimentally demonstrated. Using three metasurface layers with 800-μm-diameter aperture, we achieve simultaneous conversion of 20 input beams to the desired Hermite–Gaussian modes at 1550 nm, demonstrating a scalable optical interface for space-division-multiplexed systems.

talks.title: Tu4-E2: Inversely Designed Ultrasmall Scrambling-Type Mode Multiplexer Based on Mosaic Structure
talks.abstract:
Authors: Aomori, Shizunari / Tsuji, Yasuhide / Mitarai, Takuya / Sawada, Yusuke / Okimoto, Takuya / Hiratani, Takuo / Komatsu, Kento / Yagi, Hideki / Fujiwara, Naoki / Fujisawa, Takeshi

We propose and experimentally demonstrate first scrambling-type mode multiplexers based on mosaic structure. Two- and three-mode multiplexers with an ultrasmall footprint of < 10 µm2 are successfully demonstrated with the help of inverse design method based on gradient-based and machine learning techniques.

talks.title: Tu4-E3: Ultrasmall 8-Channel Wavelength/Mode Hybrid Multiplexer with Mosaic Structures for Beyond-Tbit/s Optical Ethernet
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sawada, Yusuke / Fujisawa, Takeshi / Mitarai, Takuya / Komatsu, Kento / Okimoto, Takuya / Hiratani, Takuo / Yagi, Hideki / Fujiwara, Naoki

We demonstrate ultrasmall wavelength/mode hybrid multiplexers for the C- and O-bands. Integrating mosaic structures designed using machine learning enables ultrasmall footprint of 50 × 50 µm2 while maintaining low loss property. To the best of our knowledge, these devices are the smallest for 8-channel multiplexers.

sessions.title: Tu4-F AI for 6G and 6G for AI
Tu4-G Optical sensing in telecommunications networks
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: Tu4-G1: Enhancing Telecommunications Network Availability through Infrastructure Protection with High-Spatial-Resolution Sensing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sandmann, André / Rapp, Lutz / Azendorf, Florian

A framework for increasing optical fiber network availability by integrating high-spatial-resolution distributed fiber sensing in data transmission systems is presented. Coexistence with parallel data channels on a separate wavelength, mitigation of nonlinear signal interaction impacts, applications and challenges are investigated.

talks.title: Tu4-G2: Generalised Bidirectional ODN Characterisation with Unknown Number of Loss Events for Coherent PONs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tan, Chenxi / Ye, Xiaoyan / Savory, Seb

We propose a generalised bidirectional DSP-based framework using adaptive Gaussian process regression and Bayesian information criterion for precise and efficient ODN characterisation in coherent PONs with unknown loss events. Experiments demonstrate accurate dual-loss localisation and quantification, with maximum mean errors of 0.26km and 0.17dB.

talks.title: Tu4-G3: Multipoint Vibration Localization in Forward Coherent ISAC Enabled by Blind Source Separation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yin, Bowen / Shi, Yang / Gao, Yalin / Zhao, Zhiyong / Tang, Ming

We demonstrate multipoint vibration localization in forward ISAC by extracting perturbations directly from the communication signal phase. Leveraging blind source separation, three concurrent vibrations are blindly localized over a 63-km link with meter-level accuracy, alongside penalty-free 30-GBaud 16-QAM transmission.

talks.title: Tu4-G4: Flexible DAS Implementation over a Self-Homodyne Optical Link
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yao, Yucheng / chen, Can / Chen, Junda / Lin, Zhonghong / Zhao, Zhiyong / Tang, Ming / A. Andrekson, Peter / Karlsson, Magnus

We demonstrate a flexible ISAC architecture over a 25-km polarization-division-multiplexed self-homodyne link using a shared continuous frequency-swept carrier, achieving 160-Gbps 16QAM transmission with negligible communication penalty and 30-kHz vibration recovery. High-sampling-rate DAS is realized via continuous-wave sub-band multiplexing, increasing sampling rate 45× without spectral overhead.

talks.title: Tu4-G5: Hybrid Phase and Polarization Sensing Using OIF DSP Frame Pilot Symbols and Training Sequences in Integrated Receivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhou, Hao / Yang, Fan / Tang, Du / Zuo, Wen / Li, Zekai / Jiang, Yingjie / Quan, Baoxuan / Zhou, Yutao / Xu, Hengying / Bai, Chenglin / Qiao, Yaojun

A hybrid feedforward phase and polarization sensing architecture is proposed for integrated coherent receivers with 100-kHz ECLs, directly utilizing OIF-defined DSP frame pilot symbols and training sequences. By adaptively selecting modalities based on frequency-dependent sensing SNR, we achieve sub-Hz-to-10-MHz vibration detection for fiber-ISAC optical networks.

sessions.title: Tu4-H Impairments monitoring in optical networks
sessions.track: SC 06: Architecture, modelling and performance of optical networks

talks.title: Tu4-H1: Estimation of Nonlinear Intra- and Inter-Channel Impairments in Optical Fiber Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Girard-Jollet, Joana / Shi, Lina / Boitier, Fabien / Delezoide, Camille / Antona, Jean-Christophe / Layec, Patricia

We propose a neural network to estimate the relative contributions of intra- and inter-channel nonlinear impairments in fiber optic transmission from received-signal power spectral densities. Trained and tested on experimental data, the model achieves 1% RMSE across varying launch powers, symbol rates, and transmission distances.

talks.title: Tu4-H2: First Distributed PDL Monitoring on Coherent DSP Chip in Pluggable Transceiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Takahashi, Minami / Sasai, Takeo / Yamazaki, Etsushi

We demonstrate the first experimental localization and quantification of distributed PDL, fully implemented on a coherent DSP in a 118-GBd OSFP transceiver. Over a WDM link, on-chip digital-SOP-optimized polarization-resolved power profiles identify multiple PDL elements solely from ZR+ traffic signals, with <1.0-dB estimation error.

talks.title: Tu4-H3: First Implementation of NLI Estimation on Coherent DSP Enabled by On-Chip Longitudinal Power Monitoring
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sasai, Takeo / Yamazaki, Etsushi

We report the first implementation of NLI estimation on a real-time coherent DSP, enabled by on-chip longitudinal power monitoring inside an OSFP. We demonstrate NLI estimation over a 450-km link using only standard 400ZR+ traffic, achieving a 0.62-dB maximum absolute error in generalized OSNR.

talks.title: Tu4-H4: Near-Symbol-Rate Linear Least-Square Longitudinal Power Monitoring
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chang, Junho / Hahn, Choloong / Guo, Qingyi / Jiang, Zhiping

We characterize the dependency of the spatial response function on the waveform sampling rate used for LPM. By proposing an optimized near-symbol-rate approach, we achieve mean absolute error of the estimated profile comparable to 2-SpS processing with lower sampling requirements, supporting more resource-efficient real-time monitoring.

talks.title: Tu4-H5: Generalizable PDL Regression via Transfer Learning in Optical Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shi, Lina / Girard-Jollet, Joana / Boitier, Fabien / Layec, Patricia

We demonstrate transfer learning for PDL regression by adapting a simulation-trained model to experimental data under unseen operating conditions. Across different symbol rates, launch powers, and modulation formats, it consistently outperforms a source-only baseline, demonstrating robust cross-domain generalization with few target samples.

Tu5-C Hack your research! Tools and tricks for today’s telecommunications techies
Morning coffee
We1-A SDM systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: We1-A1 High capacity SDM transmission
We1-A2: 10.33 Pb/s GMI Data-Rate S+C+L Transmission over a Standard-250 μm Coating Diameter, 6-Mode, 7-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gaiani, Stefano / Luís, Ruben S. / Schneck, Julian / Orsuti, Daniele / Sakaime, Katsuyoshi / Chen, Haoshuo / Ryf, Roland / Fontaine, Nicolas K. / Chung, Dicky / Man, Ray / Rademacher, Georg / Boffi, Pierpaolo / Furukawa, Hideaki

We achieve 10.33 Pb/s (GMI-estimated) or 9.72 Pb/s (FEC-decoded) data-rate by transmitting 775, polarization-multiplexed, 256-QAM channels across S+C+L-bands (19.25 THz bandwidth) over a 26.6 km, standard-coating, 6-mode, 7-core fiber with a cladding diameter of 171 μm, which is the lowest reported to date.

talks.title: We1-A3: A Simplified Model for Linear Mode Coupling in Multimode Fibers with Experimental Assessment
talks.abstract:
Authors: Carniello, Paolo / Ferreira, Filipe M. / Barbosa, Fabio A. / Li, Ming-Jun / Hanik, Norbert

We propose a novel surrogate model for linear coupling in graded-index multimode fibers that is computationally more efficient than existing models, and can be tuned through a single measurable parameter. The model is benchmarked numerically and experimentally on a 90-polarization-mode fiber.

sessions.title: We1-B Optical computing
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: We1-B1: Microring Resonators as Neuromorphic Primitives for Optical Computing: Spiking Networks, Complex Perceptrons, and Pho-tonic Preprocessing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pavesi, Lorenzo

Silicon microring resonators are versatile neuromorphic primitives. We present three applications: all-optical spiking networks for sparse signalling, complex photonic perceptrons for link equalization, and reservoir arrays for sensor pre-processing. These architectures leverage nonlinear dynamics and non-fading memory to enable low-latency, high-speed optical computing solutions.

talks.title: We1-B2: 20 GHz In-situ Optical Backpropagation for Training AWGR-based Hyperdimensional Photonic Tensor Cores
talks.abstract:
Authors: Asimopoulos, Odysseas / Kovaios, Stefanos / Tsakyridis, Apostolos / Moralis-Pegios, Miltiadis / Avramelou, Loukia / Passalis, Nikolaos / Tefas, Anastasios / Vyrsokinos, Konstantinos / Pleros, Nikolaos

We demonstrate in-situ optical backpropagation and train a hyperdimensional AWGR-based photonic tensor core, performing both forward and backward MVM operations at 20 GHz and presenting inference accuracies of 93.5% and 81.6% for the Wine and Moons datasets, respectively.

talks.title: We1-B3: Photonic 5D Convolutional Tensor Core Using Time-Wavelength-Space Multiplexing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Wenjia / Guo, Jiayuan / He, Zuyuan

We present the first five-dimensional photonic convolutional tensor core integrating a 2×2×2×4 MRR weighting bank for high-accuracy edge extraction and classification. It achieves a computational density of 179.65 TOPS/mm2, which is 5 times higher than existing photonic programmable accelerators.

talks.title: We1-B4: High-Fidelity Generative Image Reconstruction using a Digital Optical Multiplier
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nay, Pierre / Xia, Chengpeng / Meng, Xiansong / Kim, Kwangwoong / Dong, Po / Cox, Ingemar J. / Lioma, Christina / Hu, Hao / Kong, Deming

We demonstrate generative image reconstruction via digital optical transposed convolution operating at 5 Gbit/s. The system reconstructs 28×28 images from feature maps with a MSE of 3.42×10−5 against ground truth. Comparison with an analog simulation shows greater robustness against noise accumulation.

talks.title: We1-B5: Noise analysis in optical computing systems based on analog bits
talks.abstract:
Authors: López, Raúl / Macho, Andres / Capmany, José

We analyse noise in optical computing systems based on analog bits (anbits) by mapping photocurrent perturbations at the receiver onto the Generalized Bloch Sphere. Our results enable the design of noise-tolerant, high-density anbit constellations in scalable photonic processors for artificial intelligence and machine learning applications.

sessions.title: We1-D THz transmission and sensing
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: We1-D1: Field Trial of 300-GHz THz Signal Transmission over Deployed PBG-HCF Using an Amplifier-Free, Full-Optically Powered RAU for Ultra-Compact, Low-Latency Seamless Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tien Dat, Pham / yoshida, Yuki / Inagaki, Keizo / Sekine, Norihiko / Fujii, Katsumi / kanno, Atsushi / Kawanishi, Tetsuya / Akahane, Kouichi / Yamamoto, Naokatsu / Takagi, Takeshi / Mukasa, Kazunori / Matsuura, Motoharu / Okamoto, Satoru / Tsuda, Hiroyuki / Yamanaka, Naoaki

We report the first field trial of THz signal transmission over a deployed PBG-HCF link using an amplifier-free, locally power-free RAU. A 50-Gb/s signal was successfully transmitted over 1 km of deployed PBG-HCF and a 120-m, 300-GHz wireless link with full optical powering.

talks.title: We1-D2: On-chip Antenna-Integrated Photonic THz Transmitter for Multi-Band 280-Gbit/s Superchannel Wireless Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Yinjun / Sun, Mingwei / Yue, Zhifeng / Xu, Mengjing / Han, Qingyu / Li, Yaxuan / Dong, Boyu / Sun, Changzheng / Hao, Zhibiao / Wang, Jian / Wang, Lai / Han, Yanjun / Li, Hongtao / Gan, Lin / Chi, Nan / Xiong, Bing / Zhang, Junwen / Luo, Yi

We demonstrate a compact antenna-integrated MUTC-PD THz transmitter enabling multi-band wireless transmission across the W- and D-bands. Simultaneous 36/34-Gbaud 16-QAM superchannel signals achieve a total line rate of 280 Gbit/s after 10-km SSMF delivery and 1-m wireless transmission, validating high-capacity broadband photonic THz operation.

talks.title: We1-D4: Dual chirps for photonic THz hyperspectral imaging with high spectral resolution and scan rate
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fang, Xing / Zhang, Lu / Lyu, Zhidong / Ozolins, Oskars / Pang, Xiaodan / Yu, Xianbin

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a photonic terahertz imaging system based on dual chirped signals, resolving 250-270GHz spectrum within 40 μs with a resolution of 31.25 MHz and leading ultrafast pixel rates for THz hyperspectral imaging.

talks.title: We1-D5: Integrated Antenna-Coupled Photonic Terahertz Spectrum Analyzer with Hz-Level Accuracy on Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gaier, Aleksei / Jülg, Gabriel / Liu, Jiawen / Benea-Chelmus, Ileana-Cristina

We demonstrate an antenna-coupled thin-film lithium niobate photonic spectrum analyzer for wide-span 80–400 GHz spectral analysis with sub-MHz resolution. Optical frequency referencing, together with comb-referenced sampling, enables Hz-accurate frequency readout, establishing an integrated platform for precise characterization of wireless terahertz and millimeter-wave signals.

sessions.title: We1-E Multicore and multimode fibres, devices and characterisation
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: We1-E1: Statistical Characterization of Spatial and Polarization Mode Coupling in Field-Deployed Coupled-core Multi-core Fibers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Raj, Manish / Zischler, Lucas Alves / Di Sciullo, Giammarco / Hayashi, Tetsuya / Mecozzi, Antonio / Antonelli, Cristian / Karlsson, Magnus

We experimentally investigate spatial and polarization mode coupling dynamics in field-deployed coupled-core multi-core fibers in both time and frequency domains. We observe that the fiber exhibits similar isotropic probability density functions in both domains, with spatial modes decorrelating faster in time than polarization modes.

talks.title: We1-E2: Detecting Longitudinal Variations of Spatial Mode Dispersion in Coupled-Core Multicore Fibers via Four-Wave Mixing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lasagni, Chiara / Serena, Paolo / Zischler, Lucas / Di Sciullo, Giammarco / Mecozzi, Antonio / Antonelli, Cristian / Bononi, Alberto

We propose a method for spatially-resolved estimation of the spatial mode dispersion (SMD) coefficient in coupled-core multicore fibers, exploiting the dependence of four-wave mixing on the local SMD. Results from simulations and measurements confirm the ability of the method to detect anomalous longitudinal SMD variations.

talks.title: We1-E3: Experimental Observation of Modal-Dispersion-Induced FWM Efficiency Increase and Non-linearity Coefficient Characterization in Deployed Coupled-Core Multi-Core Fibers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Alves Zischler, Lucas / Lasagni, Chiara / Raj, Manish / Di Sciullo, Giammarco / Karlsson, Magnus / Serena, Paolo / Bononi, Alberto / Hayashi, Tetsuya / Mecozzi, Antonio / Antonelli, Cristian

We experimentally observe enhanced four-wave mixing efficiency induced by spatial-mode dispersion at large channel spacing in a field-deployed coupled-core 4-core fiber, consistent with the theory. We characterize the MCF effective non-linearity coefficient, demonstrating a 4.26-fold reduction against a co-deployed single-mode fiber.

talks.title: We1-E4: Long-Range Birefringence Characterization in a Field-Deployed Uncoupled-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Romero Ponce, Loreto Valentina / Cappelletti, Martina / Antonelli, Cristian / Mecozzi, Antonio / Di Sciullo, Giammarco / Hayashi, Tetsuya / Galtarossa, Andrea / Schenato, Luca / Palmieri, Luca

Distributed birefringence measurements are presented for a field-deployed 4-core uncoupled-core fiber. Using polarization-sensitive OFDR with section-wise compensation, we achieve kilometer-scale birefringence characterization and observe strong inter-core correlation of the local birefringence vector over the full reconstructed distance. Bidirectional probing at the midsection corroborates measurement reliability.

sessions.title: We1-F ITU-T ION-2030: Architectures and standards of optical networks for the AI era
We1-G DSP-based optical network monitoring
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: We1-G1: Tens-Meter-Level Least Squares Longitudinal Power Monitoring:A Truncated Singular Value Decomposition Method
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Yichao / Ge, Peiyun / Sun, Tianrun / Zhang, Yu / Zhao, Jiarun / Xi, Lixia / Xu, Hengying / Bai, Chenglin / Zhang, Xiaoguang

A tens-meter-level single-channel least-squares longitudinal power monitoring scheme is proposed. By incorporating the truncated singular value decomposition method assisted by a window function, the proposed scheme achieves estimation step sizes at 50 m and 75 m in the 80-GBaud simulated and experimental systems, respectively.

talks.title: We1-G2: Practical Implementation of Power Profile estimation with Reduced complexity and Pre-FEC data
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jiang, Yingjie / Tang, Du / Zhang, Fan / Xu, Hengying / Bai, Chenglin / Yang, Aiying / Qiao, Yaojun

We demonstrate practical power profile estimation with preserved fidelity using symbol-rate data and fewer step size numbers to reduce complexity, and pre-FEC data to remove the need for ideal transmitted data, validated in an 80-GBaud DP-16QAM 5-span experiment.

talks.title: We1-G3: Highly Sensitive and Phase-Noise-Tolerant Multipath Interference Localization in IM/DD Systems by Block-based SNC
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Shen / Lin, Hong / Li, Chenjin / Nie, Junyuan / Zhou, Jiahao / Hu, Shaohua / Zhang, Jing / Qiu, Kun

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a phase-noise-tolerant block-based SNC (BSNC) method for MPI localization. This method detects MPI even at a 40-dB SIR, achieving a 14-dB sensitivity improvement. The estimation exhibits a positive correlation with MPI intensity to enable reliable in-service early fault warning.

talks.title: We1-G4: Localization of Heterogeneous Fiber Type Using Inverse Scattering Transform
talks.abstract:
Authors: Takagi, Ryoske / Motomura, Takumi / Oda, Shoichiro / Yoshida, Yuki / Furukawa, Hideaki / Maruta, Akihiro / Mishina, Ken

We demonstrate the first inverse scattering transform-based method for localizing heterogeneous fiber spans in optical links. Experimental and simulation results show accurate NZ-DSF span identification with dispersion parameter estimation error below 1 ps/nm/km.

talks.title: We1-G5: Digital Signal Processing for Longitudinal Power Monitoring and Nonlinear Interference Estimation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pilori, Dario

Longitudinal Power Monitoring (LPM) enables DSP-based receiver-side reconstruction of the optical power evolution. This paper reviews recent LPM techniques and implementations, and demonstrates its use for nonlinear interference estimation and span-wise power optimization, enabling accurate, model-light, and scalable performance monitoring in real-world optical networks.

sessions.title: We1-C Advanced integrated modulators and transmitters
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: We1-C1: Over 110 GHz Bandwidth Differential Drive EML with Flip Chip Bonding Technique for 400G/lane Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Maekawa, Kyohei / Oe, Hideki / Nakajima, Fumihiro / Kawano, Taketo / Saito, Kosuke / Honda, Masahiro / Hara, Hiroshi / Shoji, Daisei

A wideband differential drive EML using face-up mounting and flip chip bonding is reported. 3 dB bandwidth exceeds 110 GHz, with simulation indicating 123 GHz. It achieved 3.63 dB extinction ratio and 2.43 dB TDECQ at 180 Gbd PAM4 with 1.5 Vpp differential drive.

talks.title: We1-C2: Low-polarization-dependent Membrane InP-based Electro-absorption Modulator on Si Photonics Platform
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hiraki, Tatsurou / Aihara, Takuma / Maeda, Yoshiho / Fujii, Takuro / Sugiyama, Hiroki / Sato, Tomonari / Matsuo, Shinji

We demonstrate a low-polarization-dependent membrane InP electro-absorption modulator on Si photonic circuits. The device exhibits a polarization-dependent insertion loss below 1 dB. PAM4 operation at 256 and 300 Gbps is demonstrated for TE, TM, and mixed polarization, with extinction ratios of 3.0-3.4 and 3.2-3.7 dB.

talks.title: We1-C3: Reconfigurable Integrated Photonics for Massively Scaling AI Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bergman, Keren

High-performance systems are limited by the energy and bandwidth of data movement, with off-chip links lagging on-chip communication by orders of magnitude. Integrated silicon photonics ena-bles ultra-broadband, low-power DWDM links, supporting petabit/s chip escape and reconfigurable ar-chitectures that unify connectivity and accelerate distributed AI/ML workloads.

talks.title: We1-C4: Demonstration of 310 Gb/s PAM4 Operation for a Dual-modulator Differential Electro-Absorption Integrated Laser Diode on an AC-terminated Sub-mount
talks.abstract:
Authors: Uchiyama, Asami / Shirao, Mizuki / Terao, Kenichi / Okuda, Shinya / Katsumi, Shunto / Ohata, Nobuo / Matsuda, Keisuke

We demonstrate 155 Gbaud PAM4 (310 Gb/s) operation of a dual-modulator differential EML with AC termination, achieving a clear optical eye with measured TDECQ of 2.1 dB. A small-footprint AC termination using a single capacitor experimentally showed an 80 GHz bandwidth comparable to DC-terminated designs.

talks.title: We1-C5: Demonstration of an Optical I/Q Modulator Using Surface-Normal Electroabsorption Modulators
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Haoshuo / Huynh, Tam / Hu, Ting-Chen / Fontaine, Nicolas K. / Ryf, Roland / Grillanda, Stefano / Dallachiesa, Lauren / Kim, Kwangwoong / Liu, Yang / Iannone, Pat / Simsarian, Jesse E. / Essiambre, Rene / Mazur, Mikael / Xu, Xiaonan / Earnshaw, Mark / Neilson, David T. / Zheng, Aihu / Wang, Liangliang

We experimentally demonstrate a broadband optical I/Q modulator based on compact surface-normal electroabsorption modulators (SNEAMs).
The device exhibits a wide operating wavelength range, reduced footprint, and temperature insensitivity, making it well suited for high-density integration and a promising candidate for co-packaged optics applications.

sessions.title: We1-H Digital signal processing & equalization for PON
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: We1-H1: Equalization and FEC Evaluation Beyond D/E2 Class 50G-PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Anet Neto, Luiz / Chevalier, Dylan / Simon, Gaël / Inglés, Lucas / Potet, Jérémy / Saliou, Fabienne / Chanclou, Philippe

We experimentally assess different equalization schemes allowing optical power budgets beyond 41 dB post-LDPC(17280,14592) decoding in 50G-PON. We also investigate decoder performances in terms of the number of needed iterations on average and assess the accuracy of pre-FEC threshold estimations when compared to post-FEC measurements.

talks.title: We1-H2: Dual Line Coherent Detection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Castro, Nelson / Li, Yiming / Patel, Mohammed / Smyth, Frank / Turitsyn, Sergei / Ellis, Andrew

We experimentally demonstrate dual-line coherent detection using an optical frequency comb local oscillator, enabling large frequency offset tolerance with minimal additional signal processing. The proposed method achieves 200 GHz offset tolerance for 400 Gbit/s signals with low penalty, supporting uncooled, low-cost coherent transceivers.

talks.title: We1-H3: An Exploratory Study of RS Decoding and Equalization in 50G-PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chevalier, Dylan / Anet Neto, Luiz / Simon, Gaël / Potet, Jeremy / Saliou, Fabienne / Scalart, Pascal / Inglès, Lucas / Chanclou, Philippe

We investigate whether XGS -PON RS(248,216) FEC combined with stronger equalization can support 50G-PON optical power budgets with reduced ONU complexity. Experimental results show that MLSE+RS achieves performance equivalent to aFFE+HI-LDPC, while DFE+RS operates within 0.6 dB over 25 km without iterative decoding.

talks.title: We1-H4: DSP-Based Mitigation of Extreme DC Leakage for 100G/200G Coherent PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Haipeng / Jia, Zhensheng

We analyze DC leakage in coherent TDM-PON burst transmitters and demonstrate three mitigations: a frequency-domain adaptive notch, an IF-based transmitter with digital band-pass filter, and an IF plus Rx EO-edge prefilter. Experiments at 30-GBd DP-QPSK/16QAM show leakage tolerance improved from −47.1 dBm to −5.1 dBm.

talks.title: We1-H5: Integrated Hybrid 50G DD and 200G Coherent PON with a Shared OLT based on 67-GHz TFLN MZM and Bias Optimization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hu, Yimin / Zhu, Yixiao / Zhang, Ziheng / Huang, Luyao / Zhang, Dezhi / Jiang, Ming / Hu, Weisheng

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a hybrid DD-Coherent PON, leveraging single ultra-wideband TFLN MZM-based OLT and frequency-division multiplexing. The trade-off between bias voltage and signal power ratio are optimized. The architecture simultaneously supports 50-Gb/s OOK and 200-Gb/s 16-QAM signals at DD and coherent ONUs, respectively.

talks.title: We1-H6: Demonstration of 50-Gbps SSB DCPC Transmission for Over-40-km-Reach and 1:512-Split PON Using Remotely Pumped BiDi-EDFA and Distributed Raman Amplification
talks.abstract:
Authors: Koma, Ryo / Hara, Kazutaka / Uchiyama, Jin / Kani, Jun-Ichi / Shimada, Tatsuya

We propose a long‑reach, high‑splitting‑ratio PON using bidirectional remotely pumped EDFA and Raman amplification. Upstream and downstream 50‑Gb/s transmission experiments in L- and C-bands confirm feasibility of over 40–60 km reach and split ratios of up to 1:512.

sessions.title: We1-I Quantum networks
sessions.track: SC 11: Quantum communications, physical layer security, and optical quantum technologies

talks.title: We1-I1: Long-Distance Entanglement Distribution Between Integrated Silicon Photonic Chips
talks.abstract:
Authors: Roux, Damien / Guarda, Giulia / Zahidy, Mujtaba / Ding, Yunhong / Zhou, Siyan / Ribezzo, Domenico / Munkhbat, Battulga / Da Ros, Francesco / Bacco, Davide / Vigliar, Caterina

Phase decoherence prevents long-distance path-encoded entanglement distribution. We report chip-to-chip entanglement-based QKD between silicon photonic chips over an 80-km multicore fiber link. Stabilized via a phase-locked loop, we achieve an 85.7% Bell state fidelity and 2.03 bits/s secure key rate.

talks.title: We1-I2: Quantum Teleportation of Weak Coherent Polarization States on a Metropolitan Fiber Network in Coexistence With Classical Traffic
talks.abstract:
Authors: Borowska, Zofia Anna / Andrewski, Shane / De Pascalis, Giorgio / Flament, Mael / Geitz, Marc / Holschke, Oliver / Namazi, Mehdi / Sena, Matheus / Brasher, Olivia

We demonstrate polarization-encoded quantum teleportation on Deutsche Telekom’s metropolitan fiber testbed using commercial devices over a 30 km deployed-fiber loop. An average fidelity of 91.4±3.1% is achieved over 30 km, and 91.3±2.6% while co-propagating live classical traffic, confirming compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.

talks.title: We1-I3: Field Trial of a Four-User Entanglement Distribution Network for QKD over Deployed Metropolitan Fiber Using a Commercial Photon Source
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sommermeier, Sarah / Getselev, Tomi / Walenta, Nino / Perlot, Nicolas / Freund, Ronald

We demonstrate simultaneous BBM92 quantum key distribution between user pairs in a four -user network over 13.8 km deployed fiber. Using a single commercial entanglement source, wavelength-division multiplexing and White Rabbit synchronization, we achieve 2–2.5 % QBER and 40–54 bit/s secret-key rates.

talks.title: We1-I4: Single-Copy Entanglement Distillation via Hyperentanglement for Raman-Resilient Quantum Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ribezzo, Domenico / Guarda, Giulia / Zavatta, Alessandro / Bacco, Davide

We demonstrate a practical single-copy distillation protocol for hyperentangled states to enhance QKD resilience against Raman noise in shared fibers. By exploiting frequency-domain correlations, we achieve a 4~dB increase in maximum classical launch power tolerance during co-existence with genuine, co-propagating telecom traffic.

talks.title: We1-I5: A Quantum Internet Based on Solid-State Quantum Nodes
talks.abstract:
Authors: Grandi, Samuele / Distante, Emanuele

We present ARQ's approach to a deployable quantum internet: rack-compatible quantum repeaters based on solid-state rare-earth memories interfaced with telecom-band entanglement sources. We discuss how native multidimensional multiplexing in this architecture enables high-rate memory-memory entanglement distribution.

sessions.title: Coffee break
We2-A Advancements on optical fiber transmission
sessions.track: SC 06: Architecture, modelling and performance of optical networks

talks.title: We2-A1: Optical fibre communications and network innovations: the past 60 years and what the future holds
talks.abstract:
Authors: Davey, Russell

This tutorial reviews the history and vital role of optical fibre communications from a BT perspective and speculates what the future may hold.

talks.title: We2-A2: Mixed-Signal Transmission for Long-Haul High-Capacity Optical Paths and Low Latency Optical Paths Using DSF Transmission Line and Inter-Band Wavelength Conversion Technology
talks.abstract:
Authors: Matsuda, Toshiya / Cruzado, Kenji / Fukatani, Takafumi / Seki, Takeshi / Shimizu, Shimpei / Abe, Masashi / Kazama, Takushi / Enbutsu, Koji / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Umeki, Takeshi / Miyamoto, Yutaka / Hayashi, Rie

We propose mixed-signal transmission that utilises the DSF to directly transmit low-latency optical paths without dispersion compensation, while converting conventional C-band long-haul high-capacity paths to the L-band using inter-band wavelength conversion technology to avoid nonlinear effects. We also experimentally evaluate the effectiveness of our proposal.

talks.title: We2-A3: Field Trial of Digital Subcarrier Multiplexing-based P2MP over 170 km for Distributed Data Center Network Interconnect
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Chenxiao / Wang, Ceng / Nimura, Shinji / Soma, Daiki / Inohara, Ryo / Tsuritani, Takehiro

We demonstrate a DSCM-based P2MP optical interconnect architecture through a ~170‑km metro field trial. Full C-band transmission, long-term stability, coexistence with legacy services, asymmetric link tolerance, and dynamic re-grouping capabilities are experimentally validated.

sessions.title: We2-B SiP Based Modulators
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: We2-B1 Pushing terabits: 800g and 1.6t silicon photonic transmitters at scale
We2-B2: Silicon Microring Modulators with 5.2 THz FSR and 69 GHz EO Bandwidth for 3.2-Tbps DWDM Integrated Photonic Transmitters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lu, Kaihang / Yin, Yuxiang / Zhou, Wu / Chen, Hao / Wen, Baohua / Chan, Chi-Hang / Tong, Yeyu

We present a high-performance O-band silicon microring modulator with a 2.5 um radius, achieving a 5.2 THz free spectral range, 69 GHz electro-optic bandwidth, and 0.4 nm/mW heater efficiency. This design facilitates a 3.2-Tbps integrated photonic transmitter using 16×224 Gbps DWDM PAM-4.

talks.title: We2-B3: Beyond 110 GHz Silicon-Organic Hybrid Modulator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Conglin / Kara, Gokhan / Merla, Michele / Debaets, Michiel / Kim, Minkyu / Marchese, Chiara / Barzanji, Adam / Verheyen, Peter / Van Dorpe, Pol / Catthoor, Francky / Bogaerts, Wim / Van Campenhout, Joris / Haffner, Christian

First-time demonstration of 3dB bandwidth larger than 110GHz for a vertical silicon organic hybrid electro-optical (EO) modulator without back gating. For the same Pockels coefficient, the new configuration shows a two times reduced VπL compared to classical SOH devices

talks.title: We2-B4: Post-Fabrication Laser-Trimmed Microring Modulator Operating Beyond 100 Gbaud
talks.abstract:
Authors: Weckenmann, Erwan / Lassonde, Philippe / Bérubé, Jean-Philippe / Gagnon, Philippe / Duval, Simon / Potvin, Fabrice / Chevalier, Dylan / Geravand, Alireza / Levasseur, Simon / Légaré, François / Robichaud, Louis-Rafaël / Shi, Wei

We demonstrate the first laser-trimmed silicon microring modulator validated under high-speed data transmission beyond 100 Gbaud. Post-fabrication trimming enables a permanent 376 GHz resonance shift without compromising modulation efficiency or electro-optic bandwidth. Bit-error-rate measurement confirms no performance penalty induced by trimming.

talks.title: We2-B5: 200 GBaud PAM-4 Silicon Photonic Traveling-Wave Mach-Zehnder Modulator for 400G/lane IM/DD Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cammarata, Simone / Singh, Nishant / Da Silva, Leandro / Jongbloet, Gael / Jans, Jasper / Ossieur, Peter / Bruynsteen, Cedric / Yin, Xin

A silicon photonic Mach–Zehnder modulator supporting 400 Gb/s per lane with 200 GBaud PAM‑4 modulation format is demonstrated, featuring carrier-dispersion phase shifters and differential push-pull electrodes with ground shielding to suppress parasitic RF mode excitation.

sessions.title: We2-D Ultra-wideband systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: We2-D1: 423.7 + 426.5 Tb/s GMI Bi-Directional HCF Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yang, Jiaqian / Aparecido, Romulo / Sillekens, Eric / Sohanpal, Ronit / Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Gan, Zelin / Hong, Yang / Kamalian-Kopae, Morteza / Ali, Abdallah / Bakhtiari Gorajoobi, Shahab / Luís, Ruben / Orsuti, Daniele / Donodin, Aleksandr / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Luo, Jiawei / Digiovanni, David / Fontaine, Nicolas / Dallachiesa, Lauren / Mazur, Mikael / Ryf, Roland / Chen, Haoshuo / Neilson, David / Phillips, Ian / Forysiak, Wladek / Turitsyn, Sergei / Furukawa, Hideaki / Gaudette, Jamie / Richardson, David / Puttnam, Benjamin / Killey, Robert / Bayvel, Polina

We demonstrate OESCL-band same-wavelength bi-directional transmission over 60 km HCF with 42.5 THz bandwidth, achieving GMIs comparable with the highest unidirectional SMF data-rates in both directions, with an aggregate of 423.7 + 426.5 Tb/s.

talks.title: We2-D2: 75.6-Tbps (700 Gbps x 108 ch.) L+U-band Transmission over Multi-span Field-deployed DSF Link Enabled by PPLN-based OPA/EDFA Hybrid Repeater
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hoshi, Megumi / Shimizu, Shimpei / Abe, Masashi / Kazama, Takushi / Enbutsu, Koji / Kashiwazaki, Takahiro / Inoue, Asuka / Konno, Shunya / Sumihara, Kana / Kimura, Kosuke / Nakamura, Masanori / Hamaoka, Fukutaro / Umeki, Takeshi / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We demonstrated 75.6-Tbps L+U-band WDM transmission over 2×70.4-km field-deployed DSF using a hybrid repeater of EDFAs and waveband converting optical parametric amplifiers with PPLN waveguides. The gain stability of our hybrid repeater and signal quality in the L- and U-band was validated over an hour.

talks.title: We2-D3: S+C+L-band WDM Transmission Under Realistic Telco Transport Network Conditions
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pincemin, Erwan / Le Guyader, Bertrand / Genay, Naveena / L'Escop, Jenny / Evanno, Noella / Ehlert, Jannik / Lempereur, Yannick / Clements, Wallace / Papernyi, Serguei / Nassiri, Mikael / Fulop, Ludovic / Morvan, Michel

We report here a S+C+L-band WDM transmission over 4x100-km SSMF carrying 50-Tbps overall on 12-THz bandwidth with Raman-assisted mitigation of inter-band Raman crosstalk under realistic telco transport network conditions including the use of industrial coherent transponders.

talks.title: We2-D4: Time-Domain Two-Pulse Collisions Nonlinear Interference Noise Model for Ultra-Wideband Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lorenzi, Francesco / Schenato, Luca / Mecozzi, Antonio / Antonelli, Cristian / Santagiustina, Marco

We extend the time-domain model of two-pulse collisions nonlinear interference noise to ultra-wideband single-mode links. We identify key length scales, derive a classification of collision regimes, and explain similarities and differences with Gaussian noise models, especially under low dispersion and low differential group delay.

talks.title: We2-D5: Enabling Technologies for Long-Haul Ultra-Wideband Transmission Utilizing Extremely Long Wavelengths
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shimizu, Shimpei / Kimura, Kosuke / Kawai, Akira / Abe, Masashi / Konno, Shunya / Kazama, Takushi / Enbutsu, Koji / Kashiwazaki, Takahiro / Hoshi, Megumi / Nakamura, Masanori / Hamaoka, Fukutaro / Umeki, Takeshi / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We introduce our work on extending the WDM bandwidth to longer wavelengths in the U- and X-bands and its key technologies for long-haul transmission, including the ISRS design and an ultra-wideband inline repeater using high-efficiency parametric waveband conversion with periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguides.

sessions.title: We2-E Advanced distributed fiber sensing
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: We2-E1: Towards Six-Decade Dynamic Range for Distributed Strain Sensing Using Coherent Microwave-Frequency OTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ren, Yan / Fernández-Ruiz, María R. / Martin-Lopez, Sonia / Costa, Luis / Zhan, Zhongwen / Gonzalez-Herraez, Miguel

A coherent microwave-frequency OTDR scheme is demonstrated. By simultaneously extracting radio frequency and optical frequency signals through coherent detection, it supports distributed strain sensing from sub-nanostrain to hundreds of microstrain levels, offering a promising approach for saturation-free wide-range sensing in earthquake early warning applications.

talks.title: We2-E2: Distributed Single-Shot Birefringence Measurement with Sub-Meter Resolution Using Dual-Polarization TEΦOTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mateu-Comas, Julia / Soriano-Amat, Miguel / Martin-Lopez, Sonia / Gonzalez-Herraez, Miguel / Palmieri, Luca / Fernández-Ruiz, María R.

We demonstrate a single-shot, fully distributed technique for linear birefringence measurement of single-mode optical fibers based on dual-polarization TE-ΦOTDR. The method retrieves the local birefringence magnitude from local spectral shifts, achieving sub-meter spatial resolution. We also prove its capacity for sensing transverse loads.

talks.title: We2-E3: Distributed and dynamic strain sensing in a hollow-core anti-resonant fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vidal-Moreno, Pedro J. / Romero-Barrueco, Alonso / Barco-Alvárez, Javier / Costa, Luis / Martin-Lopez, Sonia / Fernandez-Ruiz, Mª Rosario / Vázquez, Carmen / Slavik, Radan / Poletti, Francesco / Gonzalez-Herraez, Miguel

Distributed acoustic sensing is limited by strain–temperature cross-sensitivity in standard fibers. We demonstrate distributed sensing in hollow-core fiber using mode walk-off interferometry, enabling spatial mapping and dynamic strain sensing without Rayleigh scattering. Results show localized perturbation detection over hundreds of meters.

talks.title: We2-E4: Phase Noise Suppression in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Using a Hollow-Core-Fiber-Assisted Interferometer
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ji, Jiazhen / Wan, Yangyang / Du, Jiangbing / Ma, Lin / He, Zuyuan

The performance of distributed acoustic sensing degrades significantly when the interrogator is subject to phase-noise induced by environmental perturbations. We propose a hollow-core-fiber delay interferometer for environmentally robust phase-noise compensation, achieving a 46% improvement in strain resolution at 50 km sensing range under environmental perturbations.

talks.title: We2-E5: Distributed measurement of hollow core optical fibres
talks.abstract:
Authors: Slavik, Radan / Wei, Xuhao / Poletti, Francesco

We review the brief history of distributed measurement techniques for characterization of anti resonant hollow-core fibres, highlighting the associated challenges and solutions, which often differ from those in single-mode optical fibre measurements.

sessions.title: We2-F ITU-T ION-2030: Architectures and standards of optical networks for the AI era
We2-G Optical processing
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: We2-G1: Microring-Based Programmable Temporal Kernels for Ultrafast Photonic Neural Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Shaojie / Xu, Tengji / Wang, Benshan / Peng, Jiayong / Xiao, Qiarong / Fan, Li / Chen, Hongwei / Huang, Chaoran

We propose a temporal convolution paradigm for photonic neural networks beyond static weighting. A single microring resonator performs programmable multi-tap convolution at 128 Gbaud, achieving 5.12 TOPS computing throughput. We demonstrate a multiplexed system enabling hardware-efficient and high-dimensional computing with 48 TOPS/mm2

talks.title: We2-G2: Experimental Demonstration of Few-Sample Energy-Aware Hardware-in-the-Loop Training of Photonic Neural Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cong, Guangwei / Matsutani, Hiroki / Konoike, Ryotaro / Yamashita, Daiki / Hirasawa, Shoichi / Koibuchi, Michihiro / Namiki, Shu / Amano, Takeru

We propose and experimentally demonstrate an energy-aware augmented simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) algorithm and few-sample in-situ training of photonic neural networks (PNNs), reducing power consumption by ~20–57% and improving both time and power efficiency in training by 10-30x while maintaining >95% classification accuracy.

talks.title: We2-G3: Heterogeneous Photonic Integration for High-Performance Communication and Computing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lu, Liangjun / Su, Jinwei / Wang, Yibo / Gao, Wei / Guo, Yuyao / Li, Yu / Chen, Jianping / Zhou, Linjie

In this talk, I will review our recent work on heterogeneously integrated photonic devices via micro-transfer printing for high-performance communication and computing, achieving a 110-GHz modulator and a −45-dB crosstalk optical switch by synergistically combining silicon nitride with thin-film lithium tantalate/niobate.

talks.title: We2-G4: Experimental Demonstration of Flexible, Multi-Wavelength All-Optical Equalization using a Receiver-Side Integrated Photonic Reservoir
talks.abstract:
Authors: Masaad, Sarah / Declercq, Jakob / Donodin, Aleksandr / Gooskens, Emmanuel / Sygletos, Stylianos / Yin, Xin / Bienstman, Peter

As IM/DD links scale, equalization across multiple wavelength channels becomes increasingly demanding. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic reservoir for adaptable, multi-wavelength equalization using TDM-assisted training. Results on 14–28 Gbaud/λ, 20–70km and up to four wavelengths show up to four orders BER improvement over DSP

talks.title: We2-G5: Compact Single Chip SiGe BiCMOS Optical Phased Array for Energy Efficient, Fast Beam Steering
talks.abstract:
Authors: Arsanjani, Saeed / Vornicu, Ion / Acasandrei, Laurentiu / Khan, Muhammad S. / Malik, Muhammad H. / Bardong, Jochen / Winzer, Georg / Zimmermann, Lars / Cassese, Tommaso

A compact, energy efficient SiGe BiCMOS optical phased array (OPA) implemented on an electro-photonic integrated circuit (EPIC) platform is presented. The 1×32 array achieves a 51.2°×15.7° beam steering range, a reduced per-channel electrical power consumption of 2.5mW /π, and a fast 2.6μs beam configuration time.

sessions.title: We2-C LLM-driven control and automation in optical networks
sessions.track: SC 10: Control and management of optical networks

talks.title: We2-C1: Token-Efficient and Output-Reliable LLM Agent for Link Fault Diagnosis via Skill-Augmented and SOP-Constrained Design
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Shengnan / Wang, Fubin / Cui, Zihao / Zhang, Min / Wang, Danshi

We propose a skill-augmented and SOP-constrained LLM Agent for optical link fault diagnosis. By organizing diagnostic capabilities into reusable skills with progressive disclosure, the Agent reduces token usage by 86% and achieves 100% RCA accuracy on a commercial-equipment testbed, while ensuring deterministic operation.

talks.title: We2-C2: A T-API-Compliant ReAct Agentic Loop for Optical Networks: Generic vs. Domain-Specific Tool Abstractions
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ahmadian, Morteza / Monti, Paolo / Natalino, Carlos

Optical networks need intent-driven, closed-loop agentic management, a key enabler for higher autonomy levels. We present the first T-API-compliant reasoning and act (ReAct) loop. We show that domain-specific composite tools achieve 90% oracle-validated correctness with threefold token savings compared to generic tools.

talks.title: We2-C3: LLMs and Optical Networks: A Symbiotic Relationship
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ibrahimi, Memedhe / Zhang, Qiaolun / Sticca, Giovanni / Xiong, Jiaheng / Musumeci, Francesco / Tornatore, Massimo

This paper explores the emerging symbiosis between LLMs and optical networks. LLMs require geo-distributed training, which demands advanced optical transport capabilities that require new technical enablers, as WAN-aware CCL algorithms, ZR+ pluggables, and Hollow-Core Fibers. Conversely, LLMs also enable new forms of autonomous network management

talks.title: We2-C4: Agentic AI for IPoDWDM Network Lifecycle Automation: An MCP-Enabled Architecture
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xia, Chunmin / Harbaczewski, Jakub / Dsilva, Nikhil / Raulin, Julie / Schneider, Dominic / Autenrieth, Achim

We present a distributed, vendor‑agnostic multi‑MCP architecture for SDN-based automation and autonomous control of multi-vendor, multi-layer IPoDWDM networks. The framework enables E2E service lifecycle automation, closed-loop cross-layer control using GNPy model and optical telemetry, and is experimentally validated on a IPoDWDM testbed.

talks.title: We2-C5: Hybrid Active-Online Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Concept Drift Adaptation in Optical Network Failure Detection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Moiz Ali, Yousuf / E. Prilepsky, Jaroslaw / Pedro, João / Srivallapanondh, Sasipim / Napoli, Antonio / K. Turitsyn, Sergei / Freire, Pedro

We propose a hybrid active-online learning framework for label-efficient concept drift adaptation in optical network failure detection. Using margin-based selective labeling, our method achieves near- ceiling accuracy and AUC scores while querying only 3.4% of streaming samples, with negligible latency overhead compared to static inference.

sessions.title: We2-H SDM transmission
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: We2-H1: Space Division Multiplexing for Ultra-High Capacity Optical Communications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Okonkwo, Chigo

We review progress in space-division multiplexing towards recent records in standard-cladding 19-core randomly coupled multi-core fibres, including 1.7 Pb/s and 568.8 Tb/s over 5,166 km, addressing the yearly increase in capacity demands from AI and hyperscale datacenter interconnects.

talks.title: We2-H2: Impact of Separated/Coupled Core Amplification on MDL and SMD Characteristics in Coupled Multi-core Fibre Link
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sakamoto, Taiji / Wada, Masaki / Imada, Ryota / Nakajima, Kazuhide / Matsui, Takashi

We quantitatively clarify that coupled-core multi-core fibre amplifiers simultaneously achieve low mode-dependent loss (MDL) and low spatial-mode dispersion (SMD) over the C-band, while separated-core amplification poses severer requirements regarding the property variations between single-mode amplifiers to lower MDL and SMD even with independent gain control.

talks.title: We2-H3: Characterization of Mode-Dependent Gain in Distributed-Raman-Amplified 90-km Multi-mode Fiber with Remote Digital Holography
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ann Shaji, Divya / Moonen, Quinten / Van Den Hout, Menno / Van Vliet, Vincent / Kalla, Besma / Bradley, Tom / Mecozzi, Antonio / Okonkwo, Chigo / Antonelli, Cristian

Using optical injection-locking-based remote digital holography, we investigate the impact of distributed Raman amplification (DRA) on the mode-dependent gain (MDG) of a 90-km, three-mode graded-index multi-mode fiber. Observed MDG trends are further supported by the corresponding mode-differential-gain due to DRA in an emulated transmission system.

talks.title: We2-H4: Demonstration of Dispersion-Diversity Signal Processing Using a 19-Core Heterogeneous Multicore Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: González, Mario / Ureña, Mario / Garcia, Sergi / Stelzer, Thomas / Uta, Linda / Frosz, Michael H. / Gasulla, Ivana

We demonstrate a 19-core heterogeneous multicore fiber operating as a tunable sampled true-time delay line for dispersion-diversity signal processing. Three distinct preforms, scaled to implement the 19 cores, enable quasi-linear chromatic dispersion increments across the channels. Experimental results confirm controlled differential delay and reconfigurable filtering.

sessions.title: We2-I Advanced signal processing and real-time implementations
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: We2-I1: Real-Time 100G Burst-Mode Coherent Receiver with Convergence-Free DSP
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zeng, Tao / Pan, Yimei / Wang, Chen / ke, Te / yang, Botao / zhong, Ziye / Liu, Ziqing / Luo, Ming / Li, Ming / Xiao, Xi / Li, Hanbing

We demonstrate a real-time 100G burst-mode coherent receiver with convergence-free DSP eliminating burst-start convergence. Fast impairments are resolved feedforward, while slow effects use pre-initialized channel states with adaptive refinement. Immediate acquisition is achieved under ±100 ppm asynchronous operation, with −30 dBm sensitivity without optical amplification.

talks.title: We2-I2: Low-Complexity FPGA Implementation of Rate-Adaptive Hierarchical Distribution Matcher
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Zulin / Li, Yan / Sun, Yaning / Wei, Pengpeng / Wei, Shuai / Sun, Xiaoting / Wu, Jian

We propose a modified hierarchical distribution matching architecture that enables flexible transmission rate adjustment with low complexity and fine rate granularity in a rate-adaptive probabilistic shaping system, achieving real-time line rate adjustment from 96 Gb/s to 179.2 Gb/s on a single FPGA.

talks.title: We2-I3: Parallel DSP Architecture with Pilot Aggregation for Real-Time MIMO Equalization Enabling Fast Polarization Tracking
talks.abstract:
Authors: Miura, Syoma / Koganei, Yohei / Igarashi, Koji

We propose a parallel DSP architecture for MIMO equalization where pilot samples are aggregated into a single parallel channel, enabling fast polarization tracking. FPGA-based evaluation shows that the proposed method significantly reduces circuit resources while achieving delay below 6 ns, demonstrating suitability for real-time implementation.

talks.title: We2-I4: AI-core Enabled Real-time 2.0-Tbit/s Coherent Transceiver Operating at 234 Gbaud
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tang, Xuefeng / Ma, Shengming / Yong, Zhikui / Hu, Wenyi / Gao, Ge / Xiao, Zhiyu / Wu, Shuangyuan / Si, Minggang / Zhang, Zhuhong

We demonstrate a real-time coherent transceiver operating at a baud rate of 234 Gbaud. The transceiver incorporates advanced ASIC-implemented DSP algorithms and an integrated AI core, delivering sufficient performance margin to support transmission over a 60-km SSMF link.

talks.title: We2-I5: Completely Optical-Filterless Comb-Based Transmitter with a Relaxed Clock Rate for Multi-Tbps Single-Carrier Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yamazaki, Hiroshi / Ozaki, Josuke / Ogiso, Yoshihiro / Nakamura, Masanori / Shibahara, Kohki / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Hashimoto, Toshikazu / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We demonstrate a transmitter architecture that optically extends signal bandwidth without any filtering of the comb lines. A digital spectral weaver with half the conventional frequency-division spacing halves the clock rate required for comb generation. Up to 2.9-Tbps single-carrier transmission is achieved with 320-GBaud signaling.

talks.title: We2-I6: First-Ever Burst-Capable Adaptive Optical Signal Processor for Next-Generation PON Upstream Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Brestas, George / Füllner, Christoph / Borkowski, Robert / Spyropoulou, Maria / Apostolopoulos, Dimitris / Kanakis, Giannis / Avramopoulos, Hercules

We experimentally demonstrate the first optical signal processor compatible with burst-mode upstream reception in Passive Optical Networks. The processor integrated in Indium Phosphide enables nanosecond-scale reconfiguration, performs equalization and noise suppression, and may potentially reduce complexity and power consumption of US digital signal processing.

sessions.title: WeL-E Women in photonics: "WIP-BEAM: Women in Photonics-Bridging Excellence and Advancement through Mentorship"
Lunch
We3-A Switching architectures in optical networks
sessions.track: SC 06: Architecture, modelling and performance of optical networks

talks.title: We3-A1: Automated Performance Optimization for Data Center Exchange over Open Optical Networks: Challenges and Future Perspectives
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mano, Toru / Nishizawa, Hideki / Sone, Yoshiaki / Takasugi, Koichi

This paper addresses data center exchange optimization over open optical networks under physical-layer uncertainty. A 300-km field experiment showed that a digital-twin framework combining physical models, digital longitudinal monitoring, and optical line system calibration can characterize unknown resources, optimize settings, and enable rapid optical-path provisioning.

talks.title: We3-A2: Evaluating Hyperconnected Optical Core Networks Under Future Traffic Requirements
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zitkovich, Mirko / Vásquez, Christofer / Sharma, Anjali / Mas-Machuca, Carmen

As optical core networks are expected to evolve toward hyperconnected topologies, understanding their trade-offs becomes critical. This work evaluates traffic redistribution, fiber deployment, and quality of transmission, showing that hyperconnectivity relieves resource pressure with relatively low signal penalties but increases transponder requirements.

talks.title: We3-A3: Optimizing 800G IPoWDM Architectures through Optical Bypass, Thin Transponders and Proprietary Channel Modulation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Morea, Annalisa / Zami, Thierry / Lavigne, Bruno / Rossi, Nicola

This work highlights the value of IPoWDM architectures with optical bypass, describing when Thin Transponders as regenerators and 800G ZR+ optical pluggable proprietary mode significantly improve energy efficiency—30% average—while optimizing interface deployment and maximizing traffic across core WDM networks.

talks.title: We3-A4: Network-Level Impact of EDFA Gain Fluctuations under Dynamic RWA in High-Symbol-Rate WDM Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sekizuka, Taisei / Shimoi, Shunya / Kuno, Takuma / Hasegawa, Hiroshi / Mori, Yojiro

We investigate EDFA gain fluctuations under dynamic RWA through network simulations, experimental characterisation, and transmission evaluation in high-symbol-rate WDM networks. Results reveal increased intra-link fibre utilisation variation, gain-profile distortion, and accumulated Q-factor degradation, highlighting EDFA gain fluctuations as a non-negligible impairment in such optical networks.

talks.title: We3-A5: Network-Wide Deployment of Pluggable Transceivers with Selective Wavelength Routing and Path-Splitting Regeneration
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shimoi, Shunya / Sekizuka, Taisei / Kuno, Takuma / Mori, Yojiro / Hosokawa, Kohei / Yanagimachi, Shigeyuki / Hasegawa, Hiroshi

We propose an architecture for regional and core networks that combines low-loss optical bypass at FXCs with regeneration at selected WXCs, enabling end-to-end connectivity using only ZR+ pluggable transceivers even with their limited transmission reach. Simulations show lower transceiver cost with modest fibre penalty.

sessions.title: We3-B Integration of magneto-optics
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: We3-B1: Nonreciprocal integrated magneto-optics: from optical isolators to new applications in communications, sensing, and computing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pintus, Paolo

Magneto-optic materials exhibit the nonreciprocal capability to control the amplitude, phase, and polarization of light with an external magnetic field.
