In this tutorial, I will highlight recent progress in their integration and explore emerging applications across communications, sensing, and next-generation computing paradigms. ©2026 The Author

sessions.title: We3-D Signal processing for high-speed IMDD
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: We3-D1: PAM12 Modulation Coding Options Enabling High-Speed IM/DD Transmission in Bandwidth-Limited Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wantee, Suttikarn / Bottrill, Kyle / Othman, Hilmi / Mcculloch, Douglas / Liu, Hao / Petropoulos, Periklis

We investigate two-dimensional bit-mapping for PAM12 transmission, identifying a valid solution for Gray coding. We experimentally demonstrate its performance in a 203 Gbit/s PAM12 transmission over 2-km single-mode fibre, showing the feasibility of high-order PAM for reduced electrical bandwidth utilisation and improved spectral efficiency.

talks.title: We3-D2: Resonant Plasmonic Optical DAC for Low-Power IM/DD Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Moor, David / Hess, Samuel / Rieben, Daniel / Moser, Annina / Fernandes, Sonia / Garrett, Matthew / Baeuerle, Benedikt / Heni, Wolfgang / Moschopoulos, Konstantinos / Christofidis, Christos / Nazarathy, Moshe / Tomkos, Ioannis / Leuthold, Juerg

We experimentally demonstrate low-power intensity-modulated links utilizing optical digital-to-analog converters (DACs) based on resonantly enhanced plasmonic devices. By enabling amplitude multiplexing in the optical domain, this approach supports transmission with reduced processing com-plexity, achieving rates up to 336 Gb/s/POL/𝜆.

talks.title: We3-D3: Photonic-Electronic Arbitrary-Waveform Generation Enabling 276 GBd Electrical and 260 GBd Optical PAM4 Signaling
talks.abstract:
Authors: Drayss, Daniel / Schmitz, Lennart / Fang, Dengyang / Winter, David / Xu, Yongchao / Kotz, Alexander / Zhang, Yu / Zhao, Yuqi / Scordo, Dominick / Mardoyan, Haïk / Renaudier, Jeremie / Zhang, Mian / Freude, Wolfgang / Randel, Sebastian / Koos, Christian

We demonstrate 276 GBd electrical PAM4 signaling using a photonic–electronic arbitrary‑waveform generator (PE‑AWG). We validate the concept in optical signaling experiments with thin‑film lithium‑niobate Mach-Zehnder modulators, achieving PAM4 symbol rates up to 236 GBd in the O‑band and 260 GBd in the C‑band.

talks.title: We3-D4: Peak Amplitude Constrained Linear Pre-Equalization Design Method for Intensity Modulation and Direct Detection Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lanneer, Wouter / Füllner, Christoph / Verplaetse, Michiel

We propose a novel design method for linear transmit-side pre-equalization in IM/DD systems that takes DAC peak amplitude constraints directly into account. Experimental 100G PON results demonstrate a loss budget improvement of 4.3 dB for PAM2 compared to conventional methods while utilizing fewer filter taps.

talks.title: We3-D5: Direct Detection with High Electrical Spectral Efficiency
talks.abstract:
Authors: Su, Yikai / Li, Jingchi / Chen, Haoshuo / Shieh, William

Carrier assisted direct detection receiver can reconstruct the optical field of a complex-valued double-sideband signal, thus achieving a high electrical spectral efficiency comparable to that of a coherent homodyne receiver, while eliminating the need for a costly local oscillator laser.

sessions.title: We3-E Innovations in high capacity, short reach links
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: We3-E1: Demonstration and Study of Silicon-Photonics-Based 720-Gbps Dual-polarization IMDD
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhao, Ying / Doerr, Christopher / Chan, Howard / Vanani, Fatemeh / Takeshita, Makoto

A 720-Gbps dual-polarization (DP) IMDD system including a 180-GBd PAM4 transmitter and a Stokes polarization demultiplexer is demonstrated. Employed PICs are comprised entirely of silicon-photonics. Demultiplexed eye diagrams are presented for homodyne and heterodyne schemes.

talks.title: We3-E2: Single-SMF Bidirectional Up-to-180GBd & 400Gb/s IM-DD Links Utilizing Optoelectronic equalization (OE-EQ) with Direction-, Wavelength- and Baudrate-shared Simple Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Paikun / Yoshida, Yuki / Shinada, Satoshi / Kitayama, Ken-Ichi

We demonstrate record single-SMF bidirectional IM-DD transmissions of 180GBd/lane 50km, 320Gb/s/lane 30km and 400Gb/s 20km in C-band with standard PAM formats. It is enabled by a bidirectional OE-EQ technique with shared low-complexity optics supporting both directions, different wavelengths & baud-rates.

talks.title: We3-E3: Accelerating the Terabit Breakthrough: Defining the Future of Ultra-High-Speed Ethernet
talks.abstract:
Authors: D'Ambrosia, John

Ethernet is accelerating to meet the extreme scale‑up and scale‑out demands of AI back‑end fabrics. IEEE 802.3dj’s 200 Gb/s–1.6 Tb/s solutions are already reshaping architectures, and the IEEE 802.3 Working Group is assessing requirements beyond 200 Gb/s to power the next wave of AI systems

talks.title: We3-E4: 2.4 Tb/s OCS-based Intra-to-Inter Datacentre IM/DD Links Over 54-km MCF Using Sub-pJ/bit Membrane DML Arrays
talks.abstract:
Authors: Diamantopoulos, Nikolaos Panteleimon / Luis, Ruben / Shinada, Satoshi / Orsuti, Daniele / Fujii, Takuro / Nishi, Hidetaka / Sato, Tomonari / Furukawa, Hideaki / Matsuo, Shinji

We demonstrate a high-bandwidth, low-latency, OCS-based WDM+SDM O-band IM/DD link for AI datacentre scale-across networking, spanning SR-to-ER distances without OEO conversion. Net 2.4 Tb/s is achieved over a heterogeneous 54-km MCF link using sub-pJ/bit membrane DML arrays, extending energy-efficient intra-datacentre DML transmitters to metro-DCI reach.

sessions.title: We3-F Integrated optical sensing and communications systems
sessions.track: SC 09: Free-space optics and optical wireless technologies

talks.title: We3-F1: Experimental Demonstration of a Mid-IR Free Space Link for Simultaneous Gas Sensing and Adaptive Communication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zuo, Yue / Jiang, Zile / Alhaddad, Abdulrahman / Ko, Wing / Zhou, Huibin / Zhang, Yixuan / Tur, Moshe / Willner, Alan E.

We demonstrate an OFDM-based mid-IR free-space link at ~3.3 μm for simultaneous multi-gas sensing and coherent communication. We show sensing results with <15% error in gas concentration, and the sensing-informed adaptive loading enables ~60-Gbit/s OFDM transmission.

talks.title: We3-F2: Integrated Mid-Infrared Ranging and Free-Space Communication using a Low-Threshold Directed-Modulated QCL
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lyu, Zhidong / Zhang, Yuhang / Cheng, Yang / Dai, Zhecheng / Jiang, Tianyu / Schatz, Richard / Sun, Yan-Ting / Salgals, Toms / Spolitis, Sandis / Cao, Yuheng / Zhang, Zhuoyan / Bobrovs, Vjaceslavs / Zhang, Lu / Yu, Xianbin / Ozolins, Oskars / Chen, Baile / Wang, Jun / Pang, Xiaodan

We report the first system-level MWIR FSO integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) demonstration at 4.52 μm, combining a low-lasing-threshold directly modulated QCL with an uncooled UTC-PD, achieving 4.28 Gb/s data transmission with ~4.0 cm ranging resolution.

talks.title: We3-F3: Hz-to-kHz Range Vibration Sensing in a 2.53 Tb/s FSO System
talks.abstract:
Authors: Matsuda, Keisuke / Xu, Chenrui / Hess, Samuel / Kulmer, Laurenz / Blatter, Tobias / Fukui, Taichiro / Leuthold, Juerg

Detection of 4 Hz to 2 kHz vibration of a transmitter was demonstrated using forward-transmitted communication signal by measuring the Doppler frequency shift. In an anomaly detection scenario of a tower, abnormal vibration reproduced from field data was detected while transmitting a 2.53 Tb/s capacity.

talks.title: We3-F4: A Silicon Photonic Integrated Quasi-Monostatic Focal-Plane-Array FMCW LiDAR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Croes, Guillaume / Prost, Mathias / Reza, Manuel / Lin, Ziduo / Perez Santacruz, Javier / Bembnowicz, Pawel / Bechthum, Elbert / Berteloot, Brecht / Venialgo, Esteban / Tian, Wenjing / Romme, Jac / Emmen, Erik / Govers, Jochem / Ramezani, Maliheh / O'Brien, Peter / Bachmann, Christian / Brouckaert, Joost / Oldenbeuving, Ruud / Jansen, Roelof / Shin, Dongjae / Gerets, Peter / Qiu, Huaqing / Dahlem, Marcus

We present a solid-state quasi-monostatic FMCW LiDAR realized on a 200-mm silicon photonics platform, integrating a 32 ×16 focal-plane-array transceiver that enables 20 m ranging and imaging of real-world targets with only 200 µW optical emission per pixel.

talks.title: We3-F5: 158° Wide-FoV Photomultiplier-Assisted Reception for Bent-Pipe Visible-Light Communication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Schrenk, Bernhard

A silicon photomultiplier is explored as spatial-diversity receiver. Its wide field-of-view enables end-to-end VLC links between end-points that do not share a direct line-of-sight connection. Towards that, LiDAR point-cloud transmission is shown around an obstructing building.

sessions.title: We3-G Subsea fiber sensing and advanced interrogation techniques
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: We3-G1: Long-Term Measurements from a North-Atlantic Deep-Ocean Observatory on Dual Telecom Cables
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mazur, Mikael / Fontaine, Nicolas K. / Ryf, Roland / Karrenbach, Martin / Kamalov, Valey / Dallachiesa, Lauren / Williams, Ethan F. / Gunnarsson, Arnar I. / Jonsson, Orn / Hlynsson, Andre A / Hlynsson, Sigurdur / Nail, Jeewan / Mistry, Ajay / Winter, David / Chen, Haoshuo / Ruiz-Angulo, Angel / Hjorleifsdottir, Vala / Neilson, David T.

We report one year of continuous data from the IRIS cable and six months from a trans-Atlantic cable. Using per-span interferometry, this >150-sensor deep-ocean observatory successfully captured concurrent seismic signals, Spring-Neap ocean tides, deep-sea turbulence, and long-term drift.

talks.title: We3-G2: Sea-Scan: High-Accuracy, ML-based Dark Vessel Detection and Localisation via Weakly Supervised DAS Monitoring
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tian, Tian / Raj, Agastya / Flanagan, Lara / Kennedy, John / Ruffini, Marco

We present an ML-based vessel detection and localization system, trained with weak supervision from imperfect AIS labels, that achieves a 97.8% detection rate at 1.98% false-trigger rate, successfully identifies dark-vessel events from unlabeled data.

talks.title: We3-G3: SOP Sensing in Hollow-Core Fiber: Forward Sensing using COTS Transponder and Localization with Coherent OTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sahu, Adrish / Boddeda, Rajiv / Dupas, Arnaud / Castineiras Carrero, Carina / Mardoyan, Haik / Guerrier, Sterenn / Lonardi, Matteo / Errea Moreno, Javier / Li, Peng / Li, Shuhaui / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Peterson, Daniel / Renaudier, Jeremie

We experimentally investigate and compare distributed state‑of‑polarization sensing in support‑tube hollow‑core and standard single‑mode fiber. Despite significantly weaker Rayleigh backscattering and reduced polarization sensitivity in hollow‑core fiber, polarization perturbations remain observable and spatially localizable, demonstrating the feasibility of SOP‑based distributed sensing in hollow‑core fiber.

talks.title: We3-G4: Characterization of a 10.9-km Hollow-Core Fiber with 920-um Resolution Using a 10-kHz-Linewidth Tunable Laser Source
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Yufeng / Zhang, Xu / Liu, Zecong / Jiang, Rui / He, Zhixue / Tang, Xinke / Guan, Xun

Based on the noise model of optical frequency-domain reflectometry (OFDR), our analysis indicates that lower reflection relaxes the linewidth requirement of the tunable laser source (TLS). We experimentally characterize a 10.9-km hollow-core fiber (HCF) with 920-um resolution using a 10-kHz-linewidth TLS. ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: We3-G5: Sensitivity Comparison of Microwave-Frequency and Optical Fibre Interferometry Based on State-of-the-Art Components
talks.abstract:
Authors: Karydis, Georgios Aias / Fasano, Marco / Parolari, Paola / Boffi, Pierpaolo / Mesaritakis, Charis / Bogris, Adonis

We compare the sensitivity of fibre interferometers to vibrations using microwave oscillators and state-of-the-art lasers over distances up to 70 km. High spectral purity lasers outperform only above 10 Hz, highlighting microwave advantages at low frequencies and the potential of hybrid microwave–optical interferometry systems.

talks.title: We3-G6: Multiple FBG Thermometry using a Dual-Comb Interrogator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Quevedo-Galán, Clara / Madrigal, Javier / Barrera, David / G. Tijero, José Manuel / Sales, Salvador / Durán, Vicente / Pérez-Serrano, Antonio

Fiber Bragg grating sensing benefits from dual‑comb interrogation, enabling faster measurements and enhanced resolution. We demonstrate quasi-distributed dual-comb thermometry based on gain-switched multimode lasers. The approach enables the sequential interrogation of multiple FBGs, expanding the spectral coverage of the sensor and achieving 30 mK precision.

sessions.title: We3-C On-chip light emission and detection
sessions.track: SC 12: CLEO® Special Session on Emerging Trends in Optics and Photonics

talks.title: We3-C1 Coherent and silicon photonics: a marriage for the long and short haul
We3-C2: The Development of Avalanche Photodetectors for Silicon Photonics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Thomas, Greg / Guo, Feng / Knights, Andrew P.

Avalanche Photodetection provides an efficient means to maintain a link budget for a photonic system. For silicon photonics there exist multiple device geometries, which are summarised here. We show that in the case of defect mediated detection, elevated temperature operation leads to improved performance.

talks.title: We3-C3: Recent progress on III-V on Si photonic transmitters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ramirez, Joan Manel / Azhar, Mourad / Korti, Mokhtar / Ben-Mokhtar, Imane / Neel, Delphine / Besancon, Claire / Blache, Fabrice / Jorge, Filipe / Malhouitre, Stephane / Hassan, Karim

We demonstrate InP-based high-speed EML-SOA transmitters integrated on silicon photonics using a single heterostructure based on AlGaInAs multi-quantum wells. Devices show a fiber-coupled modulated output power of 2 dBm, a static extinction ratio over 25 dB and a BER below the HD-FEC at 58 Gbps.

sessions.title: We3-H HCF systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: We3-H1: 202-km Single-Span 200-GBd C-Band IM/DD Transmission over Hollow-Core Fibre Using a SiN Integrated Recurrent Optical Spectrum Slicer
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Hao / Hong, Yang / Sozos, Kostas / Gholizadeh, Baset / Protsenko, Ekaterina / Teofilovic, Isidora / Wantee, Suttikarn / Bottrill, Kyle / Kamalian-Kopae, Morteza / Ali, Abdallah / Bazin, Alexandre / Mesaritakis, Charis / Vigliar, Caterina / Da Ros, Francesco / Bogris, Adonis / Gaudette, Jamie / J. Richardson, David / J. Puttnam, Ben / Petropoulos, Periklis

We report single-wavelength (145-GBd PAM4 and 200-GBd OOK) and WDM (20×160-GBd OOK) IM/DD transmission over a 202-km single-span hollow-core fibre with 34.5-dBm launch power, enabled by a silicon nitride optical pre-processor, achieving a record 646.4 Tb/s·km capacity-distance product.

talks.title: We3-H2: Unrepeatered Transmission of 2x43.2 Tb/s Bidirectional Real Time data over 266 km leveraging Low Loss GTA-ST Hollow Core Fiber with a Single Booster Amplifier
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mardoyan, Haïk / Boddeda, Rajiv / Castineiras Carrero, Carina / Dupas, Arnaud / Li, Peng / Zhang, Lei / Li, Shuhai / Luo, Jie / El Imadi, Abdelali / Renaudier, Jérémie

We report real-time unrepeatered bidirectional transmission of 2×36 channels at 1.2-Tb/s, achieving a full-duplex total throughput of 86.4-Tb/s on a single fiber over 266-km, enabled by a newly designed low-loss Gap-Tube-Assisted Support-Tube hollow-core fiber and a single high-power booster doped-fiber amplifier.

talks.title: We3-H3: 15 THz Long-Haul O-band Transmission over Hollow Core Fibre Supported by Wideband Bismuth-Doped Fibre Amplifiers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Aparecido De Paula Junior, Romulo / Yang, Jiaqian / Sohanpal, Ronit / Melo, Cristobal / Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Gan, Zelin / Hong, Yang / Kamalian-Kopae, Morteza / Gholizadeh, Baset / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Luo, Jiawei / J. Digiovanni, David / Saavedra, Gabriel / J. Elson, Daniel / Wakayama, Yuta / S. Luis, Ruben / Furukawa, Hideaki / Gaudette, Jamie / J. Richardson, David / J. Puttnam, Benjamin / Sillekens, Eric / I. Killey, Robert / Bayvel, Polina

We demonstrate long-haul, wideband O-band transmission enabled by hollow-core fibre and wideband bismuth-doped fibre amplification. A 60 km recirculating loop enables record single-amplifier-type system throughputs of 95.7, 61.1, and 31.1 Tb/s over 360, 1080, and 3000 km, respectively, across bandwidths of up to 15.3 THz.

talks.title: We3-H4: Net 12-Tb/s (30λ×400-Gb/s/λ) IM/DD DWDM Transmission Over 3.2-km Ultra-low Chromatic Dispersion DNANF Covering Full Super C-Band
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ma, Shouchuan / Wang, Qibing / Zhang, Xu / Li, Xingfeng / Mi, Shuchao / Feng, Jingbin / Li, Chao / Ding, Wei / Li, Ke / Wang, Lei / He, Zhixue / Song, Jian / Yu, Shaohua

For the first time, a net 12-Tb/s IM/DD transmission experiment using 30 160-GBaud PAM8 is carried out over a 3.2-km hollow-core double-nested anti-resonant nodeless fibre with ultra-low chromatic dispersion of less than 1.5ps/nm/km in the entire super C-band.

talks.title: We3-H5: Full C-Band Net 8.4 Tb/s (40λ×112Gb/s/λ×2dir.) Real-Time DWDM IM/DD Transmission over 22 km AR-HCF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Yunhong / Wu, Mengqi / Li, Shen / Jia, Jitao / Sun, Peng / Hu, Songyuan / Yue, Bing / Tang, Yuru / Wang, Qibing / Zhang, Xu / Liu, Zichen / Liu, Xumeng / Wang, Lei / He, Zhixue / Li, Chao / Yu, Shaohua

We demonstrate the first real-time DWDM IM/DD transmission over 22km anti-resonate hollow-core fiber loaded by 40λ 100G optical modules at C-band, achieving net capacity of 8.4Tb/s via dual-direction with BERs all below the 7 % HD-FEC threshold of 3.8×10−3.

sessions.title: We3-I Hollow-core fibre characterisation and standardisation
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: We3-I: Rayleigh speckle backscatter measurements of hollow core fiber
We3-I2: Distributed Measurement of Magnitude and Orientation of the Local Birefringence Vector in a 5-Tube NANF
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zampato, Silvia / Avesani, Marco / Guerra, Gianluca / Baldassi, Federica / Taranta, Austin / Schenato, Luca / Abokhamis Mousavi, Seyed Mohammad / Kelly, Thomas William / Sakr, Hesham / Vidiajev, Konstantin / Galtarossa, Andrea / Santagiustina, Marco / Vallone, Giuseppe / Poletti, Francesco / Palmieri, Luca

We present the first complete measurement of the local birefringence vector in a 5-tube NANF. Measurements performed from both sides of a fiber wound on two coils of different diameters show excellent self-consistency and good agreement with numerical simulations.

talks.title: We3-I3: Field Deployment Practice, Key Challenges, and Standardization Outlook of Hollow-Core Fibers and Transmission Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Dong / Ge, Dawei / Zhang, Dechao / Bai, Lirong / Zuo, Mingqing / Liu, Da / Li, Han

This paper summarizes field deployment practices and long‑term stability of hollow‑core fibres (HCFs) in real operating environments. It analyses key challenges like gas absorptions and current progress of solutions, and prospects future standardization of HCF and transmission systems.

sessions.title: Afternoon coffee break
We4-P Poster

talks.title: We4-P100: Monolithic Silicon Photonic Processor for Reconfigurable Radar Jamming with Asymmetric False-Target Clusters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Senyu / Luo, Wei / Li, Yunlong / Zheng, Shuang / Zhang, Minming

We demonstrate a 2.5 × 5.5 mm² monolithic silicon photonic processor for reconfigurable radar jamming with >20 GHz bandwidth. A gated-modulation scheme generates asymmetric false-target clusters with tunable centroid offsets from −0.55 to +0.6 μs, enabling reconfigurable asymmetric deceptive jamming.

talks.title: We4-P101: Compact Hybrid-Integrated 8-Port Optical Heterodyne Source for Wideband Gap-Free Terahertz Generation via Photonic Wire Bonding
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Wentao / Yang, Zijiang / Sun, Zhenxing / Wang, Zhuoying / Xiao, Rulei / Chen, Xiangfei

We demonstrate a compact hybrid-integrated 8-port optical heterodyne source for wideband THz generation via photonic wire bonding. Gap-free continuous beat frequency tuning from 0.08 to 0.83THz is achieved with high output power (>70mW) and narrow linewidth (∼165kHz).

talks.title: We4-P102: Distributed Sensing on a 110-kV Overhead-Line Maintenance Operation on an Operational Optical Ground Wire
talks.abstract:
Authors: Alexoudis, Konstantinos / Järvelill, Torm / Kerm, Hendrik / Kaeval, Kaida / Azendorf, Florian / Sleiffer, Vincent / Müller, Jasper / Okonkwo, Chigo / Bradley, Tom

We demonstrate dual-modal distributed sensing on an operational 110-kV OPGW during crane maintenance. DAS resolves meter-scale lifting events and matches impulsive events to phone audio, while DTSS quantifies post-reclamping residual strain up to ∼398 μϵ, enabling maintenance verification
and asset monitoring in transmission grids.

talks.title: We4-P103: Pre-Delayed Laser Modulation for Remote Radio Beam Steering
talks.abstract:
Authors: Méndez, Rodrigo / Polo, Victor / Raurich, Martí / Navarro, Àlex / Santos, María C.

We demonstrate remote radio beam steering up to 11◦ over a 10 km fiber fronthaul and a 2 m free-space link at 7.5 GHz, using four pre-delayed, individually modulated DFB lasers whose wavelengths are mapped to the horn antennas of a phased array.

talks.title: We4-P104: Silicon-based Microwave Photonics Notch Filter for Millimeter-Wave Frequency Bands
talks.abstract:
Authors: Porzi, Claudio / Malacarne, Antonio / Scaffardi, Mirco / Ghelfi, Paolo / Bogoni, Antonella

A microwave photonic notch filter based on on-chip modified Michelson interferometer in silicon on insulator technology is presented. The filter features a large rejection ratio exceeding 40 dB, positive RF gain, and unprecedented continuous tuning range over nearly 60 GHz, only limited by available equipment.

talks.title: We4-P105: Interpretable and Data-Efficient Fiber Disturbance Classification from SOP Dynamics Using Semantic Knowledge and Adaptive Retrieval
talks.abstract:
Authors: Abdelli, Khouloud

We present a data-efficient framework for fiber disturbance classification from state-of-polarization (SOP) measurements. Physically grounded semantic descriptors enable interpretable zero-shot inference, while adaptive retrieval resolves class ambiguity. Experiments on a 2600-km WDM system achieve 95% accuracy, outperforming supervised methods in robustness.

talks.title: We4-P106: Experimental Investigation of System Outage in Spatial Diversity FSO Links Using Data-Aided and Non-Data-Aided DSP
talks.abstract:
Authors: Johst, Abraham / Arnould, Aymeric / Molle, Lutz / Perlot, Nicolas / Freund, Ronald / Rademacher, Georg / Nölle, Markus

We experimentally investigate the suitability of data-aided and non-data-aided DSP for spatial diversity FSO reception with digital combining. Measurements over a 3.2-km, 32-GBd free-space link are used to emulate variable diversity order and quantify the impact of low-SNR receiver branches on the system outage probability.

talks.title: We4-P107: Real-Time Event-Based Optical Camera Communication at 80 kbit/s over a 320 m Outdoor Link with 120° Field-of-View
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nardo, Francesco / Krötz, Peter / Barrios, Ricardo / Randel, Sebastian

We demonstrate an event-based optical camera communication system using a 120° field-of-view sensor. In daylight, three transmitting nodes achieve an aggregate 240 kbit/s, with individual links reaching 106 kbit/s at 1m and 80 kbit/s at 320m. Our results, establish a new baseline for event-OCC.

talks.title: We4-P108: 10 Gb/s Fiber-Coupled and 2 Meter Free-Space Optical Link using an APD array and an Imaging Receiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pouralizadeh, Atiyeh / Saleh, Yazan / Boniello, Giulio / Kottke, Christoph / Ebmeyer, Anselm / Bode, Max Julius / Bober, Lennert / Freund, Ronald / Jungnickel, Volker

We demonstrate in a fiber-coupled setup using a manufactured silicon APD-array with a peak data rate of 10Gb/s. In a VCSEL-based free-space optical link, the APD array acts as an imaging receiver, achieving 5.6-7Gb/s over wireless distances to 2 meters while preserving full angular diversity.

talks.title: We4-P109: Mitigating Outages in a 4.6-km FSO Link via Mode-Diverse Reception: An Experimentally Validated Digital Twin Approach
talks.abstract:
Authors: Krimmer, Jonas / Van Vliet, Vincent / Van Den Hout, Menno / Tangdiongga, Eduward / Okonkwo, Chigo / Randel, Sebastian

Terrestrial coherent FSO requires mitigating turbulence-induced coupling losses. We experimentally validate a "Digital Twin" channel model against fading statistics from a 4.6-km link. Combining long-term scintillometer data with mode-diverse receiver simulations, we demonstrate that a 6-mode receiver reduces turbulence-induced outage probabilities to 2.02e-5.

talks.title: We4-P10: Parallel Photonic RF Memory Enabled by Hollow-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xu, Kai / Li, Yukang / Gao, Yuan / Li, Peng / Zhang, Lei / Liu, Xiaoyang / Xia, Yu / Cheng, Mengfan / Yang, Qi / Tang, Ming / Liu, Deming / Luo, Jie / Deng, Lei

We report the first parallel photonic RF memory and its application in radar jamming, enabled by recirculation in an HCF with minimal nonlinearity and latency. The storage capacity reaches record-breaking 1100 loops (serial) and 800 loops (parallel), featuring 24-GHz bandwidth and 33% improved delay resolution.

talks.title: We4-P110: Fully Monolithic Pseudo-Random Phase Modulated Coherent LiDAR Transceiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: López-Querol, Pablo / Domínguez-Castillejo, Diego / Quevedo-Galán, Clara / Pérez-Serrano, Antonio

A fully monolithic coherent LiDAR transceiver is demonstrated on a generic indium phosphide platform. The photonic integrated circuit combines a narrow-linewidth laser, a phase modulator, and a 120° hybrid coherent receiver. Ranging capability is validated through in-fibre distance measurements over 500 m

talks.title: We4-P111: Channel-Predictive and Content-Aware Satellite-to-Ground Semantic Optical Communication System
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Wei / Yu, Zhenming / Huang, Hongyu / Dong, Xiangyong / Ma, Yan / Wang, Xiang / Ding, Wenbo / Xu, Kun

We proposed a channel-predictive, content-aware semantic optical communication system for satellite-to-ground links. The framework enables adaptive transmission under dynamic atmospheric turbulence, achieving both strong noise resilience and high-fidelity image transmission. Experiments demonstrate a 3 dB receiver sensitivity improvement.

talks.title: We4-P112: Analysis of Nonlinear Distortions in High Power EDFAs for Coherent Optical Satellite Communications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cotrim, Ricardo / Malheiro, Diogo / Monteiro, Paulo / Guiomar, Fernando / Fernandes, Gil / Medeiros, Maria

Scaling ground-to-satellite free-space optical links to tens of watts introduces Kerr-nonlinearities that limit system capacity. We analyze the interplay between EDFA and patch-cord nonlinearities, showing that a multi-section EDFA structure effectively mitigates amplifier-induced impairments, while patch-cord nonlinearities emerge as the dominant limitation for longer links.

talks.title: We4-P113: Digital Twin-Driven Space Risk-Aware Intelligent Routing for LEO-Satellite Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shi, Lei / Xie, Yanyan / Zhu, Ruijie / Guo, Bingli / Huang, Shanguo

We propose risk-aware routing for LEO optical networks via asynchronous digital twin feedback, modeling multi-stage debris clouds and sun outage risks from synchronized observations. A reinforcement learning agent modulates link costs for routing optimization, improving service success rate by 30.42% over baselines.

talks.title: We4-P114: FMCW LiDAR Demonstrator using an Integrated Silicon Photonics IQ Modulator and Dynamic Target Emulation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Van Elzakker, Gijs / Zhang, Xuebing / Perez Santacruz, Javier / Sidhique, Aboobackkar / Venialgo, Esteban / Wanjalkar, Govind / Yin, Xin / Shin, Dongjae

An integrated silicon photonics IQ modulator is used in an FMCW LiDAR demonstrator. With a tunable coupler to connect I and Q branches, we show the importance of sideband suppression for the detection of dynamic targets, which are emulated using an acousto-optic modulator.

talks.title: We4-P115: Two-Stage Rollback-Aware Recovery for Cross-Datacenter Training under Failure-Induced Optical-Link Capacity Degradation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yang, Zheng / Dai, Jun / Wang, Xiaorun / Li, Xingde / Fang, Kexiong / Wang, Tianli / Liu, Yuyang / Gu, Zhiqun / Zhang, Jiawei

Bandwidth degradation caused by failures disrupts cross-datacenter training. We propose a two-stage recovery strategy using minimum sustainable bandwidth to preserve rollback-aware training value. At 40% residual capacity, it preserves over 2x the value of rigid-priority protection and cuts weighted slowdown by 25% versus equal sharing.

talks.title: We4-P116: Energy-Efficient FSO Reconfiguration under User Mobility in Hybrid Fiber-IAB Backhaul
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lechowicz, Piotr / Madapatha, Charitha / Natalino, Carlos / Svensson, Tommy / Monti, Paolo

User mobility creates stochastic, time-varying backhaul demand that static capacity provisioning cannot match. We propose a closed-loop, load-aware hysteresis controller for hybrid fiber-IAB-FSO backhaul and show that energy drops faster than coverage: 8% to 44% energy savings cost only 0.9% to 6.7% coverage.

talks.title: We4-P117: A Physics-Guided Learning Framework for Compound Soft-Failure Identification from Single-Failure Training Data
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Yun / Yang, Keyuan / Cheng, Guangye / Yang, Yu / Ke, Changjian

We propose a physics-guided learning framework for compound soft-failure identification in optical communication links using only single-failure training data, achieving 92.8% accuracy and strong generalization to unseen failure combinations through physical spectrum synthesis and decision fusion.

talks.title: We4-P118: Descriptor-Conditioned Multi-Agent Small Language Models for On-Premises Optical Network Control
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tanimura, Takahito / Kikuchi, Nobuhiko

Secure optical network control requires local processing, but locally deployable SLMs remain limited in capability. We propose text-defined SLM teams sharing a backbone and diversified by deterministic Text-to-LoRA parameter modulation. In fiber launch-power control, the proposed method achieves higher GOSNR than single-agent and prompt-only baselines.

talks.title: We4-P119: Demonstration of Novel Key-Rate and Trust Aware Routing Scheme for Maximum QKD Link Utilization in Integrated Quantum-Communication Network
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Xinyu / Han, Liuyan / Dai, Longfei / Huang, Qixuan / Wang, Haohua / Wang, Minxue / Zhang, Dechao / Li, Han

We propose a key-rate and trust aware routing scheme maximizing QKD link utilization in integrated quantum-communication networks. Demonstrated for the first time via simulation and experiment, 8.61% utilization improvement, stable key pools, and trusted relays are achieved, overcoming barriers to scalable QKD under limited resources.

talks.title: We4-P11: Single-Ended Crosstalk Measurement in Field-Deployed Multi-Core Fiber Using Commercial OTDR
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gokhale, Abhay / Sarma, Jonaq Niveer / Venkitesh, Deepa

We demonstrate a single‑ended method for measuring inter‑core crosstalk in multi‑core fibers using a single-channel commercial OTDR. The method is validated by comparing with power meter measurements, through simulations and field testbed experiments.

talks.title: We4-P121: Dynamic tracking-enabled indoor free-space BBM92 access for mobile quantum users
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jiang, Shan / Yang, Ruizhi / Tan, Jianxiong / Tai, James / Wang, Rui / Simeonidou, Dimitra

Wedemonstrate a tracking-assisted indoor free-space optical entanglement distribution system for mobile quantum access. Over 3.4-10.1m FSO links, QBER remains below 10.58% with SKR up to 208 bps under ambient light. Results confirm stable end-to-end entanglement delivery under mobility and alignment variations.

talks.title: We4-P122: A Practical Countermeasure Against Attacks Exploiting Detection Efficiency Mismatch in High-Speed Quantum Key Distribution
talks.abstract:
Authors: Taylor, Ben

We demonstrate a practical countermeasure against quantum hacking strategies on quantum key distribution (QKD) systems exploiting detection efficiency mismatch, where the receiver’s detectors do not exhibit identical responses to incoming photons. This countermeasure enables almost complete recovery of the GHz-clocked system’s ideal secret key rate.

talks.title: We4-P123: Optimizing Resource Allocation and Scheduling in Quantum Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bouchmal, Oumayma / Smith, Jake / Wehner, Stephanie

We propose a scheduling framework for resource allocation in quantum networks to maximize served demands. Evaluating ILP, EDF, and simulated annealing across 200 scenarios shows ILP achieves offline optimality, EDF enables fast real-time operation, while simulated annealing offers negligible performance benefit at higher computational cost

talks.title: We4-P124: Optimization of CV-QKD Under Practical Constraints
talks.abstract:
Authors: Matsenko, Svitlana / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein / jarzyna, Marcin / banaszek, Konrad / Zibar, Darko

Using reinforcement learning, we optimize for practical hardware constraints, including limited FIR filter taps at the transmitter and receiver, mean photon number and finite DAC/ADC resolution. Under these realistic conditions, the proposed approach achieves significant performance improvements.

talks.title: We4-P125: Experimental Demonstration of C-Band DWDM Multi-Classical Multi-QKD Coexistence with Pretrained Rapid QBER Evaluation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Guo, Qianhui / Zhu, Xun / Gao, Shang / Zhang, Zikun / Huang, Yanlu / Wu, Liyan / Guo, Mingyang / Han, Shangya / Jin, Kai / Lu, Zhikai / Wang, Zhipeng / Xu, Kun / Ou, Yanni

We experimentally demonstrated a 20-km DWDM system comprising 4-QKD-channels coexisting with 6-classical-channels, investigated the heterogeneous impairments experienced by different QKD users under multi-channel combinations, and proposed a pretrained rapid QBER estimator to adaptive QKD parameters optimisation, increasing the total DV-QKD SKR by 28.25% to 127.64-kbps.

talks.title: We4-P126: Fiber-Coupled Negative Feedback Avalanche Diode Module for Single-Photon Detection in the Optical O-Band
talks.abstract:
Authors: Akal, Muhammed Fatih / Collin, Elisa / Rustige, Pascal / Runge, Patrick

We present a fiber-coupled negative feedback avalanche diode (NFAD) module, characterized in free-running mode with active hold-off circuitry, demonstrating a dark count rate below 100 Hz for 20% single-photon detection efficiency at 1301 nm and 233 K.

talks.title: We4-P127: Key-Aware Shared Wavelength Management for Coexisting Quantum and Classical Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Huang, Wenjie / Yu, Xiaosong / Liu, Jingjing / Nag, Avishek / Zhao, Yongli / Zhang, Jie

We propose a key-aware shared wavelength management (KA-SWM) algorithm for CV-QKD and classical service coexistence over SDN-enabled WDM networks. A dual-threshold mechanism dynamically expands and recycles quantum channels based on real-time key pool status, achieving up to 79.62% relative improvement in service success probability.

talks.title: We4-P128: Passive Polarization-Insensitive QKD Receiver Module in a Standard CFP2 Form Factor
talks.abstract:
Authors: Oh, Junsang / Choe, Joong-Seon / Choi, Byung-Seok / Baek, Ju Hee / Lim, Kyongchun / Youn, Chun Ju

We report the first passive polarization-insensitive QKD receiver implemented in a CFP2 module through hybrid QPIC integration. The proposed self-compensating configuration removes active polarization control while enabling high integration density, offering a scalable route toward compact and commercial quantum communication systems.

talks.title: We4-P129: Characterization of Coherence From Spontaneous to Stimulated Four-Wave Mixing in Si3N4 Microresonators
talks.abstract:
Authors: Famà, Francesca / Dello Russo, Stefano / Giaccari, Stefano Gregorio / Virzì, Salvatore / Lucia, Lorenzo / Clivati, Cecilia / Gionco, Chiara / Siciliani De Cumis, Mario / Condio, Stefano / Donadello, Simone / Bertaina, Gianluca / Meda, Alice / Cerrato, Erik / Gramegna, Marco / Genovese, Marco / Levi, Filippo / Degiovanni, Ivo Pietro / Calonico, Davide

We experimentally characterize spectral coherence in four-wave mixing using high-Q silicon nitride microresonators. Employing time-correlation and phase-sensitive techniques, we follow the expected extension of the coherence time from cavity- to pump- limited regimes, providing a method for characterizing tunable quantum sources, useful for quantum communication.

talks.title: We4-P12: High Δ Single-Mode Polymer Waveguides with Athermal Mode-Field Diameter for Co-Packaged Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yamagishi, Taiki / Ishigure, Takaaki

We demonstrate athermal polymer waveguides suitable for co‑packaged optics. We measure the temperature dependence of core-cladding index difference using 3D-OWFM on circular cores in polymer waveguides and identify a core/cladding combination with |dΔn/dT| ≅ 10-6 / oC, enabling a stable mode-field diameter up to 100 °C.

talks.title: We4-P130: Octave-spanning Supercontinuum Generation with Optimized Ultralong-Ultrafast Fiber Lasers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hernández Martín, Laura / Cáceres-Pablo, Inés / Corredera, Pedro / Ania-Castañón, Juan Diego

Pulsed supercontinuum generation centered at 1550 nm with a-30 dB bandwidth in excess of 1000 nm is generated from optimized ultralong ultrafast ring fibre sources with intra-cavity polarization and gain control, using commercially available HNLF.

talks.title: We4-P131: Silicon Nitride Microring Resonator for Broadband Near-Infrared to Telecom Wavelength Conversion
talks.abstract:
Authors: Upadhyay, Chandan / Shetewy, Abdou / He, Menglong / Jamshidi, Kambiz

A silicon nitride pulley microring resonator is designed for broadband 780-to-1550 nm frequency conversion via four-wave mixing Bragg-scattering. Measured loaded Q-factors of 0.52×106 (780 nm) and 0.48×106 (1550 nm) yield a simulated on-chip conversion efficiency of -4.6 dB at 50 mW pump powers
each.

talks.title: We4-P132: Measuring Nanometer-Scale Process Variation in Lithography Using Image-Based Anomaly Detection
talks.abstract:
Authors: Douven, Yanick / Van Der Palen, Stefan / Schrinner, Philip / Wetzels, Rik / Dekker, Ronald

This work evaluates image-based anomaly detection as a fast, low-cost method to estimate nanometer-scale lithography variation from optical microscope images. A reference-trained model is applied to parameter-sweep structures and validated with SEM, showing that process-induced fill-factor-shifts, corresponding to 20 nm can be detected and quantified.

talks.title: We4-P133: A Fourier Neural Operator Surrogate Model for 3D Diffusion in Photonic Glass Core Substrates
talks.abstract:
Authors: Choy, Dennis / Chojne, Tom / Haffner, Maurice / Schwietering, Julian

Three-dimensional diffusion simulation in glass core substrates is computationally expensive. We present a Fourier Neural Operator surrogate that maps 2D masks to 3D diffusion fields. On heldout data, it achieves 0.0236 normalized RMSE with 140 ms inference, enabling rapid design-space exploration.

talks.title: We4-P13: Low-Power Consumption and Stable Broadband Optical Frequency Comb Generation in X-Cut Lithium Tantalate
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Xin / Xiao, Mingkun / Sun, Min / Su, Yikai / Ji, Xingchen / Zhang, Yong

We demonstrate controllable switching between Raman and Kerr frequency combs via dispersion and coupling engineering in X-cut lithium tantalate. The Kerr comb exhibits low power consumption, over 450 nm spectral span and hour-scale stable operation without dual-pump excitation or complex thermal control.

talks.title: We4-P14: Mid-Infrared Optical Parametric Amplification in a Quasi-Phase-Matched Silicon Nitride Waveguide with a Broad Bandwidth of 130 nm
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Shaoxing / Du, Jiangbing / Li, Yuan / Xu, Ke / He, Zuyuan

A 2.5-m-long Si3N4 waveguide (4.74 × 4.31 mm2) featuring sign-alternated dispersion for quasi-phase-matched optical parametric amplifier is demonstrated. It achieves 2-dB/m low attenuation and 130-nm amplification bandwidth, offering robust fabrication tolerance and promising potential for efficient continuous-wave broadband amplification in the mid-infrared regime.

talks.title: We4-P15: Four-Port Oblique-Coupled Ge-on-Si Photodetector with Improved Bandwidth Retention at High Photocurrent
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Chao / Tang, Rui / Okano, Makoto / Toprasertpong, Kasidit / Takenaka, Mitsuru

We demonstrate four-port oblique-coupled Ge-on-Si photodetector enabling high photocurrent and bandwidth. The device achieves a record-high responsivity–bandwidth product, with 1.04 A/W responsiv-ity and 64.4 mA photocurrent, and maintains 15-5 GHz bandwidth up to 35 mA, improving the trade-off between high-current operation, bandwidth, and responsivity.

talks.title: We4-P16: Metasurface-based Transmissive 2×2 Polarization Beam Splitter/Combiner for Circular and Linear Polarizations
talks.abstract:
Authors: E. Elfiqi, Abdulaziz / Soma, Go / Ishimura, Shota / Suganuma, Takahiro / Ren, Chun / Takahashi, Hidenori / Tsuritani, Takehiro / Tanemura, Takuo

Transmissive 2-input 2-output polarization beam splitter/combiner based on ultrathin metasurface is demonstrated. Efficient polarization splitting is achieved experimentally for all port combinations over a ~60 nm wavelength range, with the maximum polarization extinction exceeding 17 dB for both linear and circular polarization bases.

talks.title: We4-P17: Tuneable RF Signal Generation Through Integrated Self-Injection-Locked Gain-Switched Combs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dominguez-Castillejo, Diego / Venkatasubramani, Lakshmi Narayanan / Rajeswari, Gayatri Vasudevan / Prasad, Deepa / Atar, Fatih Bilge / Moehrle, Martin / Barry, Liam / Corbett, Brian

High frequency tuneable gain-switched combs are demonstrated through a monolithically integrated multi-section laser. Photon-photon resonance extends modulation bandwidth beyond 43.5 GHz, enabling comb generation up to 30 GHz without external injection. Downconverted microwave tones exhibit resolution-limited linewidths below 50 Hz.

talks.title: We4-P18: Spiking Photonic Nodes based on Two Section InP Semiconductor Lasers on Silicon
talks.abstract:
Authors: Skontranis, Menelaos / Charbonnier, Benoit / Girard, Olivier / Bogris, Adonis / Mesaritakis, Charis

Spiking behaviour of two-section InP quantum-well lasers fabricated on a Silicon-on-Insulator platform is experimentally validated. Dynamic regimes, including integrate-and-fire and resonate-and-fire are achieved through bias variation. Impact of cavity length and absorber ratio are evaluated, providing design guidelines for scalable active neuromorphic photonic integrated circuits.

talks.title: We4-P19: First Statistical 2,000-hour Reliability and Reflow Compatibility Results of Silicon-Ferroelectric Nematic Glass (Si-FNG) Electro-Optic Modulators
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chiang, Li-Yuan / Christensen, James / Jahn, Jerome / Tsai, Yi-Chuan / Quinonez, Dominic / Patel, Chirag / Savechenkov, Pavel / Huang, Ching-Wen / Huang, Pao-Chieh / Bathaei, Neda / Ding, Jerry / Mahpeykar, Milad / Tzu, Ta-Ching / Nissov, Morten / Pecinovsky, Cory / Masini, Gianlorenzo / Harrison, Mark

We report the first industry-standard (Telcordia) reliability and reflow compatibility assessment of hybrid-integrated Si-FNG modulators. With 167 devices, we demonstrate robust parametric stability and failure-free life over 2,000-hour HTS, 2,000-hour uBDH, 200-cycle TC, and 4-cycle Solder Reflow stresses.

talks.title: We4-P1: Multimode Multicore Fiber with 19 Cores for Short Reach Data Center Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mccarthy, Joseph / Griffin, Seth / Xiao, Licheng / Liu, Jie / Zakharian, Aramais / Wu, Qi / Li, Ming-Jun

A multimode multicore fiber with 19 cores was designed and fabricated for short reach datacenter applications using VCSEL or micro-LED arrays. Fiber characteristics such as core refractive index profile, core position accuracy, attenuation, crosstalk are reported.

talks.title: We4-P20: Inverse-Designed Silicon Six-Mode Multiplexer for 1.6T/λ Mode-Division Multiplexing Interconnect with AI-Enhanced Reception
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Aolong / Yuan, Yuqin / He, Jialin / Yan, An / Hu, Yongzhu / Zhao, Junhao / Chi, Nan / Zhang, Junwen

We demonstrate a silicon-photonic mode-division multiplexing interconnect employing an inverse-designed six-mode multiplexer with insertion loss below 1.9 dB and crosstalk below −14.6 dB at 1550 nm. A 1.62 Tb/s/λ capacity is realized by transmitting 90-GBaud PAM-8 signals over six modes using a temporal convolutional network.

talks.title: We4-P21: Frequency Response Engineering of EO-Equalized Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Modulator Using Capacitive-Loaded Traveling-Wave Electrodes with Two Distinct Periods
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yamaguchi, Yuya / Tien Dat, Pham / Takano, Shingo / Hirata, Shotaro / Kataoka, Yu / Ichikawa, Junichiro / Fujino, Tetsuya / Shinada, Satoshi / Akahane, Kouichi / Yamamoto, Naokatsu / Kanno, Atsushi / Kawanishi, Tetsuya

We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate modulator with engineered frequency response using an electro-optic equalizer based on capacitive-loaded traveling-wave electrodes with two distinct loading periods. The device achieves a 1 dB bandwidth exceeding 110 GHz with a half-wave voltage of 2.2 V.

talks.title: We4-P22: High-Baud-Rate Data Transmission Through a Non-Volatile Sb2Se3 Phase-Change Switch on Silicon Nitride
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lopez-Mulet, Iñigo / Liu, Hao / Yu, Xingshi / Chakraborty, Ipsita / Dominguez Bucio, Thalia / Johnson, Isaac / Parra, Jorge / Sanchis, Pablo / Gardes, Frederic / Petropoulos, Periklis

We experimentally evaluate high-baud-rate transmission through a non-volatile Sb₂Se₃ phase-change optical switch on silicon nitride, supporting up to 200-GBd OOK, 135-GBd PAM4, and 80-GBd PAM8. An up to 2 dB penalty is observed with no phase-state-dependent degradation, confirming compatibility with high-speed, reconfigurable photonic interconnects.

talks.title: We4-P23: Compact Slow-Light-Enhanced TFLN Modulator for CWDM4
talks.abstract:
Authors: He, Ruiqing / Li, Chenlei / Ma, Ruitao / Sun, Dongyue / Li, Hanwen / Wang, Zexu / Bao, Yaoxin / Xie, Jin / Li, Huan / Dai, Daoxin

We present a compact slow‑light‑enhanced TFLN transmitter for CWDM4, enabling an aggregate line rate of 800 Gbps. The device exhibits a reduced modulation length of 2 mm and a modulation efficiency of 1.22 V·cm. In addition, low-loss CWDM operation is provided by integrated cascaded Bragg‑grating filters.

talks.title: We4-P24: Co-fabrication of Graphene Modulators and Detectors on Silicon-on-insulator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wen, Chao / Montanaro, Alberto / Tiberi, Matteo / Symeon, Petros / Schreiner, Paul / Li, Yang / Chen, Lu / Zhang, Jincan / Littlejohns, Callum / Sorianello, Vito / Ferrari, Andrea

We report co-fabrication of high-speed graphene modulators and photodetectors on silicon on insulator by optimising modulator and photodetector designs under CMOS-BEOL constraints. The resulting platform balances extinction ratio, responsivity and bandwidth, establishing a practical route towards integrated >67GHz SLG optoelectronic transmit/receive systems.

talks.title: We4-P25: A 240 Gb/s O-band Silicon Micro-ring Modulator with 3 THz FSR and 110 GHz bandwidth
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhou, Zhiyuan / Sun, Zhihan / Yuan, Yuqin / Wan, Huajie / He, Jialin / Hu, Liyun / Wu, Yantao / Tian, Qi / Liu, Siyang / Li, Zhen / Hu, Changyu / Hu, Hao / Liu, Jun / Dai, Shengjiang / Zhang, Junwen / Shen, Li / Zheng, Shuang / Zhang, Minming

A 4-µm-radius O-band silicon micro-ring modulator featuring a 3-THz FSR and >110-GHz EO bandwidth is demonstrated. Offering a finesse of 50, it supports 160-Gb/s NRZ and 240-Gb/s PAM4 below the SD-FEC limit, enabling >16-channel high-density WDM.

talks.title: We4-P26: Workload-Aware Passively Biased Short-Electrode MZI for Efficient Vector-Matrix Multiplication in Neural Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhao, Shi / Zeng, Chenxuan / Yang, Jie / Leong, Jin Feng / Pan, Jieming / Yan, Ao / Yu, Tiancheng / Zhang, Xiangyu / Zamburg, Evgeny / Thean, Aaron Voon-Yew

Exploiting the skewed distribution of neural-network weights, we report a passively biased MZI that reduces phase tuning from π to ~0.16π for efficient VMM. Measured devices validate design targets with good reproducibility, enabling 5.3× footprint reduction, 0.11 pJ/OP and 1079 TOPS/(W·cm²) at <0.1% accuracy drop

talks.title: We4-P27: Dual-Pump Pulsed Degenerate Optical Parametric Oscillation in a Silicon Nitride Microresonator with Anomalous Dispersion
talks.abstract:
Authors: He, Menglong / Dzieia, Nora / Shetewy, Abdou / Jamshidi, Kambiz

We experimentally demonstrate modulated degenerate optical parametric oscillation in an anomalous-dispersion silicon nitride microresonator using an optimized dual-pump scheme, achieving pulsed operations up to 30 MHz with 5.34 dBm optical power and an 18 dB signal-to-noise ratio, establishing its potential for coherent Ising machines.

talks.title: We4-P28: Integrated Photonic Physical Unclonable Function based on Multi-Resonant Structures in a Hexagonal-Reconfigurable Mesh
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tzekas, Nikolaos / Karydis, George- Aias / Charbonnier, Benoit / Capmany, Jose / Bogris, Adonis / Mesaritakis, Charis

we propose a physical unclonable function based on a silicon reconfigurable mesh programmed to implement multi-resonant structures. By harnessing manufacturing imperfections as a stochastic source, each device produces unique spectral fingerprints. When combined with a Gabor fuzzy-extractor a probability of cloning of 10-16 is achieved

talks.title: We4-P29: Nanosecond Silicon Photonic BiDi Splitter-Switch for Point-to-Multipoint Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Stern, Brian / Borkowski, Robert / Vijayan, Kovendhan / Kim, Kwangwoong / Simsarian, Jesse

We demonstrate a 1×8 silicon photonic splitter-switch enabling independent switching for upstream and downstream directions in an access network. Nanosecond-scale switching is shown with 1.1 dB loss per Mach-Zehnder stage, showing feasible scaling to higher port count and enabling higher power budgets than with splitters.

talks.title: We4-P2: 200 km SSMF Transmission of C+L-Band 800 Gbps Signals Using Bidirectional Distributed Raman Amplification with High Power Incoherent Forward Pumping
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ogata, Daichi / Hayashi, Shunya / Takasaka, Shigehiro / Kawabata, Shoichi / Yoshida, Junji / Ohishi, Norihiro / Nakanishi, Michihiro

We demonstrate 201.6km standard SMF single-span transmission of C+L-band 60 channel 100 GBd DP-16QAM signals employing bidirectional distributed Raman amplification. Amplified incoherent forward pumps suppress relative intensity noise transfer to the signals, while forward and backward Raman pumps each operate with sub-1 W power.

talks.title: We4-P30: Reconfigurable On-Chip Spectrometer with Adaptive Spectral Resolution
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Wanlu / Xu, Kangning / Yao, Chunhui / Huang, Huiyu / Yan, Ting / Penty, Richard / Cheng, Qixiang

In this paper, we present a reconfigurable on-chip spectrometer based on a cascaded Mach–Zehnder interferometer network with programmable optical path differences (0–180 μm). It enables adaptive spectral acquisition across multiple resolution scales within a single device, establishing a new paradigm for reconfigurable on-chip spectroscopy.

talks.title: We4-P31: Experimental Demonstration of Sub-10 kHz Linewidth Tunable DFB Laser Array Based on Self-Injected Feedback
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Yue / Yang, Zijiang / Sun, Zhenxing / Xiao, Rulei / Chen, Xiangfei

We demonstrate a high-power, narrow-linewidth REC-DFB laser array using SCOW and self-injection feedback. Integrated with PLCs via photonic wire bonding (PWB), the array achieves >100mW power, 12.8nm tuning range, and SMSR >50dB. The Lorentzian linewidth is compressed to <7kHz.

talks.title: We4-P32: A 1.2 Vpp Driver-free Differential Ge Eelectro-absorption Modulator Enabling 150 Gbps NRZ and 360 Gbps PAM-8 modulation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Liu, Yufei / Hamulati, Kaisa / Zhao, Xinran / Li, Jun / Zhou, Yue / Cai, Haiwen / Yang, Fenghe / Chu, Wei

A differential Ge Franz-Keldysh EAM with 2.78 dB insertion loss operates at 1.2 Vpp without a driver. It achieves 150 Gbps NRZ and 360 Gbps PAM‑8. The ultra‑low swing enables direct CMOS driving for future LPO/CPO links.

talks.title: We4-P33: PAM4 448 Gb/s per Lane InP MZM-SOA Array PIC for Next-Generation CPO Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tatarczak, Anna / Steib, Michael / Varga, Laszlo / Melgar, Alirio / Chen, Young-Kai

We demonstrate a monolithic 1310 nm InP Mach–Zehnder modulator and semiconductor optical amplifier array operating at 448 Gb/s per lane with an external laser. After 500 m transmission, a BER of 1.1×10⁻³ is achieved with 25-tap FFE, supporting InP for next-generation co-packaged optics.

talks.title: We4-P34: On-Chip Pulse Amplification and Compression Using Silicon Nitride Photonic Integrated Circuits
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Jie / Tong, Yitian / Geng, Zhaoting / Zhang, Chuchen / Du, Zhenmin / Chen, Xuewen / Lin, Jinwen / Huang, Yuhao / Fu, Yunqi / Xia, Yu / Yu, Di / Chen, Hongwei / Xiang, Chao

We demonstrate on-chip pulse amplification and compression using a silicon-nitride-based erbium-doped waveguide amplifier and a chirped spiral Bragg grating. Our work achieves >50-fold amplification and 32-fold pulse compression, paving the way toward fully integrated high-power ultrashort pulse sources for diverse applications.

talks.title: We4-P35: C-band Compact Hybrid-Integrated Multi-port Multi-wavelength Laser Source for DWDM Communication in Optical I/O
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yang, Zijiang / Sun, Wentao / Zhang, Yue / Sun, Zhenxing / Chen, Xiangfei

A C-band compact MP-MWL for optical I/O has been presented. The source architecture comprises an 8-wavelength high-power DFB laser array based on the REC technique, hybrid-integrated with a Si3N4 8×8 MMI via the PWB technique.

talks.title: We4-P36: Compact Waveguide-Integrated Graphene Photodetector with >110-GHz Bandwidth for 240-Gbit/s PAM-4 Reception
talks.abstract:
Authors: Peng, Hejie

We experimentally demonstrate a compact waveguide-integrated graphene photodetector based on a geometry-optimized plasmonic slot waveguide. With an 80 nm slot, 53 nm electrodes, and a 10 μm interaction region, the device exhibits >110 GHz bandwidth and clear 240 Gbit/s PAM-4 reception for ultrafast optical interconnects.

talks.title: We4-P37: Fully integrated CWDM Optical Engine with III-V/Si DFB Laser Arrays and Silicon Mach-Zehnder Modulators
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yong, Zheng / Denis-Le Coarer, Florian / Liu, Xiaodong / Thiessen, Torrey / Mak, Jason / Das, Alok / Da Benta, Elory / Goward, John / Froberger, Kevin / Puaud, Apolline / Hsu, Sharon / Qiu, Benton / St-Arnault, Charles / Plant, David / Menezo, Sylvie

We report on an O band 4-CWDM transmitter consisting of a single Silicon chip comprising heterogeneous DFB lasers, Si MZMs and monitoring Ge-PDs. The Tx chip is wire bonded to a 56 Gbaud PAM4 commercial driver. 64Gbaud PAM4 eye diagrams are reported.

talks.title: We4-P38: High-Connectivity, Low-Latency Optical Perceptron Enabled by Time-Multiplexing and All-Optical Nonlinearity
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Hao / Zhu, Xinyi / Azaña, José

We experimentally demonstrate an end-to-end optical single-layer perceptron (SLP). This computing engine combines stable optical temporal interference with all-optical nonlinearity, enabling 8,100 connections and low latency of ~670 ns. The optical SLP successfully recognizes 90 distinct binary patterns with an accuracy of 100%.

talks.title: We4-P39: Accelerating Convergence of Longitudinal Power Profile Estimation based on Adaptive Tikhonov regularization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Xiang, Junjiang / Chen, Zhuoting / Li, Chao / Zhou, Gai / Xiang, Meng / He, Zhixue / Fu, Songnian / Qin, Yuwen

We propose adaptive Tikhonov regularization for accelerating convergence of longitudinal power profile estimation. Only single-shot execution can secure an estimation error of 0.13dB over the anomaly loss range of 0.74~3.4dB, when the 120Gbaud DP-QPSK signals with 14dBm launch power are transmitted over 3×50km G.654.E fiber.

talks.title: We4-P3: Ultra-Large Mode Area All-Solid Antiresonant Fiber with Effective Single Mode Guidance
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hean, Kevin / Dutta, Debjit / Yoo, Seongwoo / Dussardier, Bernard / Du, Zehui / Chang, Wonkeun / Goel, Charu

We demonstrate effectively single-mode guidance in an all-solid antiresonant fiber with an ultra-large mode area exceeding 3000 µm2. The fiber offers strong broadband suppression of higher-order modes over a short propagation length of 1 m, enabling scalable design for high-power lasers.

talks.title: We4-P40: Improved Chase–Pyndiah Decoding for Product Codes with Scaled Messages
talks.abstract:
Authors: Miao, Sisi / Birincioglu, Mert / Schmalen, Laurent

We propose an enhanced Chase–Pyndiah decoder that scales extrinsic messages based on decoder confidence of the component decoder, achieving a 0.1 dB gain over the original with negligible complexity increase.

talks.title: We4-P41: Subcarrier Channel Polarization-Based Low-Complexity FEC for 16-QAM SDM Digital Subcarrier Multiplexing System
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shi, Hao / Zhao, Jian / Cao, Lingguo / Zhao, Xue / Wang, Shunfeng / Tang, Jianwei / Ye, Gao / Fan, Linsheng / Sun, Zhongliang / Xu, Zhaopeng / Liang, Junpeng / He, Zhixue / Wei, Jinlong

We experimentally demonstrate the first subcarrier channel polarization low-complexity FEC encoded 1.92Tb/s 16-QAM-DSCM signal transmission over a 50-km four-core fiber, achieving a 4.2-dB OSNR gain and 80% decoding-complexity reduction at the KP4-FEC threshold compared to conventional FEC scheme.

talks.title: We4-P42: Simulation-to-Experiment Transfer Learning for Nonlinear Equalization in Long-Haul Raman-Amplified Coherent Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Moustakas, Georgios / Deligiannidis, Stavros / Jia, Xiaoshuo / Zhang, Xiaona / Sun, Yaning / Luo, Ming / Li, Yan / Wu, Jian / Baziana, Peristera / Mesaritakis, Charis / Bogris, Adonis

This paper employs transfer learning to train a machine learning equalizer for Raman-amplified systems using limited experimental data. Pre-training on simulated synthetic data allows the model to achieve performance comparable to, or exceeding, optimized digital back propagation, effectively mitigating nonlinear impairments over long-haul distances.

talks.title: We4-P43: Optimized Spatio-temporal Spike Encoding for Low-power Spiking Neural Network Equalizers in IM/DD Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Shuangxu / Calabrò, Stefano

A convolutional neural network spike encoder paired with a spiking neural network equalizer is proposed for an IM/DD link. It achieves a 1.7 dB gain over a linear equalizer while reducing spike activity by 80%, offering a low-complexity, low-power solution for neuromorphic hardware.

talks.title: We4-P44: Pilot Symbol-Aided Timing Error Correction for Equalization-Enhanced Phase Noise and Clock Timing Jitter Compensation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Medra, Ahmed / Mohammadian, Amirhossein / Li, Chuandong

We propose a novel pilot symbol-aided timing error correction algorithm designed to mitigate impairments from equalization-enhanced phase noise (EEPN) and clock timing jitter. The proposed architecture employs a hybrid feedback loop for analog-to-digital converter (ADC) clock refinement and a feed-forward path for digital timing correction.

talks.title: We4-P45: Joint Probabilistic and Geometric Constellation Shaping for Complexity-Constrained Direct Detection Optical Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fischer, Rodrigo / Chimmalgi, Shrinivas / Rode, Andrej / Schmalen, Laurent

We evaluate joint probabilistic and geometric constellation shaping via reinforcement learning for complexity-constrained joint equalization and demodulation of direct detection optical signals. We demonstrate the proposed technique in a simulated 56 GBd, 2.2 km C-band direct-detection system, demonstrating its effectiveness for complexity-constrained receivers.

talks.title: We4-P46: Order-Dependent Characterisation and Cutdown of Volterra Kernels in NL-MLSE for Net 400-Gb/s O-Band PAM-6 IM-DD
talks.abstract:
Authors: Taniguchi, Hiroki / Yamamoto, Shuto / Nakajima, Yukinobu / Nakamura, Masanori / Yamazaki, Etsushi

Volterra NL-MLSE kernels of 1st and 2nd/3rd order play distinct roles: 1st-order tracks CD while 2nd/3rd-order capture CD-invariant device nonlinearity. This decoupling enables independent channel modelling. Cutdown to 15 kernels (73%) preserves −6 to +8 ps/nm CD tolerance at 182 GBd PAM-6 without BER penalty.

talks.title: We4-P47: Semantic Holographic-Type Co-frequency Co-time Full duplex Communication Over a 100 km Single-span Hollow Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Anxu / Dong, Xiangyong / Ma, Yan / Zhang, Wei / Mu, Yueqiu / Feng, Lipeng / Huo, Xiaoli / Li, Junjie / Yu, Zhenming / Xu, Kun

We demonstrate the first semantic holographic-type co-frequency co-time full duplex (HT-CCFD) communication system over 100 km hollow-core fiber. The semantic scheme achieves 73.3 dB PSNR, outperforming 16QAM and QPSK by 5 dB and 8 dB, respectively, while maintaining reliable transmission at low received optical power.

talks.title: We4-P48: Pruning-Assisted Model Adaptation for Real-Time Neural Network Equalization in Photonic-Aided Wireless Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Jie / Hu, Sheng / Wang, Qihang / Bian, Chenzhen / Wang, Kaihui / Yu, Jianjun / Zhou, Wen

We propose an updatable real-time neural-network equalizer using iterative magnitude pruning and transfer fine-tuning, validated in a 300 m, 3.75 Gbaud DMT-64QAM experiment. Compared with the best dense network, it cuts complexity by 89% with nearly unchanged performance under a 2 m channel offset.

talks.title: We4-P49: Polarization-Multiplexed Coexistence of 100 Gb/s MultiCAP Transmission and DD-COTDR Distributed Sensing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sevillano, Pascual / Herguedas, Natalia / Izquierdo, David / Cajal-Pérez, Ramón / Garcés, Ignacio

We demonstrate co-propagation 100 Gb/s MultiCAP communication and DD-COTDR sensing over 25km of SMF- Using orthogonal polarization multiplexing and spectral guard band tailoring, interference is mitigated. A trade-off between sensing SNR and BER is identified, enabling operation below the FEC threshold under practical coexistence conditions

talks.title: We4-P4: Experimental Demonstration of 34 OAM Modes Reaching the Third Radial Order in a Weakly Guiding Three-Layer Ring-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Niu, Quanhao / Tang, Zhouxuan / Shen, Lei / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Wang, Jian

We design and fabricate a three-layer weakly guiding ring-core fiber capable of supporting the third-order radial OAM modes, with a total of 34 OAM modes. Experimental characterization shows superior performance of the fabricated fiber with low loss and low crosstalk.

talks.title: We4-P50: A Closed-Form Solution for Fiber Anomaly Detection in C+L-Band Systems Based on Stimulated Raman Scattering
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cui, Zihao / Li, Shengnan / Luo, Xiao / Zhang, Min / Wang, Danshi

We propose an SRS-based closed-form method for fiber anomaly localization in C+L-band systems. A PSO-based refinement enhances robustness under dynamic conditions. Experiments demonstrate <1.5 km average localization error with low complexity and rapid calculation.

talks.title: We4-P51: Dual-Polarization Optical Coherent Transmitters IQ Impairment In-service Monitoring Using a Single Low-Bandwidth PD
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cui, Xiuquan / Cao, Lingguo / Fan, Linsheng / Shi, Hao / Tang, Jianwei / Jia, Yingxiang / Sun, Zhongliang / Liang, Junpeng / Wang, Shunfeng / Xu, Ke / He, Zhixue / Wei, Jinlong

We propose an enhanced Wiener-Hammerstein model-based framework to monitor dual polarization optical coherent transmitter IQ impairments via a single low-bandwidth photodetector. Experimental results demonstrate an IQ skew estimation error of 0.3ps(2.3ps) for the RLS(LMS) algorithm,with RLS achieving an order-of-magnitude faster convergence than LMS.

talks.title: We4-P52: Blind dispersion slope estimation for high-symbol-rate coherent systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Moreno Morrone, Juan L. / Ebner, Laurenz / Emmerich, Robert / Schubert, Colja / Fischer, Johannes K. / Freund, Ronald

We propose a two-stage scanning method for chromatic dispersion estimation in high symbol-rate coherent systems, including accumulated dispersion slope. The performance is evaluated by simulations at a symbol rate of 240 GBd and experimental emulation of up to 70.8 ps/nm2 dispersion slope at 160 GBd.

talks.title: We4-P53: Field-Trial Validation of EKF Embedded Real-Valued MIMO Equalization for Transmitter Impairment Mitigation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Yingyu / Gao, Hanyu / Chen, Ruqi / Yu, Ying / Zhang, Yifan / Li, Zhaohui

We experimentally validate a real-valued MIMO equalizer embedding EKF phase estimator for transmitter impairment mitigation over a 70-km submarine multicore fiber link. The proposed method maintains Q-penalties below 0.5-dB under 10-ps IQ skew and 2.5-dB gain imbalance with improved frequency offset tolerance up to 50-MHz.

talks.title: We4-P54: Split-Sideband Digital Subcarrier Multiplexing for IQ-Impairment Compensation without Inter-Subcarrier MIMO
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kuno, Takuma / Sekizuka, Taisei / Mori, Yojiro / Hasegawa, Hiroshi

We propose a split-sideband DSCM architecture that eliminates the need for a high-dimensional inter-subcarrier joint MIMO equaliser. Experiments with two 50-Gbaud DP-16-QAM subcarriers, corresponding to an aggregate symbol rate of 100 Gbaud, show performance comparable to that of inter-subcarrier MIMO while using a lower-dimensional equaliser.

talks.title: We4-P55: High-Precision SOP-based Event Localization Using Coherent WDM Polarisation Localisation (CWPL) Technique
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vieira, Rafael / Gomes, Geraldo / Bogdanov, Stepan / Kbashi, Hani / Freire, Pedro / Turitsyn, Sergei / Mecozzi, Antonio

Source localization of SOP transients via CWPL is demonstrated for the first time. By exploiting the correlation between error standard deviation and Δλ, we selectively average measurements from 12 channels, achieving a standard error of the mean of 930 m over a 10000 km link.

talks.title: We4-P56: Joint Subcarrier Phase Recovery for Nonlinearity Mitigation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Secondini, Marco / Civelli, Stella

We propose a low-complexity phase recovery scheme that simultaneously mitigates laser phase noise and fiber nonlinearity across several subcarriers. In a long single-span link with Raman amplification, the scheme achieves 0.9 dB gain with 99 real multiplications per complex symbol.

talks.title: We4-P57: Accurate Multi-perturbation Localization in Optical Fibers with Polarization-based Forward Sensing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lanaras, Lampros / Butler, Rick M. / Häger, Christian / Alvarado, Alex

We present a method to accurately localize multiple perturbations from fiber outputs. We cross-correlate received polarizations between two wavelengths, apply peak detection, and interpolate peaks to boost accuracy. We localize five simultaneous perturbations in a 10 GSa/s numerical fiber model with 3.5 m median error.

talks.title: We4-P58: Frequency Domain Timing Recovery for Baud-rate Sampled Coherent Receivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Afouda, Serge / Nguyen, Trung-Hien / Mumtaz, Sami / Charlet, Gabriel

We propose a generalized roll-off factor independent timing error detector (TED) cost function suitable for frequency-domain DSP working at 1-sample/symbol (1-sps). We numerically and experimentally investigate the effectiveness of proposed TED, an alternative to conventional Godard-TED, in 123.6-Gbaud DP-16QAM transmission systems with only 1-sps Rx-DSP.

talks.title: We4-P59: Feedforward and Iterative Phase Noise Compensation for Channels with Chromatic Dispersion
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jäger, Alex / Kramer, Gerhard

Equalization-enhanced phase noise is avoided by applying phase noise compensation (PNC) before chromatic dispersion compensation. Feedforward and iterative PNC algorithms based on expectation propagation are proposed. Both achieve information rates close to channels without phase noise for 100 GBaud 64-QAM and 10,000 km of fiber.

talks.title: We4-P5: Increased Gain per Unit Length in O-band Bismuth Doped Amplifiers with Trench Assisted Fibre
talks.abstract:
Authors: Elson, Daniel J. / Donodin, Aleksandr / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Luo, Jiawei / Nicholson, Jeffrey W. / Tsuritani, Takehiro / Wakayama, Yuta

Trench assisted bismuth doped fibre (TA-BDF) is used for O-band amplification. TA-BDF is compared to standard BDF, higher gain per meter and lower noise figure are demonstrated for both forward and backwards pumping configurations. RIN transfer of both doped fibres are compared to SMF.

talks.title: We4-P60: Error-Propagation-Aware Transmitter Compliance Metric for Next-generation Optical Interconnects with MLSE Receivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Yongxin / Xin, Haiyun / Fei, Leyan / Xu, Yicheng / Zhu, Yixiao / Hu, Weisheng / Zhuge, Qunbi

We propose an error-propagation-aware MLSE TDECQ based on an analytical Zig-zag model for next-generation optical interconnects. Experimental results in 112-Gb/s PAM-4 systems demonstrate near-unity correlation (slope=1.024, R2=0.994) with actual receiver sensitivity across diverse impairments, ensuring reliable transmitter compliance testing.

talks.title: We4-P61: O-band 3.2 Tb/s Kerr Microcomb Coherent Transmission for Short-Reach DCI Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Donodin, Aleksandr / Kanger, Lou / Elson, Daniel J. / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Emmerich, Robert / Stoliarov, Dmitrii / Kangul, Mustafa / Tremblay, Jean-Etienne / Cavadore, Eline / Koptyaev, Sergey / Luo, Jiawei / Luis, Ruben S. / Furukawa, Hideaki / Schubert, Colja / Freund, Ronald / Digiovanni, David / Wakayama, Yuta / Tsuritani, Takehiro / Jost, John / Karpov, Maxim / Turitsyn, Sergei K.

We report the first demonstration of an O-band Kerr comb laser in coherent transmission, achieving 3.2 Tb/s aggregate rate (GMI) over 25 km using eight comb lines from a single source.

talks.title: We4-P62: One Terahertz Full-Field Digital Back-Propagation over 3000 km
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sillekens, Eric / Luis, Ruben / Di Sciullo, Giammarco / Emmerich, Robert / Centofanti, Carlo / Orsuti, Daniele / Colares, Robson / Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Sohanpal, Ronit / Melo, Darli / Palmieri, Luca / Freund, Ronald / Schubert, Colja / Antonelli, Cristian / Killey, Robert / Bayvel, Polina / Furukawa, Hideaki

We implement full-field digital back-propagation with a 1-THz receiver using 20 synchronous frequency-adjacent coherent receivers with digital stitching and a frequency-comb local oscillator. Relative to electronic dispersion compensation, per-channel DBP and full-field DBP achieve throughput gains of 2.2% and 5.4%, respectively.

talks.title: We4-P63: Evaluating the Viability of Long-haul O-Band Transmission over G.654.C Fibre
talks.abstract:
Authors: Aparecido De Paula Junior, Romulo / Yang, Jiaqian / Melo, Cristobal / Sillekens, Eric / Sohanpal, Ronit / Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Gan, Zelin / Mikhailov, Vitaly / Luo, Jiawei / J. Digiovanni, David / S. Luis, Ruben / Furukawa, Hideaki / D. Downie, John / Galdino, Lidia / J. Elson, Daniel / Wakayama, Yuta / Saavedra, Gabriel / I. Killey, Robert / Bayvel, Polina

We demonstrate the first long-haul, 15.9 THz, WDM O-band transmission using G.654.E-compliant fibre, achieving 55.5 Tb/s (GMI) over 704 km despite its high cutoff wavelength. Ultra-low fibre loss enables a single lumped amplification scheme to achieve an information rate highly competitive with state-of-the-art single-band systems.

talks.title: We4-P64: Experimental Evaluation of Optical-Analog-Optical Wavelength Converter Penalty Metric for Quality of Transmission Estimation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Clark, J. Kenji / Nakamura, Yuna / Nakamura, Toshifumi / Mori, Hiroki / Hiyama, Junnosuke / Nakagawa, Mayuri / Seki, Takeshi / Hayashi, Rie / Ota, Morihiko / Hosokawa, Kohei / Maeda, Wakako / Tamura, Toshihiko / Le Taillandier De Gabory, Emmanuel

Noise added by an optical-analog-optical wavelength converter is shown to have a gaussian-like distribution, represented by a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of wavelength conversion. Using this metric, SNR estimation with 0.8 dB accuracy of a 300 Gbps signal transmitted 400 km and wavelength converted is demonstrated.

talks.title: We4-P65: Open-Loop Calibration of Frequency-Dependent Sub-DAC Mismatch in Time-Interleaved DACs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Chenjin / Lin, Hong / Nie, Junyuan / Ren, Xuecheng / Wang, Shen / Zhang, Jing / Qiu, Kun

We propose an open-loop calibration algorithm for time-interleaved DACs by decomposing mismatches into frequency-independent components and frequency-dependent residuals. Experiments on a 92 GSa/s device with four sub-DACs show that post-compensation suppresses interleaving spurs to the noise floor. A pre-compensated PAM-16 achieves a 44% BER reduction.

talks.title: We4-P66: Experimental Investigation of U-band Transmission over 20 km of Anti-Resonant Hollow-Core Fiber Using Bismuth doped Fiber Amplifier
talks.abstract:
Authors: Castineiras Carrero, Carina / Boddeda, Rajiv / Mardoyan, Haïk / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein / Li, Peng / li, Shuhai / Zhang, Lei / luo, Jie / Renaudier, Jérémie

U-band transmission over 20 km hollow-core fiber (HCF) is experimentally investigated to assess its potential for high-capacity transmission systems. Using Bismuth doped Fiber Amplifier, we show the transmission of 16-QAM and 64-QAM signals,

talks.title: We4-P67: Experimental Study of Burst Error Induced by Relative Intensity Noise in Raman Amplified Repeaterless Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hraghi, Abir / Yu, Gegei / Andre.sampaio, Flavio / Godard, Loig / Sun, Chenyu / Haoyang, Qiu / Lorences.riesgo, Abel / Charlet, Gabriel

We experimentally investigate the burst-error penalty caused by RIN-transfer noise in forward-Raman-amplified transmission systems, observing 0.6 dB larger SNR fluctuations when having 10 dB Raman gain. Our modelling results confirm that RIN-transfer burst penalty should be accounted for when estimating the performance of forward Raman.

talks.title: We4-P68: Breaking the Complexity Barrier of Volterra Equalization via End-to-End Sparse Compression and Recovery in 106-Gb/s PAM4 IM/DD Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yadav, Govind Sharan / Widhianto, Benedictus Yohanes Bagus / Zheng, Sheng-Yuan / Chuang, Chun-Yen / Feng, Kai-Ming / Chen, Jyehong / Chen, Young-Kai

We propose and experimentally validate a novel SLQF-VE for nonlinear distortion compensation in 106-Gb/s PAM4 IM/DD over 6-km SMF. It achieves ~90% complexity reduction at KP4-FEC and ~97% at HD-FEC at −4 dBm ROP, outperforming baseline and sparse VEs, with quantization-aware fine-tuning enabling low-precision operation

talks.title: We4-P69: EEPN-Aware Phase-Gradient MIMO Equalization for Robust Short-Reach Coherent Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Tianhong / Pan, Yutong / Zhu, Yixiao / Cai, Xiang / Zhang, Fan

We propose EEPN-aware phase-gradient MIMO (PG-MIMO), which augments conventional 2-sps MIMO with a phase-gradient-modulated branch to model phase-memory-induced perturbations. In 80-GBaud, 80-km DP-16QAM transmission, PG-MIMO reduces BER by 46.6% and improves Q2 by 0.71 dB.

talks.title: We4-P6: Characterization of Resonance-Induced PDL in ST-HCF via Mueller Matrix Method and Coherent Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hao, Xinyu / Hua, Xuchen / Zhang, Youmin / Qian, Zichen / Li, Peng / Zhang, Lei / Wang, Ruichun / Deng, Li / Li, Bozhong / Zhang, Mingming / Tang, Ming

PDL in HCFs is mainly induced by asymmetric cladding-resonance-interference leakage mismatch. By analysing the Mueller matrix characterization of a 150-km ST-HCF, 2.54-dB PDL peak is identified @192.2 THz. In transmission experiments, the Q-factor penalty between X/Y polarisations reveal highly correlations with this resonance-induced effect.

talks.title: We4-P70: GPU-Accelerated Optimisation of Symmetric Bidirectional Ultrawideband Coherent Transmission Under Launch Power Constraints
talks.abstract:
Authors: Jarmolovicius, Mindaugas / Sillekens, Eric / Bayvel, Polina / Killey, Robert

We optimise bidirectional OESCL-band coherent transmission under total fibre power constraints using a GPU-accelerated boundary-value Raman solver and launch-power optimisation. While no gain is observed without power constraints, for a 18-dBm limit 3-span transmission reversing the O-band direction increases aggregate capacity by up to 24.5%

talks.title: We4-P71: On the Nonlinear Impairments Induced by High-Power Doped Fiber Amplifiers in HCF Transmission Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sorensen Braga, Leonardo / Ghazisaeidi, Amirhossein

We numerically demonstrate that the nonlinearities in high-power EDFAs induced by signal signal interactions in WDM systems are not negligible and may become a limiting factor in future HCF systems and may be captured by the existing EGN models.

talks.title: We4-P72: DRL-Based Joint RSA and Reconfiguration Using Integrated Graph-Based GNN and State-Adaptive Reward
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tanaka, Takafumi

We propose a novel multi-agent DRL framework for joint RSA and optical path reconfiguration, featuring a GNN with a unified graph schema and a state-adaptive reward. Simulations demonstrate over 40% blocking probability reduction compared to conventional approaches, validating the importance of joint planning

talks.title: We4-P73: A Novel Minimum Latency Transport Framework by Satellite-Terrestrial Cross-Physical-Layer Hybrid Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kaida, Yuto / Hirano, Akira / Suzuki, Taiga / Hirota, Yusuke / Xu, Sugang / Awaji, Yoshinari / Furukawa, Hideaki

We propose a two-level minimum latency framework for Starlink-like LEO transport: OTN-like hit-less switching suppresses handover-related latency penalty, while hybrid multi-path FEC with Systematic-on-LEO and CRC early completion enables low-latency loss recovery, with larger gains under smaller path-delay gaps or higher loss.

talks.title: We4-P74: AI-EON for Self-Adaptive Multi-Task Computing Power Access and Its Field Trial
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dong, Wang / Sun, Jiang / Zuo, Mingqing / Sun, Guanghui / Cao, Shan / Qi, Bin / Ge, Dawei / Zhang, Dechao / Li, Han

A scale-across AI-powered elastic optical network is proposed for self-adaptive multi-task computing power access, and is validated in a field 640 km 3,000-GPU dual-node training with <2% efficiency degradation using 800G OTN and 272×272-port OCS.

talks.title: We4-P75: Securing 5G/6G Networks Applying Moving Target Defense over Elastic Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Manolopoulos, Alexandros Ioannis / Alevizaki, Viktoria Maria / Anastasopoulos, Markos / Tzanakaki, Anna
