This work proposes a Moving Target Defense framework using Live Virtual Machine Migration over Elastic Optical Networks to enhance 6G security. Optimized migrations and Markov-based evaluation demonstrate reduced attack success and improved network resilience.

talks.title: We4-P76: Maximum Achievable Burst Size in All-Optical Satellite Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Röthig, Thomas / Mouammar, Sleman / Brasileiro, Ítalo / Hosseini, Soheil / Jukan, Admela

We analyze the maximum burst size achievable in all-optical satellite networks across different constellations. With a 100 Gbps uplink capacity, a WDM-based optical burst switching network supports burst sizes of up to 500 MB in high-altitude LEO constellations and 600 MB in low-altitude LEO constellations.

talks.title: We4-P77: Experimental Demonstration of Fabric Resilience Using a 4 × 4 Dual-Microring Optical Switch for AI Data Centers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Bin / Liang, Qishen / Hou, Baojie / Zhu, Huihui / Zou, Tao / Shi, Junhui / Zhao, Zichao / Ma, Haoran / Yu, Hui / Wang, Yuehai / Yang, Jianyi

We demonstrate an optically connected network architecture with fault recovery for building ML training clusters, enabled by a nonblocking optical switch based on dual-microring resonators. We present experiments on our HPC/ML testbed leveraging the optical programmable network to automatically failover from hardware or software failures.

talks.title: We4-P78: Data-Efficient Few-Shot Modeling of EDFA Gain for QoT Estimation Using Machine Learning
talks.abstract:
Authors: Moawad, Abdelrahmane / Karunakaran, Vignesh / Emmerich, Robert / Yeh, Sharon / Autenrieth, Achim / Shariati, Behnam / Fischer, Johannes Karl / Bauschert, Thomas / Freund, Ronald

We compare few-shot EDFA gain modeling using transfer learning and physics-informed gaussian process regression, enabling data-efficient cross-vendor adaptation under extreme scarcity and achieving sub-0.1 dB mean absolute error for gain prediction.

talks.title: We4-P79: Experimental Investigation of Optical Fiber Amplifier Based All-Optical Relays for Inter-Satellite Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shinada, Satoshi / Kotake, Hideaki / Umezawa, Toshimasa / Hirota, Yusuke / Oda, Shoichiro

The transmission performance of all‑optical relays employing watt‑class optical fiber amplifiers was experimentally investigated. Although the large link losses assumed for inter‑satellite optical links cause significant OSNR degradation, all‑optical relaying of WDM signals over distances exceeding 10,000 km is shown to be feasible.

talks.title: We4-P7: Three-wavelengths fiber optical parametric oscillator tunable from 1296 to 1916 nm
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bastamova, Mariia / Stoliarov, Dmitrii / Doran, Nick / Gordienko, Vladimir

We demonstrate a continuous-wave pumped fiber optical parametric oscillator tunable over the 1296-1916 nm range with output powers of 10-25 dBm. Three waves (signal, idler and residual pump) are available at the output and can be used simultaneously.

talks.title: We4-P80: A Comparative Study on Linear and Nonlinear SNR Estimation Using Neural Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bajaj, Vinod / Silvestre, Henrique Watanabe / Ramantanis, Petros / Layec, Patricia

We compare spectral correlation-based features against well-explored amplitude noise covariance and phase noise correlation-based features for linear and nonlinear SNR estimation using neural networks. Simulation results indicate errors reduced by > 30% when spectral correlation-based features are included.

talks.title: We4-P81: 50 Gbps 25km SSMF Quasi-Coherent Transmission for C-band Optical Access, Mobile Fronthaul and Edge AI Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Herguedas, Natalia / Altabas, Jose A. / Cajal-Pérez, Ramon / Amati, Lorenza / Squartecchia, Michele / Sevillano, Pascual / Izquierdo, David / Carro-Temboury, Miguel R. / Düzgöl, Onur / Shrinivas, Rakshick / Johansen, Tom K. / Garces, Ignacio / Jensen, Jesper B.

Quasi-coherent reception of 50/53.125 Gbps C-band multiCAP/PAM4 signals after 25/10 km SSMF transmission. The PAM4 signal was received error free after real-time FEC decoding. The QC-receiver is implemented in a Silicon Photonics PIC. Applications include mobile fronthaul, edge AI, SMPTE ST2110 video and access networks.

talks.title: We4-P82: Synchronization Reliability Analysis and Real-Time Verification for Burst-Mode 200G Coherent PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Dechao / Jia, Xiaoshuo / Li, Junwei / Wang, Ning / Ye, Zhicheng / Feng, Qiguang / Yu, Hongchen / Lu, Yanzhao / Li, Han

A real-time burst-mode synchronization emulator is demonstrated using 10 FPGAs for 200G coherent PON upstream, executing 1e15 trials. A theoretical model for reliability evaluation is proposed and validated. Results confirm high synchronization reliability could be achieved over 20-km fibre with specially designed preambles.

talks.title: We4-P83: Field Trial of a 50G HS-PON architecture supporting 1×16 All-Photonic Gateway and Time Sensitive Network Traffic
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vargemidou, Maria / Vagionas, Chris / Gatzianas, Marios / Saliou, Fabienne / Deleurme, Erwan / Atwi, Hawraa / Fylaktaki, Margarita / Raptis, Savvas I. / Kalfas, George / Chanclou, Philippe / Pleros, Nikos / Miliou, Amalia

The first field trial of a Next Generation Central Office featuring a 1×16 all-photonic gateway comprising a C-/O-band glass diplexer-array and MEMS-based optical switch is reported, flexibly provisioning multiple traffic-classes of a 50G HS-PON and 10G C-band high-precision Time-Sensitive Network traffic at 1.6 km-long drop-fibers.

talks.title: We4-P84: Flexible Coherent PON using LUT-Based Channel-Adaptive Modulation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Jie / Pi, Zebang / Li, Xiang / Li, Ming / Li, Hanbing / Luo, Ming

We propose a LUT-based GS-FCLS-PON scheme and experimentally demonstrate it in a TFDM system with flexible rates ranging from 100 Gb/s to 600 Gb/s. Both the sensitivity and dynamic range are improved using the proposed scheme.

talks.title: We4-P85: Impact of Burst Traffic in Upstream Converged Coherent Metro-Access Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Alzoubi, Safana / Rizzelli, Giuseppe / Gaudino, Roberto

For future all-optical metro-access networks using PON upstream burst mode transmission, we experimentally investigate on the resulting EDFAs gain transient and its impact on the “regular” DWDM coherent metro wavelengths, focusing specifically on typical 125 microsecond frame time-constants and evaluating the post-FEC OSNR penalty.

talks.title: We4-P86: Traffic-Aware Dynamic Spectral Allocation in AWGR-Based AI Datacenter Scale-Out Fabrics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Klinkowski, Miroslaw / Tomkos, Ioannis

We evaluate dynamic spectral subcarrier (SC) allocation in arrayed-waveguide grating router (AWGR)-based AI datacenter (AI-DC) fabrics under realistic traffic characteristics. Gains over static allocation arise with temporal misalignments, while near-synchronous incast limits benefits. Performance depends on control responsiveness and spectral resource dimensioning.

talks.title: We4-P87: When LLM Meets PON: Distributed Edge Inference Framework and Scheduling over TDM-PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Lu, Junfeng / Gu, Zhiqun / Zhang, Jiawei

We propose a distributed edge inference framework for LLMs over TDM-PON, with a joint computation-communication scheduling scheme eliminating the DBA polling cycles via delay budgeting and phase-aware bandwidth reservation. The performance is evaluated by time per output token and jitter under edge inference workloads.

talks.title: We4-P88: Dual-Channel 60 GBaud PON System Signal Equalization Using Micro-Ring Resonators-Based Reservoir Computing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Seifi Laleh, Mohammad / Kühl, Sebastian / Fonk, Lukas / Oettinghaus, Silas / Pachnicke, Stephan

Based on simulations, a silicon photonic reservoir computer using cascaded add-drop micro-ring resonators successfully performs joint signal equalization and dual-channel demultiplexing for 60-GBd PAM-4 PONs. This integrated processor is cost-effective, improves BER and extends transmission reach over conventional DSP-based FFE.

talks.title: We4-P89: Experimental Assessments of O-band 32x32x8λ Wavelength Cross-connect Switch at 100Gbpsλ for Data Center Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zheng, Boyang / Palmer, Robert / Talli, Giuseppe / Calabretta, Nicola

We experimentally demonstrate an O-band 32×32×8λ WCS architecture for optical interconnections. By exploiting SOA switch/amplification with transmitter optimization and receiver-side sparse Volterra equalization, OSNR and nonlinear impairments are mitigated. Results show <6dB fiber-to-fiber loss, cross-talk <-35dB, total system power penalty <4.3dB, and 6.5dB link-budget.

talks.title: We4-P8: Pluggable-Transceiver-Compatible 4-Core Multi-Core Fibre Cable for High-Density Intra-Data Centre Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Soma, Daiki / Sasaki, Tsubasa / Imamura, Katsunori / Wakayama, Yuta / Tsuritani, Takehiro

We propose a pluggable‑transceiver‑compatible aggregated multi‑core fibre cable for in-tra‑data‑centre optical wiring. By aggregating standard‑cladding four‑core fibres, the proposed design supports 2×400G‑DR4 links while reducing cable cross‑sectional area and weight by more than 86%. Error‑free transmission using commercial pluggable transceivers is confirmed at 1310 nm.

talks.title: We4-P90: 240-Gb/s Bipolar Dual-Polarization IM Coherent PON with 10-ns Preamble and 38-dB Power Budget Using 9-MHz DFB Laser
talks.abstract:
Authors: Huang, Dangui / Zhu, Yixiao / Pan, Yutong / Zhang, Tianhong / Zhang, Ziheng / Yang, Guangying / Man, Lina / Zhang, Yikun / Wang, Wenhao / Zhang, Ning / Zhang, Fan / Hu, Weisheng

We demonstrate bipolar dual-polarization intensity-modulation coherent PON leveraging sensitivity gain over unipolar modulation while mitigating frequency offset and phase noise with 9-MHz DFB laser. We use 10-ns short preamble to recover 240-Gb/s signal over 20-km SSMF at 38-dB power budget, supporting flexible rates of 120~300-Gb/s.

talks.title: We4-P91: Low-Complexity Hierarchical Polar Quantization for CPRI-Based Radio-over-Fibre Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Hongliang / Townsend, Paul / Ouyang, Xing

We propose a low-complexity, memory-efficient optimized polar quantization scheme with cross-ring continuous mapping for RoF systems. A 117 Gb/s/λ signal is transmitted over 40-km S-SMF, achieving ~8-dB SNR gain compared with conventional square-domain quantization under equivalent fronthaul capacity.

talks.title: We4-P92: Early-Warning Fiber Event Classification Operating over Commercial Single- and Dual-polarization Sources Using Stokes-Parameter Features and Lightweight Machine Learning
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dass, Devika / Sadighi, Leyla / Bjørnstad, Steinar / Ruffini, Marco

We present an SOP-based scheme for early-warning classification of 4-physical fiber-events (twisting/vibration/bending/tapping) over 20km field-fiber. Using a polarimeter monitoring different sources: single-polarized (SP)-unmodulated, SP-modulated, and dual-polarized (DP)-modulated sources, we achieve classification accuracies of 99.7%, 100%, and 94.5%, respectively, without requiring a dedicated sensing wavelength.

talks.title: We4-P93: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning Between Coherent Telemetry and Distributed Brillouin Sensing for Fiber Perturbation Analysis
talks.abstract:
Authors: Usmani, Fehmida / Bukovsky, Jan / Dejdar, Petr / Ranjha, Wadood Ur Rehman / Munster, Petr / Horvath, Tomas / Tomasov, Adrian / Furdek, Marija

We propose a contrastive learning (CL) framework for sensing of otherwise non explicitly represented environmental perturbations from coherent receivers’ telemetry data. Through alignment with Brillouin sensing data in latent space as ground truth, ∼96% CL accuracy in temperature-bin retrieval from telemetry data is experimentally demonstrated.

talks.title: We4-P94: A Widely Tunable ASE-Driven Optoelectronic Oscillator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Zhuoran / Bernal, Santiago / Plant, David / Chen, Lawrence

We experimentally demonstrated a single-mode ASE-driven optoelectronic oscillator tunable up to 25 GHz. Single-mode oscillation is enabled by cascaded zero-dispersion loops, while wide tunability is achieved through balanced photodetection for baseband suppression and chirp-like slicing for mitigating filter amplitude degradation induced by third-order dispersion.

talks.title: We4-P95: Ultra-low Phase Noise 58-GHz Optoelectronic Oscillator Driven by a Narrow-Linewidth Quantum Dot DFB Laser
talks.abstract:
Authors: Matsumoto, Atsushi / Umezawa, Toshimasa / Nakajima, Shinya / Akahane, Kouichi / Yamamoto, Naokatsu / Shinada, Satoshi

We demonstrate a 58.2 GHz optoelectronic oscillator using a narrow-linewidth quantum-dot DFB (QD-DFB) laser. Compared to a conventional MQW-DFB laser, the QD-DFB significantly reduces phase noise to -102.5 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset, achieving a 19 dB improvement with a 100 m fiber loop.

talks.title: We4-P96: A Hardware-Efficient FMCW-Based Point-to-Multipoint Forward Sensing Scheme Compatible with Existing PON Infrastructures
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zou, Yi / zhang, Chenbo / Zhu, Yixiao / Liu, Xu / Lin, Jingjing / Yang, Jiachuan / Hu, Weiwei / Hu, Weisheng / Chen, Zhangyuan / Xie, Xiaopeng

We propose a hardware-efficient FMCW-based P2MP sensing scheme seamlessly compatible with existing PON infrastructures. By introducing only passive components, namely an MZI and an ODL, at each ONU, we achieve simultaneous and unambiguous interrogation of all branches with a localization accuracy better than 10 m.

talks.title: We4-P97: Hybridization of sensing technologies to detect fibre distribution cabinets and environmental variations in a terrestrial fibre link to improve deployed fibre localization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hilbert, Tjorven / Azendorf, Florian / Philipp, Tobias / Dochhan, Annika / Pachnicke, Stephan

In this work, we used multi-modal sensing and monitoring approaches to find reference points within a communication fibre network. These points were identified by their spectral signature in the range of 1-15 Hz and their Brillouin frequency shift variations in the range of 5-30 MHz.

talks.title: We4-P98: Fully Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing Enabled by Kalman Filtering
talks.abstract:
Authors: Marin, Juan M. / Ermakov, Roman / Azendorf, Florian / Sandmann, André / Da Ros, Francesco / Zibar, Darko

Signal fading creates points along the fiber where phase cannot be extracted, so they are conventionally discarded. Instead, we propose a Kalman-based solution for ϕ-OTDR full-fiber monitoring. Experiments demonstrate phase and temperature estimation with approximately 15 times better spatial density than if removing these points.

talks.title: We4-P99: High-Bandwidth Branch-Ambiguity-Free Probing for Single-Wavelength DAS in PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Geyang / Choudhury, Pallab K. / Chen, Lian-Kuan / Awwad, Élie

We propose and validate new probing sequences achieving the bandwidth-branch-distance bound of a single-wavelength DAS over PON. Results show up to 300% improvement in acoustic bandwidth or 100% improvement in sensing distance compared to state-of-the-art schemes, resolving simultaneously branch ambiguity in event detection over drop-fibers.

talks.title: We4-P9: Inter-core Spontaneous Raman Scattering in a 39-core 3-mode/1-mode Heterogeneous Multi-core Fiber System
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sakaguchi, Jun / Furukawa, Hideaki

We systematically characterize the forward/backward inter-core spontaneous Raman scattering of a 39-core 3-mode/1-mode heterogenous multi-core fiber system. Low forward direction crosstalk is expected for most three-mode cores distant from the 1-mode core, indicating high potential of the system for use in classical-quantum coexisting transmission.

sessions.title: We5-A Network operation and fault management in optical networks
sessions.track: SC 10: Control and management of optical networks

talks.title: We5-A1: SDN Agents for IPoWDM Routers and Coherent Pluggables
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sgambelluri, Andrea / Sambo, Nicola / Castoldi, Piero / Cugini, Filippo

This tutorial presents an overview of the IPoWDM technology and devices, coherent pluggable transceivers and recent studies on SDN agents enabling the deep control of those devices, exposing standard NETCONF/YANG APIs, while envisioning the next future towards agentic paradigm.

talks.title: We5-A2: Experimental Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Soft-Fault Classification in Coherent Optical Transmission Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sun, Zhiming / Cai, Xiang / Fan, Runzhe / Yan, Xulong / Wang, Cen / Zhou, Xian / Zhang, Fan

We present a multimodal experimental dataset for soft-fault classification in coherent optical transmission systems. It contains 3463 receiver captures, 34 structured features, and four tensor modalities. Extra Trees achieves 0.9356 macro-F1 on the four-class benchmark, with WSS showing the clearest separation.

talks.title: We5-A3: Fault Prediction and Localization in Optical Networks Based on Incremental Tensor Network-GRU
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gao, Yuxuan / Rottondi, Cristina / Bianco, Andrea / Guo, Bingli / Sgambelluri, Andrea / Valcarenghi, Luca / Paolini, Emilio / Huang, Shanguo

An iTenGRU model is proposed for fault prediction and localization,achieving 91% prediction and 96% localization accuracy in the testbed.When retraining less than 1% of parameters on unseen faults, >93% prediction and 96% localization accuracy with respect to full retraining are still achieved.

sessions.title: We5-B Optical transmitters and transceivers
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: We5-B1: Progress of High-speed VCSELs and VCSEL-based Co-Packaging for Short Reach Communications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kuchta, Daniel

This talk will cover the state of art of VCSELs used for short reach data communications and VCSEL-based packaging solutions of co-packaged transceivers for scale-up applications.

talks.title: We5-B2: 19.1-THz Tunable Wideband TFLN/SiPh Hybrid Integrated 800G CFP2 Transceiver for AIDC Scale-Across Clusters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yan, Baoluo / Deng, Decai / Yang, Zhenqian / Qin, Tao / Zhu, Haiqing / Shen, Shikui / Zhang, Dongchen / Liu, Hong / Shi, Hu / Zhao, Zhiyong / Liu, Yangguang / Qiao, Kezhi

We demonstrate a CFP2 coherent transceiver with hybrid TFLN/SiPh COSA and ultra-wideband SOA, enabling 800G PS-16QAM across 19.1-THz S+C+L bands. Achieving 0-dBm output, >35-dB Tx OSNR, and 74.8% fiber saving, it addresses AIDC scale-across cluster demands.

talks.title: We5-B3: Industry’s First 12.8T 8×DR8 High-Density Liquid-Cooled 64-Channel Pluggable XPO Optical Module for Scale-Up
talks.abstract:
Authors: Priyadarshi, Sunil

This work presents a 12.8T liquid-cooled pluggable optical module addressing bandwidth and thermal challenges in AI data centers. The XPO architecture enables high-density silicon photonics integration. Measurements demonstrate 212 Gbps PAM4 performance, ~188 W power consumption, and improved thermal efficiency. ©2026 The Author(s)

talks.title: We5-B4: Advanced Industrial Silicon Photonics Platform on 300mm wafer for Optical Interconnect and Beyond
talks.abstract:
Authors: Boeuf, Frederic / Bataille, Louise-Eugenie / Virot, Leopold / Allegret, Stephane / Bruel, Guillaume / Frauenrath, Marvin / Guerber, Sylvain / Myko, André / Fowler, Daivid / Plihon, Aurelia / Henry, David / Bellemin-Comte, Amelie / Volpert, Marion / Kempf, Eva / Lazzari, Lorenzo / Monfray, Stephane / Milon, Victor / Blampey, Benjamin / Gellida, Sylvie / Cremer, Sebastien

We review the development of 300mm wafer Silicon Photonics platform for 200Gbps/lane and its extension towards Co-Packaged-Optics (CPO) through the addition of 110GHz GeSi electro-absorption modulator (EAM), 70GHz Micro-Ring Modulators (MRM) and Through Silicon Via (TSV). Investigations on integration of III-V materials is also discussed.

sessions.title: We5-D Optical wireless technologies for next-generation networks systems
sessions.track: SC 09: Free-space optics and optical wireless technologies

talks.title: We5-D1: In-Orbit Demonstration of Dual-ITLA Silicon Photonics Coherent Optical Module Supporting 100/200 Gbps Communications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Quan / Wei, Fang / Hu, Xiao / Zhao, Kun / Cao, Quan / Lu, Luluzi / Liang, Hong / Song, Jinwen / Yan, Yi / Du, Jianlai / Chu, Wei / Chai, Jiao / Cao, Yun / Sun, Jianfeng / Cai, Haiwen

We demonstrate the in-orbit validation of a dual-ITLA silicon photonics coherent optical module for LEO inter-satellite laser communication. In-orbit loopback test at 492 km LEO confirms the key performances at both 100 Gbps and 200 Gbps PM-QPSK modes.

talks.title: We5-D2: Hybrid Free-space-optics and Millimetre-wave D-band Trans-mitter enabled by Optically Harmonically Locked Lasers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhou, Zichuan / Htay, Zun / Kassem, Amany / Darwazeh, Izzat / Liu, Zhixin

We demonstrated hybrid free-space optics (FSO) and D-band (110-170GHz) millimetre wave transmitter enabled by a single phase-locked laser pair, simultaneously enabling ultra-low RF phase noise and optical linewidth for communications. Based on this, we further study combined capacity with beam angle misalignment using >100Gb/s signalling.

talks.title: We5-D3: Optical Satellite Communication Systems – A Canadian Perspective
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hranilovic, Steve / Flannigan, Liam / Bradley, Jonathan D.B. / Deen, M. Jamal / Knights, Andrew P. / Kumar, Shiva / Xu, Chang-Qing / Kleiman, Rafael

Optical satellite communications is maturing globally, yet Canada faces unique challenges including high-latitude orbital constraints, persistent cloud cover, and connectivity for remote northern communities. This paper surveys recent Canadian research at McMaster University highlighting advances in coherent receivers, mid-infrared links, silicon photonics, and adaptive optics.

sessions.title: We5-E PON sensing, monitoring & energy efficiency
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: We5-E1: Sensing in PON – techniques and applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Maes, Jochen / Van Rompaey, Robbe / Füllner, Christoph / Straub, Michael / Guerrier, Sterenn / Borkowski, Robert / Vijayan, Kovendhan / Van Veen, Dora / Houtsma, Vincent

We provide an overview of use cases and methodologies for sensing in passive optical networks. With its point-to-multipoint nature, we address the potential to resolve events between drop fibers, and the preference for low-cost central-side solutions.

talks.title: We5-E2: Burst-Mode Polarization Sensing and ODN Monitoring for Aerial Fiber Using a Commercial 25G PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Houtsma, Vincent / Van Veen, Doutje / Borkowski, Robert / Das, Sandip / Straub, Michael / Vijayan, Kovendhan / Van Rompaey, Robbe / Maes, Jochen

We report on a low-cost polarization sensing element located at OLT side of a commercial 25G PON system to enable ODN monitoring. Sensing is performed in burst-mode on upstream PON wavelength. Field results using aerial fiber are reported as well.

talks.title: We5-E3: Experimental Demonstration of Simultaneous SOP Sensing on All Active ONUs in Upstream GPON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Pellegrini, Saverio / Greborio, Laura / Rizzelli, Giuseppe / Ferrero, Valter / Pagano, Annachiara / Gaudino, Roberto

We experimentally investigate SOP-based sensing in upstream GPON using a single OLT-side polarimeter, focusing on sampling rate, synchronization, averaging strategies, and resulting SOP angular deviation. We show coarse localization capabilities, discriminating whether vibrations occurred on the feeder or in each distribution fiber.

talks.title: We5-E4: Experimental Evaluation of Energy Saving in XGS-PON ONU
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chanclou, Philippe / Le Huérou, Stéphane / Saliou, Fabienne / Simon, Gaël / Potet, Jérémy

This paper experimentally evaluates XGS-PON ONU doze mode, demonstrating up to 1 Watt energy savings while preserving service continuity. It analyzes how low-power and aware intervals affect consumption, and shows practical bandwidth–energy trade-offs for 128 shared ONUs and supporting greener broadband network operation.

sessions.title: We5-F Quantum devices
sessions.track: SC 11: Quantum communications, physical layer security, and optical quantum technologies

talks.title: We5-F1: Contextuality-based Integrated Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator
talks.abstract:
Authors: Genzini, Maddalena / Vigliar, Caterina / Zahidy, Mujtaba / Tebyanian, Hamid / Gajda, Andrzej / Petermann, Klaus / Zimmermann, Lars / Bacco, Davide / Da Ros, Francesco

We demonstrate an integrated semi-device-independent quantum random number generator based on contextuality. By implementing a KCBS inequality test on a programmable photonic circuit, we certify genuine randomness and achieve an extractable rate of 0.077 bits per round, enabling scalable, chip-based certified QRNGs.

talks.title: We5-F2: High-Speed Quantum Random Number Generator Using Flip-Chip Bonded Laser
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bomhals, Axl / Bastiaens, Sarah / Cammarata, Simone / Bruynsteen, Cédric / Yin, Xin

We present an advancement in quantum random number generator integration by using a fully integrated vacuum fluctuation-based noise source containing a flip-chip bonded laser and low-noise TIA to produce secure random numbers in real-time at rates up to 87.46 Gbit/s.

talks.title: We5-F3: Engineering Deterministic Quantum Light Sources at Telecom Wavelengths
talks.abstract:
Authors: Holewa, Pawel / Polczynska, Karolina E. / Ruiz, Christian / Zieba-Ostój, Emilia / Vajner, Daniel A. / Mikulicz, Marek Grzegorz / Lefaucher, Baptiste / Mrowinski, Pawel / Wyborski, Pawel Daniel / Munkhbat, Battulga / Xiong, Meng / Yvind, Kresten / Gregersen, Niels / Huck, Alexander / Heindel, Tobias / Syperek, Marcin / Semenova, Elizaveta

Deterministic telecom quantum light sources are limited by stochastic emitter properties and placement. We present paths to address these issues: near-critical InAs/InP quantum dot (QD) epitaxy, Stark tuning, deterministic cavity fabrication, and site-controlled epitaxy,- enabling QD device fabrication with improved yield, tunability, and single-photon purity.

talks.title: We5-F4: Ultra-Compact and High-Bandwidth Silicon Photonic Chip for Fully Integrated CV-QKD Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Li, Taijie / Zhang, Gong

We demonstrate a fully integrated CV-QKD chip system including a laser chip, a transimpedance amplifier chip, and silicon photonic chips, which features a compact micro-ring IQ modulator and a high-speed homodyne detector operating up to >16 GHz frequency

talks.title: We5-F5: Towards Scalable Quantum Clock Synchronization Networks Using InGaAs Single Photon Avalanche Detectors and High-Brightness Integrated Entanglement Photon Pair Sources
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sozos, Kostas / Kourelias, Panagiotis / Nicolaides, Hercules / Gradkowski, Kamil / He, Xiuyun / Nudds, Noreen / Bazin, Alexandre / Stathis, Aristeidis / Ntanos, Argiris / Apostolopoulos, Dimitris / Avramopoulos, Hercules / Kaminski, Veronika / Protsenko, Ekaterina / Vigliar, Caterina / Tosi, Alberto / Mesaritakis, Charis / Giannoulis, Giannis / Bogris, Adonis

We experimentally showcase the potential of ps-level precision quantum clock synchronization based on silicon nitride microring resonators as sources of entangled photons. We also propose a quantum clock synchronisation architecture that improves scalability requiring only one single-photon avalanche detector per user at the server side.

sessions.title: We5-G Advance phase and timing recovery
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: We5-G1: Mitigation of Error Bursts after Pilot-Aided Carrier Phase Recovery
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cui, Han / R. Kschischang, Frank / Karlsson, Magnus / Agrell, Erik

We propose two phase estimation error (PEE)-aware schemes for bursty phase noise channels: one based on average PEE and one capturing bursty PEE statistics. Simulations show that both outperform the conventional scheme, with the latter performing best under strong burst conditions.

talks.title: We5-G2: Phase-Recovery-Free 6bit/4D Coherent Transmission Using Subcarrier-Joint Modulation for Large-Linewidth Lasers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhang, Tianhong / Pan, Yutong / Zhu, Yixiao / Wang, Wenhao / Zhang, Ning / Zhang, Fan

We propose a subcarrier-joint modulation scheme and experimentally demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first high-order coherent transmission without phase recovery in a large-linewidth system. Robust 80-km operation and strong linewidth tolerance are verified under 100-kHz and 1-MHz lasers.

talks.title: We5-G3: Baud-Rate Timing Recovery with 1UI DGD Tolerance for Dual Polarization Coherent Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Su, Xiaofei / Ye, Tong / Li, Jingnan / Nakashima, Hisao / Hoshida, Takeshi / Aoki, Yasuhiko / Tao, Zhenning

A baud-rate timing recovery to mitigate the impact of polarization mode dispersion is proposed and validated by simulations and experiments. It does not rely on successful PMD compensation and carrier phase recovery and achieves 1 UI DGD tolerance, enhancing robustness in baud-rate coherent systems.

talks.title: We5-G4: Receiver-Side Compensation of TI-DAC Offset Mismatch in Optical Transceivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Qiu, Meng / Tang, Xuefeng / Fung, Yiki / Li, Chuandong

We propose a calibration and compensation technique, performed in receiver digital signal processing, to mitigate effects of offset mismatch in digital-to-analog converters (DAC) with time-interleaving (TI). It enables on-demand re-calibration during system operation thanks to its post-processing nature, and achieves effective compensation with low complexity.

talks.title: We5-G5: Modeling and Mitigation of Equalization-Enhanced Phase Noise
talks.abstract:
Authors: Geiger, Benedikt / Buchali, Fred / Aref, Vahid / Schmalen, Laurent

Equalization-enhanced phase noise (EEPN) emerges as a key performance limitation in high symbol-rate coherent transmission systems. In this paper, we highlight recent advances in modeling EEPN and show that the temporal Gaussian noise model reproduces the characteristic burst-like SNR degradation, enabling efficient system simulation.

sessions.title: We5-C Integrated sensing and communication
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: We5-C1: Experimental Assessment of CP-DAS+DWDM Co- and Counter-propagation in C+L Bands
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hernández-Martín, Laura / Pellegrini, Saverio / Rizzelli, Giuseppe / Ania-Castañón, Juan Diego / Martins, Hugo Fidalgo / Gaudino, Roberto

An in-depth experimental characterization of the compatibility between C+L band DWDM coherent transmission and chirped-pulse DAS is performed under realistic conditions, showcasing strong impairments to the telecom signals in co-propagating configurations, but robust performance in counter-propagation, with DAS performance largely unaffected in both cases.

talks.title: We5-C2: Field Trial of SDN-controlled Point-to-MultiPoint Sensing of Weak Urban Events in 50G HS-PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fylaktaki, Margarita / Vargemidou, Maria / Saliou, Fabienne / Deleurme, Erwan / Raptis, Savvas I. / Bideau, Maël / Vagionas, Chris / Pleros, Nikos / Chanclou, Philippe / Miliou, Amalia

The first field-trial of Point-to-MultiPoint sensing in field-deployed 50G HS-PONs is demonstrated exploiting real-time SDN-allocation of its wavelength-tunable sensing-channels and wavelet-transform-based DSP-techniques for detection of weak non-stationary urban events beyond the limits of conventional Fourier-transform spectrograms

talks.title: We5-C3: Advancing Forward-Transmission Fibre Sensing for Precise Event Localisation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fang, Jian / Huang, Ming-Fang / Ip, Ezra / Kotrla, Scott / Mundt, Jeffrey / Huang, Yue-Kai / Wang, Ting / Aono, Yoshiaki

We review recent progress in forward-transmission fibre sensing from a practical perspective, revisit the fundamental challenges in the localisation performance, and discuss possible approaches to improve event localisation accuracy.

talks.title: We5-C4: Large-Scale Integrated Sensing and Communication over Bidirectional 200-Gb/s Coherent PON with 256 ONUs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wu, Qi / Qu, Shuai / Tang, Zhihang / Zhang, Xiaoying / Lu, Chao / Zhong, Kangping / Lau, Alan Pak Tao / Yan, Yaxi

We experimentally demonstrate a large-scale PON that integrates distributed optical fiber sensing with bidirectional single-wavelength 200-Gb/s transmission. The system achieves 37-dB optical power budgets, 25-m localization accuracy, and supports up to 256 ONUs with distinguishable multi-point simultaneous vibrations.

talks.title: We5-C5: Over-80-km Transmission of Image-Derived Semantic Data via a Distributed Fiber-Optic Acoustic Sensing Link
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kohno, Wataru / Ozharar, Sarper / Li, Yaowen / Murakami, Shuji / Hu, Junqiang / Wang, Ting

We demonstrate underwater acoustic transmission of image-derived semantic messages using an over-80-km distributed fiber-optic acoustic sensing link with chirp-coded pulse interrogation, Raman amplification, and fiber-optic hydrophones. At 50~bps with Raman amplification, 100 scene-graph messages (21,193 bits) are delivered without observed errors (BER upper bound $<4.72\times10^{-5}$

sessions.title: We5-H Coupled core MCF systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: We5-H1: 1.17-Pbps C + Extended-L Band 68-km Transmission over Field-Installed 12-Coupled-Core Fibre Cable
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shibahara, Kohki / Kawai, Akira / Hoshi, Megumi / Shimizu, Shimpei / Nakamura, Masanori / Hamaoka, Fukutaro / Imada, Ryota / Sakamoto, Taiji / Arikawa, Manabu / Hosokawa, Kohei / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We demonstrate 10.2-THz-bandwidth 12-coupled-core-fibre multiband transmission over a field-installed cable, achieving a record 1.17-Pbps net capacity (12 SDM × 68 WDM × 1.43 Tbps/λ/SDM). Real-time FPGA-based MIMO-DSP prototype also confirms stable BER performance for 1-GBd QPSK with C+extended-L band spatially-coupled channel copropagation.

talks.title: We5-H2: Real-Time Dual-Polarization IM-DD Transmission over Coupled-Core 4-Core Fiber Using All-Optical MIMO and FPGA Transceivers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Grillanda, Stefano / Fontaine, Nicolas / Idjadi, Mohamad Hossein / Kim, Kwangwoong / Winter, David / Tran, Cuong / Chen, Haoshuo / Ryf, Roland / Arnould, Aymeric / Oezsuna, Pamir / Rademacher, Georg / Freund, Ronald / Nagashima, Takuji / Hayashi, Tetsuya

We perform the first real-time dual-polarization IM-DD transmission over 5 km of randomly-coupled 4-core fiber using a silicon photonic all-optical MIMO chip and a real-time DSP engine, made by hard-silicon transceivers inside an FPGA. We show real-time demultiplexing and tracking of 10 Gb/s NRZ-OOK channels.

talks.title: We5-H3: Power-Safe Inter-Core Split-Pumping for C+L-Band Distributed Raman Amplified Transmission Using Randomly Coupled 12-Core Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Taguchi, Kouki / Shimizu, Shimpei / Shibahara, Kohki / Imada, Ryota / Sakamoto, Taiji / Nakajima, Kazuhide / Kobayashi, Takayuki / Miyamoto, Yutaka

We propose an inter-core split-pumping scheme for power-safe operation in distributed Raman-amplified transmission over randomly coupled multicore fibers. A ≥5-dB distributed gain (up to 8.3 dB) in a 51-km 12-core fiber over the 10.2-THz C+L-band is demonstrated with <800 mW launched into each SMF section

talks.title: We5-H4: Unrepeatered 312.5 km Transmission Over a Randomly-Coupled Multicore Fiber With Bidirectional Raman Amplification
talks.abstract:
Authors: Luis, Ruben / Kalla, Besma / Orsuti, Daniele / Lasagni, Chiara / Antonelli, Cristian / Nakanishi, Michihiro / Takasaka, Shigehiro / Yoshida, Junji / Tomina, Shuhei / Sakuma, Hirotaka / Hasegawa, Takemi / Hayashi, Tetsuya / Bradley, Thomas / Okonkwo, Chigo / Furukawa, Hideaki

We demonstrate a 39.9 nm, C-band, 312.5 km, 160.8 Tb/s transmission on a 4-core, randomly-coupled, multicore fiber. The link uses bidirectional Raman amplification with conventional and incoherent pumps shared over all cores through random coupling in the fiber.

sessions.title: We5-I VCSELs
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: We5-I1: 2.3 Tbit/s Backside-Emitting 1060 nm VCSEL Array on Silicon Interposer for CPO Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kohli, Manuel / Ganzhorn, Marc / Eberhard, Franz / Maineult, Wilfried / Mueller, Rokhaya / Marcon, Leonardo / Taeschler, Philipp / Schaefer, Christian M. / Kaiser, Wolfgang / Thies, Achim / Bonfrate, Donato / Spieser, Martin / Teissier, Jean / Tirelli, Stefano / Zibik, Evgeny

Communication inside AI datacenters requires highest bandwidth-densities and energy-efficiency. We demonstrate a 2x9 VCSEL array at 128 Gbit/s PAM-4 (2.3 Tbit/s) with 160 µm pitch. We further show 32 Gbit/s NRZ operation up to 125° C without DSP and no power degradation at 125° C.

talks.title: We5-I2: 62-GHz Bandwidth 1060-nm Metal-Aperture VCSELs Enabling 256-Gbps PAM4 and Modal-Dispersion-Free SMF/MMF Links
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ibrahim, Hameeda / Hassan, Ahmed / Gu, Xiaodong / Koyama, Fumio

We report record 62-GHz bandwidth in 1060-nm metal-aperture coupled-cavity VCSELs with highly-strained QWs and optimized damping. These devices enable 256-Gbps PAM4 back-to-back and 200-Gbps over 1-km SMF. Additionally, SMF-mode-filtered 500-m MMF (OM4) links exhibit >50-GHz link bandwidth with ±4-µm VCSEL-coupling tolerance, ensuring modal-dispersion-free MMF transmission.

talks.title: We5-I3: Low-Threshold Single-Frequency Intra-Cavity VCSELs for Scalable Cryogenic Computing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Namvar, Behzad / Rajala, Patrik / Hakkarainen, Teemu / Guina, Mircea / Viheriälä, Jukka

VCSELs suitable for cryogenic optical interconnects to superconducting processors are demonstrated. An intra-cavity design was used to minimize Joule losses and ensure high thermal dissipation. Single-mode operation with SMSR > 45 dB and 130 µA threshold is demonstrated at 5 K.

talks.title: We5-I4: 1060 nm back-emitting VCSEL modulated at 106 Gbps PAM4 transmission over 100 m OM3 MMF for NPO Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hu, Huawen / Ji, Yipeng / Zhao, Binbin / Zhang, Sui / Li, Shasha / Chen, Jianqiang / Zhang, Zhenglai / Shen, ChihChiang / Wang, Jiaxing / Chang-Hasnain, Connie J.

We demonstrate 1060 nm back‑emitting VCSELs with 37 GHz bandwidth, −149.5 dB/Hz RIN, and transmits 50 Gbps NRZ and 106 Gbps PAM4 over 100 m OM3 fiber. Accelerated aging predicts >1000‑year lifetime under normal operation, promising for low‑cost optical interconnects.

talks.title: We5-I5: Performance, Reliability and Manufacturability of 1060nm VCSEL Arrays for AI Data Center Scale-Up
talks.abstract:
Authors: Peters, Matthew

Lumentum’s 1060nm multi-mode VCSEL arrays will enable scalable parallel optical interconnects for high-speed links with excellent power efficiency, thermal performance, and reliability making them well suited for both scale-up bandwidth density and scale-out reach in next-generation data center architectures. ©2026 Matthew Peters

sessions.title: Conference dinner at Finca Nadales
Morning coffee
Th1-A Novel modulators
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: Th1-A1: Silicon Slow-Light-Based Modulators and High-Efficiency Optical Transmitters
talks.abstract:
Authors: Baba, Toshihiko / Kawahara, Keisuke

We present CMOS-compatible silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators in which slow-light phase shifters enable a small footprint suitable for dense integration, high-speed at 200 Gb/s and beyond, and low bit-energy consumption below 100 fJ/bit. Such modulators also enable reduced transmitter power consumption through an open-collector configuration.

talks.title: Th1-A2: Epitaxial PLZT Mach–Zehnder Modulators with Low Vπ?L, Low Loss, and High-Speed Operation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nashimoto, Keiichi

Epitaxial PLZT Mach–Zehnder modulators achieve Vπ·L of 0.21 V·cm with propagation loss of 0.8–0.9 dB/cm. Small-signal measurements show ~25 GHz bandwidth, extendable beyond 40 GHz. The devices also support high optical power operation up to 30 dBm.

sessions.title: Th1-B Turbulence mitigation in free-space optical communications
sessions.track: SC 09: Free-space optics and optical wireless technologies

talks.title: Th1-B1: Coherent Free-Space Optical Communications in AtmosphericTurbulence: Principles, Limits, and Emerging Strategies
talks.abstract:
Authors: Belmonte, Aniceto

Coherent free-space optical communication is fundamentally limited by atmospheric turbulence. This tutorial presents a unified statistical modal framework for analyzing performance limits and reviewing mitigation strategies, highlighting statistically matched transmission modes that enable robust and scalable link design without instantaneous wavefront correction.

talks.title: Th1-B2: Turbulence-Resilient MMF-MCF Interface for FSO-to-Fibre SDM Transmission via Adaptive Wavefront Shaping
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hua, Xuchen / Liu, Zhuyixiao / Zhang, Mingming / Wu, Hao / Zhou, Huibin / Tang, Ming

We demonstrate an interface between free-space OAM-multiplexed link and multi-core fibre link using an MMF-MCF coupling structure with wavefront shaping. We achieve SDM transmission of two 32-GBaud-QPSK channels under turbulence (D/r0 ~14), with channel crosstalk reduced by 12.6 dB compared to conventional mode demultiplexing approach.

talks.title: Th1-B3: Reducing Turbulence-Induced Outages in a Deployed Terrestrial Free-Space Optical Communication Link via Interleaving
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gumus, Kadir / Van Vliet, Vincent / Van Den Hout, Menno / Bradley, Thomas / Tangdiongga, Eduward / Okonkwo, Chigo

We present an experimental study of data interleaving for terrestrial free-space optical communication over a 4.6 km urban testbed. Results demonstrate a two-order-of-magnitude reduction in outage probability. A dependency between measured turbulence strength, interleaver length, and achievable data rate is revealed, enabling robust system design.

sessions.title: Th1-D Advanced photonic integration
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: Th1-D1: Silicon Photonic CWDM Filter with Compact Footprint, Low Loss, Flat-Top Transmission and High Yield
talks.abstract:
Authors: Deng, Qingzhong / Elshazly, Alaa / Magdziak, Rafal / Witters, Liesbeth / Bipul, Swetanshu / Chakrabarti, Maumita / Velenis, Dimitrios / Ferraro, Filippo / Sar, Huseyin / Verheyen, Peter / Absil, Philippe / Ossieur, Peter / Jadli, Imene / Van Campenhout, Joris

A novel silicon photonic CWDM filter design is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The design has achieved flat-top transmission across all dies on a wafer, with a device footprint of 48×25µm2, an insertion loss of 0.24±0.18dB, and a channel central wavelength standard deviation of 0.77nm.

talks.title: Th1-D2: Dual Self-Injection Locking for Hybrid-Integrated Laser Linewidth Reduction and Stabilization
talks.abstract:
Authors: Esmaeeli, Omid / Mohammad Khani, Jamal / Bahrani, Masih / Yuan, Tenna / Chrostowski, Lukas / Shekhar, Sudip

Short on-chip external cavities improve laser stability but offer limited linewidth reduction, while long reflections narrow linewidth. We combine phase- and amplitude-controlled short and long cavities in a zero-process-change silicon-on-insulator circuit to simultaneously reduce linewidth and enhance stability against reflections in a hybrid-integrated DFB laser.

talks.title: Th1-D3: Field demonstration of an unshielded InP photonic integrated circuit (PIC) onboard a PocketQube picosatellite payload
talks.abstract:
Authors: Delgado Mendinueta, José Manuel / Guzmán, Robinson / César-Cuello, Jéssica / Alonso, Eduardo / González-Guerrero, Luis / Carpintero Del Barrio, Guillermo

We developed a picosatellite payload with a PIC consisting of a laser and a photodiode, mounted with no metallic shielding. Experimental field results demonstrate a success in the mission after more than one year orbiting the earth, showing no degradation due to ionizing radiation.

talks.title: Th1-D4: Monolithically Integrated Quad-Line Comb Generation in Thin-Film LiNbO3 enabling 3.2 Tb/s Superchannel Transmission
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chowanek, Fabian / Emmerich, Robert / Schmidt-Langhorst, Carsten / Schubert, Colja / Chen, Hanwei / Hoshida, Takeshi / Freund, Ronald

We realize a 3.2 Tb/s superchannel (4x800 Gb/s/λ) at 1550 nm by using monolithic integrated quad-carrier generation. The fabricated TFLN device exhibits 36% on-chip conversion efficiency and 32 dB suppression of interjacent sidelines. Employing 81.1 GBd DP-64QAM, the BER after 100.8 km remains below 2E-2.

talks.title: Th1-D5: Low loss Digitally Tunable Dispersion Controller Using Ridge Waveguides
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ma, Ruitao / Liu, Shujun / Wang, Zexu / Yao, Yuyan / Yu, Zejie / Dai, Daoxin

We demonstrate a low-loss digitally tunable dispersion controller based on rib waveguides on a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform. The device achieves a digital dispersion tuning range of −251.87 to +262.33 ps/nm over the 1544–1553.2 nm wavelength band.

sessions.title: Th1-E Sub-THz transmission and photonic sensing techniques
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: Th1-E1: 400-Gbit/s Net Transmission Over a 56-m Single-Carrier and Single-Aperture Dual-Polarization Sub-THz Link
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dittmer, Joel / Pilori, Dario / Bhutani, Akanksha / Beuthan, Felix / Seidel, Josefine / Mezger, Yanick / Tessmann, Axel / Wagner, Sandrine / Nolte, Lisa / Li, Haizheng / Freude, Wolfgang / Koos, Christian / Thomas, Zwick / Schmalen, Laurent / Randel, Sebastian

We demonstrate a single-carrier and dual-polarization wireless point-to-point transmission at 287 GHz over 56 m with a net data rate of 400 Gbit/s using a single aperture. We employ a novel mHEMT receiver and PCS-16-QAM at 64 GBd, compliant with IEEE 802.15.3d.

talks.title: Th1-E2: In-band Noise Mitigation of Broadband Chirped Signals Based on Joint Time-Frequency Photonic Processing
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Xinyi / Crockett, Benjamin / Sun, Hao / Azaña, José

We demonstrate a real-time microwave photonic approach for in-band noise mitigation using time–frequency domain processing. In the experiment, chirped signals with up to 23-GHz bandwidth are recovered under strong optical noise, achieving up to ~9 dB SNR improvements for high-speed applications.

talks.title: Th1-E3: Demonstration of Photonic Chip-based Ultra-high-resolution Dual-band Microwave Imaging of Non-cooperative Targets
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ma, Weichao / Shen, Zichao / Liu, Jianwei / Li, Wangzhe

To break electronic bandwidth bottleneck limited frequency band and resolution, and architectural constraints from generic discrete components, a photonic transceiver chip for radar is presented. It enables concurrent dual-band ultra-high-resolution imaging, demonstrating the first photonic chip-based microwave imaging of non-cooperative targets in realistic environment.

talks.title: Th1-E4: Pulsed Interferometry Towards Real Time PON Monitoring with Feeder and Drop Fibres Discrimination
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fasano, Marco / Karydis, Georgios Aias / Parolari, Paola / Madaschi, Andrea / Mesaritakis, Charis / Bogris, Adonis / Boffi, Pierpaolo

We present a non-invasive interferometric method for simultaneous and unambiguous monitoring of PON drop fibres. Drop fibre discrimination is demonstrated with a 30 km feeder fibre deployed in Athens, even with 1:32 splitting ratio and 52 dB budget losses.

talks.title: Th1-E5: Gain-switched DOFC for real-time interrogation of FBGs
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wei, Minghao / Mcardle, Conor / Rosado, Alejandro / Nagar, Malhar A. / Janner, Davide / Anandarajah, Prince

We demonstrate a real-time fibre Bragg grating interrogation system using externally injected gain-switched dual optical frequency comb and embedded receiver. The system achieves interrogation rates up to 1 kHz, while a minimum Bragg wavelength tracking uncertainty of 64.9 fm is obtained at reduced measurement rate.

sessions.title: Th1-F Programmable photonics: architectures, control and applications
Th1-G Ai-training in optical networks
sessions.track: SC 06: Architecture, modelling and performance of optical networks

talks.title: Th1-G1: Modeling the Impact of Fiber Latency on Compute-Communication Overlap in Geo-Distributed Multi-Datacenter AI Training
talks.abstract:
Authors: Papavasileiou, Ioannis / Prabhakar, Sairam / Deo, Indu Kant / Makovejs, Sergejs

We use discrete-event simulation to quantify the impact of fiber latency on the efficacy of geo-distributed AI model training with data parallelism. We conclude that the optimum distances between two AI clusters is 10-100km, over which hollow-core fiber enables 25% higher compute-communication overlap.

talks.title: Th1-G2: Accurate and Dynamic Network Topology Representation based on Functional Block-based Disaggregation for a Common Reference of Network Digital Twins
talks.abstract:
Authors: Ishii, Kiyo / Kunita, Kazuya / Matsuura, Hiroyuki / Namiki, Shu / Mizutani, Kenji

We develop a data platform integrating component-level topology and port-based reservations using a relational database for optical network digital twins. Field-testbed experiments evaluate the execution times of digital- and physical-space update operations, demonstrating timely and consistent synchronization and its role as a real-time common reference.

talks.title: Th1-G3: Agent-to-Agent Protocol Enhanced Multi-Agent Coordination for Autonomous Service Provisioning in Agentic Optical Networks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cui, Zihao / Song, Yuchen / Li, Shengnan / Pang, Yue / Zhang, Min / Wang, Danshi

The A2A protocol is implemented into a multi-agent system for autonomous service provisioning in optical networks. The test results demonstrate reliable end-to-end execution across heterogeneous agents, with 100% routing accuracy and low overhead, supporting interoperable and scalable optical network O&M.

talks.title: Th1-G4: Anything over Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing with Programmable Data Planes and Software Defined Networking
talks.abstract:
Authors: Bermudez Serna, Cristian / Diederich, Philip / Mas-Machuca, Carmen

This work proposes using Programmable Data Plane (PDP) switches with Digital Coherent Optical (DCO) pluggables to enable Anything over Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (XoDWDM) Open Line Systems (OLSs) with Software-Defined Networking (SDN) control plane. Feasibility is verified in a testbed using hardware PDP switches.

talks.title: Th1-G5: Trade-Offs of AI-based Optical Performance Monitoring and Sensing Techniques
talks.abstract:
Authors: Natalino, Carlos / Kaeval, Kaida / Wosinska, Lena

Modern optical networks leverage AI/ML for performance monitoring and fiber sensing across Phi-OTDR/DAS and SOP technologies. We present a unified data-rate framework, showing that monitoring precision choices impact the generated data volumes over nine orders of magnitude, and analyze AI/ML processing trade-offs across these configurations.

sessions.title: Th1-C Photodiodes
sessions.track: SC 02: Discrete photonic devices and technologies

talks.title: Th1-C1: Record Gain-Bandwidth Product Si-Ge Avalanche Photodiode Enabling an 8x300 Gbps DWDM Receiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cheng, Chao / Yu, Xishan / Liu, Qian / Bu, Xianglin / Bao, Shen / Xue, Jintao / Zhang, Wenfu / Wang, Binhao

We demonstrate a Si-Ge avalanche photodiode with a record 9460 GHz gain-bandwidth product via inductive peaking, achieving a 55 GHz bandwidth and a peak gain of 172. Integrated with dual-ring filters on an SOI platform, it enables an 8×300 Gbps PAM4 DWDM receiver.

talks.title: Th1-C2: 100-GHz and >0.5-A/W Balanced Photodiodes with Interference-Enhanced Absorption in O- and C-Bands
talks.abstract:
Authors: Yamada, Yuki / Araki, Yusuke / Hoshi, Takuya / Kosuga, Shohei / Nakamura, Takahiro / Tatsumi, Shoko / Nakajima, Fumito

We demonstrate vertical-illumination InGaAs/InP balanced photodiodes (PDs) using interference-enhanced absorption for high-speed coherent detection. O-band- and C-band-optimized PDs achieve 100 GHz bandwidth, 0.52 A/W responsivity, 0.06 nA dark current, <0.1 dB polarization-dependent loss (PDL), and <-35 dB common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR).

talks.title: Th1-C3: Bias-free operational 200 GHz bandwidth photodetector toward 800 Gbps/ lane communication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Umezawa, Toshimasa / Nakajima, Shinya / Matsumoto, Atsushi / Yamaguchi, Yuya / Akahane, Kouichi / Yamamoto, Naokatsu / Shinada, Satoshi

We proposed a bias-free operational 200-GHz photodetector assuming an integrated photoreceiver with a transimpedance amplifier toward the next-generation 800-Gbps per lane optical transceiver. The device performance of its high-baud-rate signal detection are discussed.

talks.title: Th1-C4: 100 GHz Ge/Si Avalanche Photodiodes Enabling Net 400 Gbps Data Reception at a Low Voltage of 5 V
talks.abstract:
Authors: Shahin, Amir / Coughlan, Conor / Singh, Nishant / Kobbi, Hakim / Dasilva, Leandro / Cammarata, Simone / Vankerrebrouck, Joris / Jakanadan, Shalini / Loo, Roger / Bipul, Swetanshu / Jadli, Imene / Yin, Xin / Aktas, Ozan / Ferraro, Filippo / Ossieur, Peter / Vanthourhout, Dries / Vancampenhout, Joris

We present Ge/Si avalanche photodiodes operating at low voltages (<6.5 V) achieving BWs of 100 GHz and 50 GHz at 1.8 A/W and 3.7 A/W responsivity levels across the O- and C-bands, enabling net 400 Gbps PAM-4 data link demonstration below the FEC threshold.

talks.title: Th1-C5: High Performance Waveguide GeSi Avalanche Photodiode Fully-integrated on a 220nm Silicon Photonics Platform
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wu, Jiliang / Qi, Fan / Cai, Pengfei / Shi, Bin / Hong, Chingyin / Chiu, Tehuang / Hou, Guanghui / Zhao, Jiaxing / Sun, Ming / He, Zengwen / Pan, Dong

We demonstrate a 100Gbps Ge/Si waveguide APD integrated with low loss SiN edge couplers and other components on a 220nm SOI platform, achieving ultra-low dark currents and record sensitivity. Our results offer a high-density integration path for APDs in high-link budget and low-power dissipation scenarios.

talks.title: Th1-C6: Heterogeneous Integration of Low Loss Si3N4 Waveguides and High-Speed Si-Ge Photodiodes
talks.abstract:
Authors: Souleiman, Amin / Peyrou, Martin / Virot, Léopold / Routier, Baptiste / Dunoyer, Nicolas / Brision, Stéphane / Hartmann, Jean-Michel / Larrey, Vincent / Fournel, Franck / Lima, Gabriel / Mathieu, Vincent / Kerdiles, Sébastien / Faugier-Tovar, Jonathan / Wilmart, Quentin

We demonstrate a Ge photodiode heterogeneously integrated on a low-loss Si3N4 200mm platform, achieving a 3dB bandwidth beyond 50GHz at 1550nm. This approach enables high-speed photodetection while leveraging low-loss waveguides, compatible with Kerr frequency comb generation, paving the way for highly scalable DWDM transceivers.

sessions.title: Th1-H Coherent systems
sessions.track: SC 05: Optical transmission systems

talks.title: Th1-H1: High Capacity Coherent Systems: EEPN Characterization, System Impact and Mitigation Options
talks.abstract:
Authors: Buchali, Fred

Equalization-enhanced phase noise (EEPN) is a critical impairment in high-symbol-rate coherent optical systems. This paper analyses EEPN characteristics, system-level effects, and mitigation options. The dominant role of EEPN-induced timing jitter is demonstrated, and implications for pluggable transceivers across DCI, metro, and long-haul applications are discussed.

talks.title: Th1-H2: Reach Extension of WDM DP-16QAM Signals Based on Decision-Feedforward Digital Backpropagation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Inoue, Takashi

We experimentally demonstrate an improved decision-feedforward digital backpropagation (DFF-DBP) to mitigate self- and cross-phase modulation in long-distance WDM systems without using neighboring-channel amplitudes. DFF-DBP with optimized design parameters extends the transmission reach of a 21-channel, 64-Gbaud DP-16QAM system from 2140 km to 2634 km.

talks.title: Th1-H3: Post-FEC Performance Prediction Using Distribution Transform Functions Under Non-Stationary Conditions
talks.abstract:
Authors: Abolfathimomtaz, Abbas / Ke, Jianhong / Li, Chuandong / Hashemi, Yoones

Static pre-FEC thresholds fail to guarantee requirements under non-stationary conditions. We propose a transform function leveraging pre-FEC distributions for accurate post-FEC estimation, simplifying to specific distribution moments at high SNR. Experimental validation confirms superior accuracy, preventing significant link margin monitoring errors in dynamic fiber environments.

talks.title: Th1-H4: Demonstration of PDM-16QAM Transmission Robust to Fast SOP Variations Using Real-Time 2×2 MIMO Equalization on a GPU
talks.abstract:
Authors: Arikawa, Manabu / Odagawa, Takahiro / Hosokawa, Kohei / Kamiya, Norifumi

We demonstrated 5-Gbaud PDM-16QAM transmission using GPU-based real-time DSP with 2×2 MIMO equalization tailored for parallel processing. The pre-FEC BER remained stable below 10-4 for over one hour after 240-km SMF transmission, and degradation was small under fast SOP variations up to 10 krad/s.

talks.title: Th1-H5: Optical-Analog-Optical Wavelength Converter for Multi-Domain Optical Direct-Connect Boundaries: 100G/400G Multi-FEC Characterization and Network Demonstration
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mori, Hiroki / Hiyama, Junnosuke / Nakagawa, Mayuri / Seki, Takeshi / Clark, J. Kenji / Nakamura, Yuna / Maeda, Wakako / Hosokawa, Kohei / Hayashi, Rie / Le Taillandier De Gabory, Emmanuel / Tamura, Toshihiko

We experimentally evaluate an Optical-Analog-Optical wavelength converter as a boundary node for multi-domain optical direct-connect networks. 100G/400G multi-FEC and multi-vendor measurements indicate OSNR penalty variations correlate more strongly with transceiver-dependent characteristics than with FEC scheme. Multi-domain network demonstration confirms measurable margin and frequency-offset detection capability.

sessions.title: Coffee break
Th2-A Security of optical communication systems
sessions.track: SC 11: Quantum communications, physical layer security, and optical quantum technologies

talks.title: Th2-A1: Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions: Foundations and Applications
talks.abstract:
Authors: Doosti, Mina

Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions extend the no-cloning principle from states to transformations, enabling hardware-rooted security for quantum networks. This tutorial introduces foundations, security notions, impossibility and positive results, and applications to authentication, identification, hybrid PUFs, and practical quantum communication infrastructures, with implementation considerations and outlook.

talks.title: Th2-A2: Performance Evaluation of Hardening Measures for Quantum Key Management Systems
talks.abstract:
Authors: Berl, Jonas / Wenning, Mario / Grießer, Helmut / Fehenberger, Tobias

We propose a hardened QKMS for resilient key relaying, combining secret sharing, PQC-hybridization, path verification, and confidential computing techniques. Emulation of a nation-wide QKD network demonstrates that these safeguards add only minor processing overhead, with overall key relay latency dominated by propagation delay.

talks.title: Th2-A3: Breaking AES at 50 km: Long-Range Optical Side-Channel Attack over Fiber
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gérenton, Victor / Jaillon, Philippe / Lavignotte, Antoine / Patanè, Rosario / Gillet, Franck / Saliou, Fabienne / Lepers, Catherine

Passive optical networks rely on AES-128 for traffic confidentiality. We demonstrate that AES-induced power fluctuations on microcontrollers can modulate a co-powered laser and propagate through 50 km of fiber. This enables key recovery using 1500 optical traces, making this the first long-range optical side-channel attack.

sessions.title: Th2-B SoP sensing and aplications
sessions.track: SC 08: Sensing and microwave photonics

talks.title: Th2-B1: Fully Unsupervised Detection of Physical Contacts on Subsea Cables via State-of-Polarization Monitoring
talks.abstract:
Authors: Raj, Agastya / Doval, Alvaro / Tian, Tian / Bjørnstad, Steinar / Ruffini, Marco

We present a fully unsupervised Fast-Slow DSVDD detector for continuous State-of-Polarization monitoring on a deployed subsea cable. Trained without event labels, it ranks all five confirmed trawler contacts within the top 13 of 122,174 recordings and surfaces additional corroborated cable-contact events.

talks.title: Th2-B2: On SOP Vibration Sensitivity in Hollow Core Fibers and the Impact of Multipath Interference
talks.abstract:
Authors: Tovar, Pedro / Lan, Yang / Wang, Xutao / Guan, Xianchao / Luo, Han / Zhou, Xingyu / Jiang, Zhiping

A recent study reported two-order-of-magnitude higher SOP vibration sensitivity in hollow-core fibers (HCF). We demonstrate that multipath interference might greatly skew these measurements when using narrow-linewidth lasers. Utilizing a proposed robust characterization method, we show that HCF SOP sensitivity is actually comparable to solid-core fibers.

talks.title: Th2-B3: State-of-Polarisation (SoP) Monitoring of Wind-Induced Resonance Oscillations on Power Lines
talks.abstract:
Authors: Doval, Alvaro / Bjørnstad, Steinar / De Vries, Krister / Skarvang Vaskinn, Kristina

Aeolian vibrations cause fatigue damage to power-line infrastructure. We monitor SoP on a live OPGW link over seven months, correlating with wind-speed data. Discrete resonance tones below 25 Hz occur at wind speeds up to 7 m/s, demonstrating SoP sensing for proactive structural condition monitoring

talks.title: Th2-B4: Per-Span Microwave Frequency Fiber Interferometry in Subsea Cables for Scalable Deep-Ocean Geophysical Monitoring
talks.abstract:
Authors: Karydis, Georgios Aias / Celli, Nicolas / Craig, David / Jónsson, Örn / Arnar Hlynsson, Andrés / Kenny, Eoin / Mesaritakis, Charis / Bean, Christopher / Bogris, Adonis

We demonstrate low-cost microwave frequency fibre interferometry for per-span monitoring of a 1,770 km operational subsea cable connecting Ireland and Iceland. Over four months, this approach successfully resolved tidal variations, storms, and teleseismic earthquakes, highlighting its potential for large-scale, cost-effective ocean monitoring

talks.title: Th2-B5: The Mediterranean as an Earth-Scale Geophysical Sensor: Polarization Sensing on Subsea Fiber Infrastructure
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mecozzi, Antonio

We demonstrate that commercial coherent submarine telecommunication links can operate as ultra‑low‑frequency environmental sensors by monitoring polarization telemetry from DSP receivers. Multiple Mediterranean cables detected both Rayleigh waves and Earth‑scale precursor anomalies preceding the 29 July 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake at ~9000 km distances.

sessions.title: Th2-D Advances in coherent PON
sessions.track: SC 07: Optical networks for access, mobile X-haul, in-building, and intra-datacentre interconnects

talks.title: Th2-D1: 960/480/240/120 Gbit/s Single-Carrier Super-Rated Hybrid Coherent Upstream Burst-Mode PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Vijayan, Kovendhan / Borkowski, Robert / Van Veen, Doutje / Houtsma, Vincent

We propose and experimentally verify a hybrid coherent architecture for an upstream TDMA PON, in which multiple ONU transmitter types can be supported by a single OLT receiver. We demonstrate more than 40-dB loss budget for 480-Gbit/s using 120-GBd DP-QAM4 in upstream burst-mode reception.

talks.title: Th2-D2: Experimental Burst-Mode Reception of LDPC Forward-Error-Corrected 256Gbps Coherent PON with 24 dB Dynamic Range using a Static-Gain TIA
talks.abstract:
Authors: Sarkis, Jad / Palmer, Robert / Matuz, Balazs / Talli, Giuseppe / Ferrero, Valter / Gaudino, Roberto

We demonstrate post-FEC error-free upstream burst-mode transmission of 256 Gbps DP QPSK over 20 km in the C-band. The proposed receiver scheme with commercial ICR and static-gain TIA supports 24 dB of dynamic range (DR) exceeding the typical 20 dB ITU-T requirement for PON systems.

talks.title: Th2-D3: Low-Complexity FPGA Implementation of Channel Estimation and Equalization for 100G Real-Time Upstream Burst-Mode Detection in Coherent PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zheng, Renle / Yan, An / Luo, Penghao / He, Shuhong / Deng, Xuyu / Zhao, Junhao / Hu, Yongzhu / Chi, Nan / Zhang, Junwen

We experimentally demonstrate low-complexity FPGA-based channel estimation and equalization for 100-Gb/s real-time upstream burst-mode detection in coherent PON. Reduced-parallelism one-tap SOP-aided MMSE decreases FPGA resource consumption by 35.8% versus full 128-parallel processing, with only 1-dB dynamic-range penalty and a 45.7-dB power budget.

talks.title: Th2-D4: First Field Trial of Coherent TDM-PON Up to 300 Gb/s
talks.abstract:
Authors: Zhu, Yixiao / Huang, Luyao / Hu, Yimin / Zhang, Ziheng / Ge, Chaofeng / Zhang, Dezhi / Jiang, Ming / Hu, Weisheng

We report the first field trial demonstration of coherent TDM-PON over 57-km deployed urban fiber (~34-dB loss), achieving flexible rates up to 300 Gb/s and fast-convergence DSP with a 30-ns preamble. The power budgets are 42/39 dB for 200-/300-Gb/s data rates.

talks.title: Th2-D5: Impact of Rayleigh backscattering on next-generation bidirectional 200 Gb/s FDMA coherent PON
talks.abstract:
Authors: Moreno Morrone, Juan L. / Ebner, Laurenz / Moawad, Abdelrahmane / Fischer, Johannes K. / Freund, Ronald

We experimentally evaluate the impact of Rayleigh backscattering in the upstream in a single‑wavelength 200 Gb/s DP‑QPSK FDMA coherent PON between two ONUs and an OLT. Simulations show a trade-off between downstream and upstream transmit powers and identify an operational region enabling simultaneous bidirectional transmission.

sessions.title: Th2-E Receivers and photodetectors
sessions.track: SC 03: Photonic integrated circuits, assemblies and packaging

talks.title: Th2-E1: A 4-𝜆 x 64 Gb/s Polarization-diverse Silicon Photonic DWDMReceiver using low-PDL 2D Grating Couplers
talks.abstract:
Authors: Mehta, Nandish / Greer Iii, Thomas H / Sakib, Meer / Gray, C. Thomas

We demonstrate a 4-λx64 Gb/s silicon-photonic polarization-diverse receiver using a low-PDL 2D grating coupler. Co-optimized grating geometry and fiber coupling angle yield <+/-0.2-dB PDL across a 300-mm wafer. Stable eye-diagrams and BER measured under fast 2000-rad/s SOP scrambling confirm fully passive reception independent of polarization.

talks.title: Th2-E2: Neural Inverse Design of Electrodes Enables Uni-Traveling-Carrier Photodiodes with 220 GHz Bandwidth and 2.7 dBm Output Power at 170 GHz
talks.abstract:
Authors: Chen, Jianwei / Zhu, Min / Chen, Xingyu / Zhang, Jiao / Cai, Yuancheng / Hua, Bingchang / Wang, Yunwu / Zhang, Long / You, Xiaohu

We demonstrate neural inverse-designed uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes achieving a 220 GHz bandwidth and 2.7 dBm output power at 170 GHz. By tailoring the inductive-capacitive resonance of the on-chip electrodes to compensate for intrinsic RC roll-off, this approach simultaneously enhances bandwidth and output power without heterogeneous integration.

talks.title: Th2-E3: Highly Reliable CMP-Free Ge-on-Si Waveguide Photodiodes for Data Center Optical Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Musibau, Solomon / Coughlan, Conor / Rajasekaran, Natarajan / Kobbi, Hakim / Tsiara, Artemisia / Balakrishnan, Sadhishkumar / Shiramin, Leili / Absil, Philippe

We demonstrate reliable CMP-free Ge‑on‑Si photodiodes, validated through extensive accelerated aging, showing stable dark current. The device exhibits 0.89 A/W responsivity, 65.3 GHz bandwidth, and sub-10 nA dark current, enabling simplified silicon photonics integration for optical interconnects in AI data centers with strict reliability requirements.

talks.title: Th2-E4: On-Chip Real-Time Polarization Demultiplexing using an Adaptive MZI Photonic Mesh
talks.abstract:
Authors: Seyedinnavadeh, Seyedmohammad / De Gaetano, Samuele / Crico, Monica / Melloni, Andrea / Zanetto, Francesco / Morichetti, Francesco

We demonstrate on-chip real-time demultiplexing of two 25 Gbps signals with orthogonal, randomly scrambled polarizations. The photonic circuit consists of a polarization-insensitive 4x2 reconfigurable MZI mesh that also compensates phase drifts of the input signals and is adaptively configured through monolithically integrated electronic multiplexers.

talks.title: Th2-E5: A High Sensitivity 200 Gbps PAM4 Receiver with Flip Chip Integrated Si-Ge Avalanche Photodiode and CMOS Transimpedance Amplifier
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cheng, Chao / Yang, Yihao / Bao, Shenlei / Lai, Houyou / Yu, Xishan / Liu, Qian / Xue, Jintao / Zhang, Wenfu / Wang, Binhao

This paper reports a high-sensitivity optical receiver based on flip-chip integrated Si–Ge avalanche photodiode and CMOS transimpedance amplifier. Clear eye diagrams are achieved at 100 Gbps NRZ and 200 Gbps PAM4, with sensitivities of -26.1 dBm and -20 dBm, respectively.

sessions.title: Th2-F Programmable photonics: architectures, control and applications
Th2-G Enabling fibre based devices and handling
sessions.track: SC 01: Novel fibres, fibre devices and amplifiers

talks.title: Th2-G1: In-Fibre Optical Logic Gate Utilizing Laser-Inscribed Multi-Mode Interference within Multi-Core Fibre
talks.abstract:
Authors: Kamimura, Kiyoshi / Wada, Masaki / Yamashita, Yoko / Matsui, Takashi

We propose the in-fibre logic gate based on laser-inscribed multi-mode interference (MMI) within multi-core fibre to realize core switching by optical phase for the first time. The MMI-based logic gate is experimentally demonstrated, and we show its applicability to 2x4 optical logic circuits.

talks.title: Th2-G2: 8 × 40-channel Gang Connector Using Snap-Beam Connectors in Co-packaged Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Fujimaki, Yuki / Ikeda, Shosuke / Watanabe, Kengo / Saito, Tsunetoshi / Kotoku, Masaki

A low-loss 8 × 40‑channel gang connector using Snap‑Beam connectors has been developed, enabling high‑density simultaneous connection in Co-packaged Optics. Low insertion loss ≤ 0.7 dB and return loss ≥ 36 dB were verified for fibre-to-fibre connections.

talks.title: Th2-G3: Efficient, Ultra-flat and Low-noise Parametric Comb Generation using Hybrid Nonlinear Fibre System and Chirped-pulse Nonlinear Loop Mirror
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cai, Yijia / Heidt, Alexander M. / Liu, Zhixin

We address efficiency, spectral flatness and noise-scaling problems in cavity-less frequency comb generation using a hybrid fibre system combining soliton and wave-breaking nonlinearities. We propose chirped-pulse nonlinear loop mirror to efficiently shape pulse and spectra, achieving 3-dB flatness across C-band and sub-3-kHz linewidth over 80nm.

talks.title: Th2-G4: Highly Efficient and Ultra-Low Loss AR-HCF Fusion Splicing with Rapid Rotational Alignment
talks.abstract:
Authors: He, Wei / Zhang, Cong / Feng, Lipeng / Lin, Di / Li, Peng / Zhang, Lei / Luo, Jie / Qin, Yuwen / Fu, Songnian

We propose a discrete-sampling gradient detection algorithm for rapid rotational alignment in anti-resonant hollow-core fiber (AR-HCF) fusion splicing, in order to resolve directional ambiguity, compress the angular search space, and achieve an 0.042 dB average splicing loss with a splicing time less than 55 seconds.

sessions.title: Th2-C End-to-end optical communications systems for space: demonstration and validation
sessions.track: SC 09: Free-space optics and optical wireless technologies

talks.title: Th2-C1: Satellite to Ground FSO Communication Links enhanced by Mode Diversity Reception and Adaptive Optics
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wu, Jian / Guo, Wenjie / Li, Yan / Li, Ao / Li, Xiaokai / Sun, Yaning / Wei, Shuai / Guo, Hongxiang / Liu, Chao / Zhang, Ze

We experimentally demonstrate a joint adaptive optics and mode diversity reception (AO+MDR) scheme for GEO satellite-to-ground laser communication. A 1 Gbit/s BPSK link achieves 4.0 dB power gain and improves the probability of BER < 1 × 10−3 from 54.2% to 88.8%, confirming synergistic compensation.

talks.title: Th2-C2: Real-Hardware Demonstration of a 1.25 Gb/s Free-Space Optical Inter-Satellite Link on 6U CubeSat Engineering Models with Simultaneous Closed-Loop PAT
talks.abstract:
Authors: Riaz, Amna / Scullion, Eamon / Wicks, Robert / Binns, Richard / Sepúlveda, Elias / Khorchef, Nassima / Martin, James / Vernon, Jethro

Real-Hardware Demonstration of a 1.25 Gb/s Free-Space Optical Inter-Satellite Link on 6U CubeSat Engineering Models with Simultaneous Closed-Loop PAT

talks.title: Th2-C3: Design and Validation of Low Penalty High-Power (>50W) Optical Amplifier for Satellite Communications using Commercial Coherent Transceiver
talks.abstract:
Authors: Boddeda, Rajiv / Dutisseuil, Eric / Umasankar, Dinesh Kumar / Bordais, Sylvain / Casale, Marco / Pollier, Vincent / Grasser, Regis / Guesmi, Khmaies / Haret, Laurent-Daniel / Bigo, Sébastien

A high‑power optical amplifier for ground‑to‑satellite optical links was developed using polarization beam combination to alleviate nonlinear effects. We demonstrate net 100‑Gb/s transmission with commercial coherent transceivers and experimentally characterize the resulting penalty from the nonlinear distortions.

talks.title: Th2-C4: Wavelength-Polarization Domain Synthetic Aperture Combining of Noncoherent Multi-beams for Turbulence-Resilient Satellite-to-Ground Laser Downlinks
talks.abstract:
Authors: Dong, Fang / Zhang, Haoyu / Liu, Yinjun / Sun, Jianfeng / Zhang, Junwen / Chi, Nan

We propose a wavelength-polarization domain synthetic aperture combining scheme for turbulence-resilient satellite-to-ground downlinks based on VCM-FSM-enabled noncoherent multibeam transmission. This architecture supports all-weather uninterrupted communication under atmospheric turbulence and demonstrates 2.24 Tbit/s transmission over a 3000 km FSO equivalent link.

sessions.title: Th2-H Faster-than-nyquist, equalization and coding
sessions.track: SC 04: Signal processing for optical communication and sensing

talks.title: Th2-H1: Maximum Coverage Chase Decoder for Optical Interconnects
talks.abstract:
Authors: Cardinale, Alessandro / Song, Wenqing / Chen, Bin / Alvarado, Alex / Burg, Andreas / Shen, Yifei

We propose a low-complexity Chase decoder for optical interconnects that formulates test pattern selection as a generalized maximum coverage problem. For concatenated RS-BCH and oFEC codes, our decoder achieves the standard Chase decoding performance with 25% and 61.3% fewer test patterns, respectively.

talks.title: Th2-H2: Robust Real-Time DSP for a Hybrid Fiber and Photonic-Assisted Sub-THz Wireless Communication
talks.abstract:
Authors: Gostner, Filipp / Dittmer, Joel / Qamesh, Ahmed / Pilori, Dario / Tessmann, Axel / Wagner, Sandrine / Koos, Christian / Simon, Frank / Randel, Sebastian

We demonstrate a real-time photonic-assisted sub-THz link. Across 10km SSMF and a 1.4m wireless link, the coherent 16-QAM system achieves 6.83Gbit/s. Our fast-acquisition DSP performs real-time, non-data-aided timing recovery, channel equalization, and phase recovery on an FPGA, operating under ±100ppm clock offset and intermitted data.

talks.title: Th2-H3: Impact of Non-Uniform Constellations on MLSE Demodulation Performance for PCS-16QAM under Bandwidth Limitation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Nakajima, Yukinobu / Yamamoto, Shuto / Nakamura, Masanori / Taniguchi, Hiroki / Yamazaki, Etsushi

We investigated the impact of the prior probability term in MLSE branch metrics and demonstrated a GMI improvement of up to 9% over the case without MLSE by optimizing the prior probability term weight through transmission experiments using PCS-16QAM signals under severe bandwidth limitation.

talks.title: Th2-H4: Low-Complexity FPGA-Based PR-9QAM Detection for Photonics-Aided 306-GHz FTN Wireless System
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wang, Yikai / Zhu, Min / Cai, Yuancheng / Zhang, Long / Ding, Junjie / Zhang, Jiao / Hua, Bingchang / Lei, Mingzheng / Xin, Zhigang / Yan, Yiting / Chen, Jianwei / Li, Jiankang / Yang, Xiongwei / Wang, Kaihui / Yu, Jianjun

This paper employs PR coding for FTN transmission, yielding a PR-9QAM signal and motivating low-complexity CMMA and carrier recovery design. The algorithms are implemented on an FPGA platform and validated in a photonics-aided 306 GHz link with error-free 30 Gbps over 3 m.

talks.title: Th2-H5: 30.2-km D-Band Photonics-Assisted Wireless Reception Enabled by FPGA-Based Equalizer-Guided SFO Compensation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Hu, Sheng / Wang, Kaihui / Zheng, Tianqi / Long, Jianyu / Chen, Jiali / Zhou, Ye / Lu, Xin / Ma, Hanson / Bian, Chengzhen / Ren, Jianxin / Liu, Bo

An FPGA-deployed receiver is demonstrated for a 30.2-km photonics-assisted D-band wireless link with equalizer-guided SFO estimation and Farrow-based compensation. Using experimentally captured waveform data loaded into on-board RAM, the FPGA receiver successfully achieves 16-Gbaud QPSK transmission below the 20% SD-FEC threshold.

talks.title: Th2-H6: Demonstration of 169-Gbaud Faster-Than-Nyquist PAM4 Transmission Using Adaptation-Free THP-FFDNN Under 37.9-GHz 3-dB Bandwidth Limitation
talks.abstract:
Authors: Wei, Yuan / Chen, Chaoxu / Yuan, Yuqin / Liu, Yinjun / Dong, Boyu / He, Jialin / Zhao, Junhao / Zhang, Haoyu / Yao, Li / Xu, Bo / Zhao, Yaotian / Chu, Wei / Cai, Haiwen / Chi, Nan / Shi, Jianyang / Zhang, Junwen

We propose a THP-FFDNN framework for faster-than-Nyquist PAM4 transmission, which eliminates adaptive updating while requiring only 408 parameters. The proposed scheme is compatible with GPU-based DSP implementation and achieves 169 Gbaud PAM4 under 37.9-GHz 3-dB bandwidth limitation, supporting the lowest spectral compression ratio of 62.5%
